B01C001.summary: The frame story opens. The bard Sauti arrives at the forest of Naimisha, where sages are gathered at a long sacrifice, and is asked to tell them the Mahabharata as Vaishampayana first recited it at King Janamejaya's snake sacrifice. He praises its source, tells how Vyasa composed it and how Ganesha wrote it down, and lists what it contains. He then retells, through Dhritarashtra's lament to Sanjaya, the whole course of the war, and Sanjaya consoles the blind king that fate is the work of Time. The chapter ends with the merit of hearing the epic and why it is called the Great Bharata.

scenes.B01C001S01: Sauti arrives at the Naimisha forest, is welcomed by the sages, and is asked what he will tell them. They choose the history composed by Vyasa.
scenes.B01C001S02: Sauti bows to the supreme being and describes the world's creation from a cosmic egg, the lineage of gods and sages, and the many ways the epic is studied.
scenes.B01C001S03: Vyasa has composed the epic but has no one to write it. Brahma tells him to call on Ganesha, who agrees to write it if Vyasa never pauses. Vyasa agrees on condition that Ganesha understand each verse first, and ties knots of hard verses to slow him.
scenes.B01C001S04: Sauti compares the epic to a lamp, a sun and a tree, and sums up its contents book by book. He names how Vyasa fathered Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura and later had the story recited.
scenes.B01C001S05: Sauti gives the size of the epic in verses and in what worlds it is known. He tells briefly of the Pandavas' birth, arrival at Hastinapura and early life.
scenes.B01C001S06: The Pandavas win Draupadi and the Rajasuya sacrifice. Duryodhana is humiliated at their hall, gets the dice game arranged, and the great war follows. Dhritarashtra starts to speak to Sanjaya.
scenes.B01C001S07: Dhritarashtra lists, one by one, the events that told him his side would lose, from Arjuna's winning Draupadi to Aswatthaman's night attack. After each he repeats that he had no hope of success. He ends by mourning Gandhari and the few survivors.
scenes.B01C001S08: Dhritarashtra wishes to die. Sanjaya comforts him with the example of kings of the past, who also died, and with the teaching that Time creates and destroys all things.
scenes.B01C001S09: Sauti explains the merit of hearing and reciting the epic, and why it is called the Mahabharata: the gods weighed it against the four Vedas and it was heavier.
scenes.B01C001S10: A short closing line: penance, study and the pursuit of wealth are harmless unless misused.

shots.B01C001S01H01: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Saraswati, and to victory.
shots.B01C001S01H02: Sauti comes to the sages at Saunaka's twelve-year sacrifice and is asked where he has been.
shots.B01C001S01H03: The question to Sauti is answered in measured, fitting words.
shots.B01C001S01H04: Sauti says he heard Vyasa's epic recited, visited holy places, and came from Kurukshetra to offer them a story.
shots.B01C001S01H05: The sages ask for the history Vaishampayana recited at Janamejaya's sacrifice.
shots.B01C001S02H01: Sauti praises the supreme being and says the epic is told in many forms.
shots.B01C001S02H02: The cosmic egg, Brahma, the Prajapatis, gods and sages arise at the world's beginning.
shots.B01C001S02H03: The world is destroyed and renewed in cycles of ages.
shots.B01C001S02H04: Genealogy of gods leading to the Kurus, Yadus and Bharatas, and the scope of Vyasa's work.
shots.B01C001S02H05: The epic is read in different ways, long or short, by different scholars.
shots.B01C001S03H01: Brahma visits Vyasa, who lists the many subjects of his poem and complains that no scribe exists.
shots.B01C001S03H02: Brahma praises the poem and tells Vyasa to call on Ganesha.
shots.B01C001S03H03: Vyasa calls Ganesha and asks him to write the Bharata.
shots.B01C001S03H04: Ganesha agrees if his pen never stops; Vyasa answers that he must understand before writing, and he ties hard knots of verse.
shots.B01C001S03H05: Sauti says he knows 8,800 hard verses and that Ganesha too paused over them.
shots.B01C001S04H01: The epic is compared to an instrument that opens the blind eye and a lamp lighting a house.
shots.B01C001S04H02: The epic is described as a tree whose parts are the books, ending with the fruit and sap.
shots.B01C001S04H03: Vyasa had three sons by Vichitravirya's wives and then withdrew to his hermitage.
shots.B01C001S04H04: After they were grown and gone, Vyasa taught Vaishampayana, who recited it at the sacrifice.
shots.B01C001S04H05: The epic shows the Kuru house, Gandhari, Vidura, Kunti, Vasudeva and the Pandavas.
shots.B01C001S05H01: The epic's length in verses and who recited which version in which world.
shots.B01C001S05H02: The Pandavas are compared to a tree with Yudhishthira as the trunk of virtue.
shots.B01C001S05H03: Pandu's hunt, the curse that followed, the five sons born from gods, and their arrival with the sages.
shots.B01C001S05H04: The people of Hastinapura argue about the boys, then welcome them with joy.
shots.B01C001S05H05: The Pandavas study the Vedas and live safely in the city.
shots.B01C001S06H01: The people love the Pandavas for their virtues.
shots.B01C001S06H02: Arjuna wins Draupadi at the swayamvara and gains fame; the brothers prepare the Rajasuya.
shots.B01C001S06H03: Yudhishthira performs the Rajasuya after Jarasandha and Shishupala are slain; Duryodhana is envious and humiliated in Maya's hall.
shots.B01C001S06H04: Dhritarashtra allows the dice game; Krishna lets the quarrel run and the war follows.
shots.B01C001S06H05: Dhritarashtra ponders and begins to address Sanjaya.
shots.B01C001S07H01: Dhritarashtra says he never wanted war and starts listing the signs of his side's loss.
shots.B01C001S07H02: A long list of early events, from Draupadi's winning to her disgrace, each ending with no hope of success.
shots.B01C001S07H03: The list continues through the exile, Virata, Krishna's embassy, the war, the deaths of Bhishma, Drona, Karna and Duryodhana, and Aswatthaman's night attack.
shots.B01C001S07H04: He mourns Gandhari, left without children, kindred or family.
shots.B01C001S07H05: Only ten survive the war and he feels his mind failing.
shots.B01C001S08H01: Dhritarashtra faints from grief, then speaks again.
shots.B01C001S08H02: He wishes to end his life.
shots.B01C001S08H03: Sanjaya answers him, sighing, with weighty words.
shots.B01C001S08H04: Sanjaya lists great kings of the past who all died, and tells him that Time creates and ends all things.
shots.B01C001S08H05: Sanjaya's comfort calms Dhritarashtra, and Vyasa composes an Upanishad on the matter.
shots.B01C001S09H01: Sauti lists the many beings and subjects the epic describes, including the supreme spirit.
shots.B01C001S09H02: Reading the introduction frees one of sin and keeps one from trouble; the epic is like butter in curd.
shots.B01C001S09H03: Reciting even one foot at a funeral rite makes the offering inexhaustible.
shots.B01C001S09H04: The Veda is understood through history and the Puranas; hearing the epic gives long life and heaven.
shots.B01C001S09H05: The gods weighed the epic against the four Vedas, and it was heavier, hence the name Mahabharata.
shots.B01C001S10H01: Closing line: harmless practices become harmful when misused.

B01C002.summary: The sages ask about the place called Samanta-panchaka and the word Akshauhini. Sauti explains how Parashurama's slaughter of the warrior class created five blood-lakes there, which later became the Kurukshetra battlefield, and he defines an Akshauhini as a vast army unit. He then gives a contents list (Parva-sangraha) of all eighteen books of the epic, with the number of sections and verses in each, and ends by praising the merit of hearing the Bharata.

scenes.B01C002S01: The sages ask about Samanta-panchaka. Sauti tells how Parashurama made lakes of blood there and how the Kuru battle was later fought on the same ground. He also defines an Akshauhini and says how many days each general led the Kaurava army.
scenes.B01C002S02: Sauti begins the table of contents and lists, in order, the sub-books of the epic. He says the eighteen books are condensed from Vyasa's longer plan and starts with the first book, Adi Parva.
scenes.B01C002S03: Contents of Adi Parva's remaining parts, then of the Sabha, Vana (Aranyaka), Virata, Udyoga and Bhishma books, each with its main events.
scenes.B01C002S04: Contents of the Drona, Karna, Shalya, Sauptika and Stri books: the war's later days, Abhimanyu's death, Karna's fall, Duryodhana's defeat, the night massacre, and the women's lament.
scenes.B01C002S05: Contents of the Shanti, Anushasana, Aswamedhika and Asramavasika books: Yudhishthira's grief, Bhishma's teachings, the horse sacrifice, and Dhritarashtra's retreat to the forest.
scenes.B01C002S06: Contents of the last books: the Yadavas' destruction in Mausala, the Pandavas' final journey, and Yudhishthira's ascent to heaven. A note on the supplement, the Harivamsa.
scenes.B01C002S07: Sauti closes the contents section with the merit of the Bharata and the benefit of hearing it.

shots.B01C002S01H01: The sages ask Sauti to explain Samanta-panchaka.
shots.B01C002S01H02: Parashurama destroys the warrior class, makes five blood lakes there, and his ancestors appear and offer him a boon.
shots.B01C002S01H03: Parashurama asks to be cleansed of his sin and for the lakes to be holy; later the Kuru-Pandava armies gather and die on that same ground.
shots.B01C002S01H04: The sages ask what an Akshauhini is.
shots.B01C002S01H05: Sauti defines the army unit, gives the numbers of chariots, elephants, foot and horse, and lists how long each commander led the war.
shots.B01C002S02H01: Sauti praises the Bharata as the first of all texts and says it was recited at Janamejaya's sacrifice.
shots.B01C002S02H02: He says he will list the parts of the epic.
shots.B01C002S02H03: A long list of the sub-books in order, from the first to the last, with a line on the content of each.
shots.B01C002S02H04: Vyasa's hundred sub-books are grouped into eighteen books.
shots.B01C002S02H05: A detailed contents of the first book, Adi Parva, from the stories of Utanka and Bhrigu through the Pandavas' marriage, exile and the burning of the Khandava forest.
shots.B01C002S03H01: Contents of Sabha Parva: the hall, Rajasuya, dice game and exile.
shots.B01C002S03H02: Contents of Vana Parva: the forest years, Arjuna's weapons, Nala, pilgrimages, Savitri and the Rama story.
shots.B01C002S03H03: Contents of Virata Parva: the year in disguise, Kichaka's death, the cattle raids, Uttara's marriage.
shots.B01C002S03H04: Contents of Udyoga Parva: war preparations, Sanjaya's embassy, Krishna's peace mission and its failure.
shots.B01C002S03H05: Contents of Bhishma Parva: the Gita and Bhishma's fall.
shots.B01C002S04H01: Contents of Drona Parva: Drona as commander, Abhimanyu's death, Jayadratha's death, Ghatotkacha's death.
shots.B01C002S04H02: Contents of Karna Parva: Karna as commander and his death at Arjuna's hands.
shots.B01C002S04H03: Contents of Shalya Parva: Shalya's fall, Shakuni's death, and the club fight between Duryodhana and Bhima.
shots.B01C002S04H04: Contents of Sauptika Parva: Ashwatthaman's night raid on the sleeping Pandava camp.
shots.B01C002S04H05: Contents of Stri Parva: Dhritarashtra's rage and grief, the women on the battlefield, the cremations.
shots.B01C002S05H01: Contents of Shanti Parva: Yudhishthira's despair and Bhishma's teaching on duty.
shots.B01C002S05H02: Contents of Anushasana Parva: further teachings and Bhishma's death.
shots.B01C002S05H03: Contents of Aswamedhika Parva: the horse sacrifice, Parikshit's revival, and the golden treasure.
shots.B01C002S05H04: Contents of Asramavasika Parva: Dhritarashtra, Gandhari and Kunti retire to the forest.
shots.B01C002S05H05: The same book ends with Vidura's and Sanjaya's passing and news of the Vrishnis' fate.
shots.B01C002S06H01: Contents of Mausala Parva: the Vrishnis kill each other and Krishna and Balarama depart.
shots.B01C002S06H03: Mahaprasthanika Parva: the Pandavas' last journey, in which the brothers fall one by one.
shots.B01C002S06H04: Svargarohana Parva: Yudhishthira refuses heaven without his dog, then sees hell and then heaven.
shots.B01C002S06H05: The Harivamsa is added as a supplement to the eighteen books.
shots.B01C002S07H01: Sauti praises the epic as the root of all later poetry and learning.
shots.B01C002S07H02: He tells the sages to turn to virtue and says hearing the epic removes sin.
shots.B01C002S07H03: Closing line that ends the contents section.

B01C003.summary: Sauti begins the Paushya section. King Janamejaya's brothers beat a dog, the son of the divine bitch Sarama, and she curses the family. To cleanse the curse Janamejaya appoints a priest. Then comes a chain of teacher-and-pupil stories about Ayoda-Dhaumya's disciples Aruni, Upamanyu and Veda, and Veda's pupil Utanka. Utanka fetches Queen Paushya's earrings as a gift for his teacher's wife, fights the serpent king Takshaka who steals them, and wins them back. He then urges Janamejaya to avenge his father Parikshit's death by a snake sacrifice, which plants the seed of the whole frame story.

scenes.B01C003S01: The curse on Janamejaya's family. The king's brothers beat Sarama's pup, Sarama curses them, the king seeks a priest and picks Somasrava, and the tale turns to Ayoda-Dhaumya's pupil Aruni.
scenes.B01C003S02: Aruni plugs a broken water channel with his own body and is named Uddalaka. Upamanyu, sent to herd cows, is stripped by his teacher of every food source until hunger drives him to eat a poisonous plant and blinds him.
scenes.B01C003S03: Dhaumya finds blind Upamanyu in a dry well and tells him to pray to the divine twin physicians, the Aswins. Upamanyu begins a long hymn about time, the year as a wheel, and the universe.
scenes.B01C003S04: The hymn ends and the Aswins appear. Upamanyu refuses their cake until he offers it to his teacher. Pleased by his loyalty, they restore his sight and promise him golden teeth.
scenes.B01C003S05: Upamanyu is praised by his teacher. Then Veda's story: he serves Dhaumya patiently, becomes a teacher himself, and leaves his pupil Utanka in charge of the house, where Utanka refuses to do wrong when the women ask him to.
scenes.B01C003S06: Utanka is thanked by Veda and sent to ask his teacher's wife for a gift. She asks for Queen Paushya's earrings. On the road a strange man on a huge bull makes Utanka eat the bull's dung. Utanka then asks King Paushya for the earrings and cannot find the queen.
scenes.B01C003S07: Paushya says Utanka is ritually unclean; Utanka washes properly and the queen gives the earrings with a warning about Takshaka. A quarrel over unclean food leads to mutual curses. On the road a beggar steals the earrings, turns into Takshaka, and flees underground, where Indra's thunderbolt helps Utanka dig after him.
scenes.B01C003S08: In the world of serpents Utanka praises the snake chiefs but does not get the earrings. He sees two women weaving, a twelve-spoked wheel and a man with a horse, and is told to blow into the horse. Fire pours out, Takshaka panics and returns the earrings.
scenes.B01C003S09: Utanka rides the horse and reaches his teacher's house just in time, and is blessed. His teacher explains the strange sights (night and day, the year, Indra and the rain god, Agni, and nectar in the bull's dung). Angry at Takshaka, Utanka goes to Hastinapura to see Janamejaya.
scenes.B01C003S10: Utanka tells Janamejaya that Takshaka killed his father Parikshit and should be burned in a snake sacrifice. The king is enraged, asks his ministers how his father died, and is overcome with grief. The chapter ends.

shots.B01C003S01H01: Chapter title card: the Paushya section begins.
shots.B01C003S01H02: At Janamejaya's long sacrifice at Kurukshetra, his three brothers beat the pup of Sarama. The pup runs crying to its mother, who storms in, asks why her innocent son was hit, gets no answer, and curses the brothers with sudden misfortune.
shots.B01C003S01H03: Alarmed by the curse, Janamejaya returns to Hastinapura after the sacrifice and starts searching for a priest who can undo it.
shots.B01C003S01H04: On a hunt the king finds the hermitage of the sage Srutasrava. He asks for the sage's son Somasrava as his priest and accepts the one condition, that the son gives any Brahmana whatever he asks. He orders his brothers to obey the new priest and conquers Takshashila.
shots.B01C003S01H05: New tale: the teacher Ayoda-Dhaumya has three pupils, Upamanyu, Aruni and Veda. Aruni is told to repair a broken water channel in a field, finds he cannot, and lies down in the gap to hold the water back.
shots.B01C003S02H01: Dhaumya asks where Aruni is, remembers sending him to the field, and takes the other pupils to find him.
shots.B01C003S02H02: Dhaumya calls out and Aruni rises from the channel, explaining what he did and letting the water escape as he came out.
shots.B01C003S02H03: Dhaumya names him Uddalaka for opening the channel, promises him success in all the Vedas and law books, and Aruni goes home.
shots.B01C003S02H04: Upamanyu is sent to herd the cows and comes back plump. Dhaumya forbids him in turn from keeping begged food, begging twice, drinking the cows' milk and sipping the calves' froth, until he has nothing left to eat.
shots.B01C003S02H05: Starving, Upamanyu eats the leaves of the arka plant, goes blind and falls into a pit. At sunset he has not returned, and the pupils report he went out with the cows.
shots.B01C003S03H01: Dhaumya guesses Upamanyu is weak from his restrictions and goes out with the pupils to look for him. Upamanyu answers from the bottom of a well and is told to praise the Aswins to get his sight back.
shots.B01C003S03H02: First part of Upamanyu's hymn to the Aswins, praising them as eternal, pure, and present in all things.
shots.B01C003S03H03: The hymn continues: the Aswins weave the year from night and day, and the 360 days are cows with a single calf, the year.
shots.B01C003S03H04: The hymn compares the year to a wheel with 720 spokes (days and nights) and twelve months, which the Aswins set in motion.
shots.B01C003S03H05: The hymn asks the Aswins to free him from the wheel of time, to make him independent of the five elements, and describes them as the Supreme appearing in forms.
shots.B01C003S04H01: The hymn recalls that the Aswins created the ten directions, the Sun and the sky, and that all sacrifices follow the Sun's course.
shots.B01C003S04H02: They mixed the three colours that make everything visible, and from these the world and its beings arose.
shots.B01C003S04H03: Upamanyu declares his worship of the Aswins and the sky they made, who give the results of all deeds yet are free of them.
shots.B01C003S04H04: He calls them parents of all and begs them for his sight.
shots.B01C003S04H05: The Aswins appear and offer him a cake. He refuses to eat it before offering it to his teacher, even after they say Dhaumya once ate theirs without offering it. Pleased, they promise him golden teeth, sight and good fortune.
shots.B01C003S05H01: Sight restored, Upamanyu tells Dhaumya everything and is blessed with knowledge of all the Vedas. This ends his trial.
shots.B01C003S05H02: The third pupil Veda is told to stay and serve. He endures heat, cold, hunger and thirst like a burden-ox and is rewarded with learning. This is his trial.
shots.B01C003S05H03: Veda leaves, marries and takes three pupils of his own, but treats them gently because he remembers his own hardships.
shots.B01C003S05H04: Kings Janamejaya and Paushya make Veda their priest. When he has to go away for a sacrifice, he leaves his pupil Utanka in charge of the house.
shots.B01C003S05H05: The women of the household tell Utanka his teacher's wife is fertile this month and that he should take the absent teacher's place. Utanka refuses, saying his teacher gave no such order.
shots.B01C003S06H01: Veda returns, hears what happened, praises Utanka and gives him leave to depart.
shots.B01C003S06H02: Utanka asks to bring a teacher's fee. Veda sends him to ask his wife, who asks for Queen Paushya's earrings, which she wants to wear on the fourth day to a feast for Brahmanas.
shots.B01C003S06H03: On the road Utanka meets a huge bull with a tall rider who makes him eat its dung and drink its urine, saying his teacher did the same. Utanka obeys, washes and goes on to King Paushya.
shots.B01C003S06H04: At the palace Utanka greets King Paushya and asks for the queen's earrings as a gift for his teacher.
shots.B01C003S06H05: Paushya sends him to the women's rooms. Utanka cannot find the queen and objects. The king says she cannot be seen by anyone who is ritually unclean from a meal and asks him to think.
shots.B01C003S07H01: Utanka remembers he washed while standing, which Paushya says is improper. He washes correctly, finds the queen, who gives him the earrings but warns him that Takshaka wants them.
shots.B01C003S07H02: Utanka brags that Takshaka cannot catch him. Paushya serves him a meal that is cold and has hair in it. Utanka curses the king to go blind, Paushya curses him to be childless, and Utanka tells him to look at the food himself.
shots.B01C003S07H03: Paushya sees the food really was unclean and begs forgiveness. Utanka says his curse stands but will lift soon; Paushya says he cannot undo his own. Utanka points out that curse cannot hold on unclean food and leaves with the earrings.
shots.B01C003S07H04: On the road a naked beggar keeps appearing and vanishing. While Utanka puts down the earrings to wash, the beggar grabs them and runs. Utanka catches him but the beggar becomes Takshaka and escapes into a hole to the serpent world.
shots.B01C003S07H05: Utanka tries to dig after him with a stick. Indra, seeing him struggle, sends the thunderbolt into the stick and widens the hole. Utanka goes in and sees the huge serpent city, and starts to praise the serpents.
shots.B01C003S08H01: First part of Utanka's praise of the serpents, naming Airavata, Dhritarashtra and their followers.
shots.B01C003S08H02: He praises Takshaka and his brother Srutasena and other serpents of Kurukshetra.
shots.B01C003S08H03: The earrings do not appear, so Utanka thinks and looks around. He sees two women weaving black and white thread on a loom, a twelve-spoked wheel turned by six boys, and a man with a horse.
shots.B01C003S08H04: Utanka recites verses about the wheel of time and the weaving of the world, praising Indra, god of thunder.
shots.B01C003S08H05: The man with the horse offers help. Utanka asks for control over the serpents. He is told to blow into the horse; fire and smoke pour out and threaten the serpent land. Terrified, Takshaka brings the earrings out and gives them back.
shots.B01C003S09H01: Utanka realises it is the day for the earrings and he is far away. The man tells him to ride the horse, which carries him to his teacher's house at once.
shots.B01C003S09H02: The teacher's wife is about to curse Utanka for being late when he arrives and presents the earrings. She blesses him instead.
shots.B01C003S09H03: Utanka tells his teacher about the delay caused by Takshaka, and asks what the weaving women, the wheel, the man with the horse and the man on the bull mean.
shots.B01C003S09H04: His teacher explains: the women are Dhata and Vidhata and the threads are night and day; the wheel is the year; the man is the rain god Parjanya and the horse is fire; the bull is Airavata, the rider Indra, and the dung was nectar, which saved Utanka's life.
shots.B01C003S09H05: Given leave to go, Utanka goes to Hastinapura, angry at Takshaka, and finds Janamejaya freshly back from Takshashila. He asks why the king acts like a child when something urgent needs him.
shots.B01C003S10H01: Janamejaya answers that he is doing his royal duty and asks what Utanka wants.
shots.B01C003S10H02: Utanka tells the king that Takshaka killed his father Parikshit and also turned back the healer Kasyapa. He urges Janamejaya to burn Takshaka in a snake sacrifice, which would also repay Utanka's own grievance.
shots.B01C003S10H03: The king flares up in anger at Takshaka, asks his ministers for the story of his father's death, and is overcome with sorrow when he hears it.
shots.B01C003S10H04: Closing line: the Paushya section of the Adi Parva ends.
shots.B01C003S10H05: Remainder of the closing line (title of the epic).

B01C004.summary: Back in the Naimisha forest, Sauti offers to tell more tales. The sages ask him to wait until their leader Saunaka finishes his rites. Saunaka arrives and sits down to question him.

scenes.B01C004S01: Sauti asks the sages what they want to hear. They say Saunaka, their chief, should be present first. When Saunaka has finished his duties and taken his seat, he begins to speak.

shots.B01C004S01H02: Sauti, standing before the sages at Saunaka's twelve-year sacrifice, says he has told Utanka's story and asks what to tell next. The sages say they will wait for Saunaka, whom they describe as learned, truthful and respected.
shots.B01C004S01H03: Sauti agrees. Saunaka finishes his prayers and offerings, returns to the sacrifice hall, sits among the priests, and begins to speak.

B01C005.summary: Saunaka asks Sauti to tell the history of the Bhrigu family. Sauti traces Bhrigu's descendants down to Sunaka and begins the story of why Bhrigu's son was named Chyavana. A demon named Puloma finds Bhrigu's pregnant wife Puloma alone, and the fire god Agni, forced to speak truthfully, confirms that she is Bhrigu's lawful wife.

scenes.B01C005S01: Saunaka asks for the history of the Bhrigu race. Sauti lists the line from Bhrigu to Chyavana, Pramati, Ruru and Sunaka. Saunaka asks why Chyavana got his name.
scenes.B01C005S02: The Rakshasa Puloma, who had once been promised the same woman, finds her alone at the hermitage, abducts her, and asks Agni whether she is truly Bhrigu's wife.
scenes.B01C005S03: Agni, afraid of both a lie and Bhrigu's curse, admits she was first chosen by the Rakshasa but was properly married to Bhrigu with fire rites.

shots.B01C005S01H02: Saunaka asks whether Sauti has studied the old Puranas and the Bharata like his father, and requests the history of the Bhrigu family.
shots.B01C005S01H03: Sauti says he learned everything his father and Vaisampayana did and promises the Bhrigu story.
shots.B01C005S01H04: He lists Bhrigu's descendants: Chyavana, Pramati, Ruru, and Sunaka, an ancestor of Saunaka.
shots.B01C005S01H05: Saunaka starts a question about why Bhrigu's son was named Chyavana (the sentence continues in the next shot).
shots.B01C005S02H01: The question finishes: why was he named Chyavana?
shots.B01C005S02H02: Bhrigu's pregnant wife Puloma is alone while he bathes. A Rakshasa also named Puloma arrives, is welcomed with forest fruit, becomes lustful, and plans to carry her off.
shots.B01C005S02H03: He seizes her. It was for this woman that her father had first promised him before marrying her to Bhrigu, so he sees his chance.
shots.B01C005S02H04: He sees the sacred fire burning and asks Agni, the mouth of the gods, to say truthfully whose wife she is.
shots.B01C005S02H05: He presses Agni again. Agni fears speaking; the Rakshasa insists that, since Agni lives in every creature as witness, he must answer, then he will take her.
shots.B01C005S03H01: Agni answers slowly: she was chosen by the Rakshasa but not married to him with rites. Her father gave her to Bhrigu and the marriage was done before Agni, so she is Bhrigu's wife.

B01C006.summary: The Rakshasa turns into a boar and carries Puloma off, but her unborn child drops from the womb with such fiery power that the demon is burnt to ashes. The child is named Chyavana (the one who fell). Her tears become the river Vadhusara. When Bhrigu learns that Agni identified her, he curses Agni to eat everything.

scenes.B01C006S01: The Rakshasa carries Puloma away as a boar, and her baby falls out and burns him to ashes. Brahma comforts her and names her tear-river. Bhrigu learns Agni gave her away and curses him to eat all things.

shots.B01C006S01H02: As the boar-demon runs with Puloma, the child falls from her womb, which is why he is called Chyavana. The demon is burnt to ashes. Brahma comforts the weeping mother and her tears become the river Vadhusara, which flows past Chyavana's hermitage.
shots.B01C006S01H03: Bhrigu angrily asks how the Rakshasa knew his wife. Puloma says Agni told him and that the child's brilliance saved her.
shots.B01C006S01H04: Bhrigu curses Agni: "Thou shalt eat of all things."
shots.B01C006S01H05: Closing line: the sixth section, the curse on Agni.

B01C007.summary: Agni protests the curse, saying he only told the truth and that he carries offerings to gods and ancestors. He withdraws from the world, stopping all rites. The gods and sages go to Brahma, who softens the curse: only the flame in Agni's lowest parts will devour everything, and whatever Agni burns becomes pure. Agni agrees and rites resume.

scenes.B01C007S01: Agni defends himself, then goes into hiding and all sacrifices stop. The gods take the problem to Brahma, who limits the curse. Agni returns and the rites resume.
scenes.B01C007S02: Closing line: the seventh section ends.

shots.B01C007S01H02: Agni replies that a truthful witness cannot be blamed, explains that he is the mouth through which gods and ancestors receive offerings, and asks how he can be an eater of unclean things.
shots.B01C007S01H03: Agni withdraws from all sacrificial fires; rites stop and creatures suffer. The gods and sages go to Brahma, who calls Agni and says the curse will only apply to his lower flame, and that everything burnt by Agni is purified.
shots.B01C007S01H04: Agni accepts, the gods and sages leave happy, and rituals resume.
shots.B01C007S01H05: Sauti sums up: this is how Agni was cursed and how the Rakshasa Puloma died and Chyavana was born.
shots.B01C007S02H01: Closing line: the seventh section of the Pauloma Parva ends.

B01C008.summary: The line of Bhrigu continues: Chyavana's son Pramati has a son, Ruru. The Apsara Menaka leaves her baby daughter by the river, and the sage Sthulakesa raises her as Pramadvara. Ruru falls in love and is betrothed to her, but days before the wedding she steps on a snake and dies. The sages gather around her and weep, and Ruru withdraws in grief.

scenes.B01C008S01: Descent from Chyavana to Ruru. The story of Pramadvara's birth and upbringing, her betrothal to Ruru, her death from snakebite, and the grief of the sages.

shots.B01C008S01H02: Sauti repeats the line (Chyavana, Pramati, Ruru, Sunaka) and promises the full story of Ruru.
shots.B01C008S01H03: The Apsara Menaka bears a girl by the Gandharva king Viswavasu and abandons her by Sthulakesa's hermitage. The sage raises her and names her Pramadvara. Ruru sees her, falls in love, and Pramati asks for her hand; the wedding is fixed for an auspicious star.
shots.B01C008S01H04: Days before the wedding, while playing, Pramadvara steps on a hidden snake and is bitten. She dies, yet looks more beautiful than before. Sages and friends gather and weep, and Ruru, overwhelmed, withdraws.
shots.B01C008S01H05: Closing line: the eighth section ends.

B01C009.summary: Ruru weeps in the forest and offers his own merit to bring Pramadvara back. A heavenly messenger says she can live if Ruru gives her half his lifespan. Dharma, the judge of the dead, agrees, and she revives. They marry, but Ruru, bitter about the snakebite, vows to kill every snake. One day he lifts his staff to kill an old Dundubha snake, which asks why.

scenes.B01C009S01: Ruru's grief in the forest, the heavenly messenger's offer, and Dharma's consent to revive Pramadvara with half of Ruru's life.
scenes.B01C009S02: Pramadvara wakes, the two marry, and Ruru begins killing snakes. He meets a Dundubha snake and raises his staff to strike it.

shots.B01C009S01H02: Ruru runs into the forest and cries out, offering all his good deeds and vows if Pramadvara can live again.
shots.B01C009S01H03: A messenger from heaven tells him the dead cannot normally return, but the gods have made one provision to restore her.
shots.B01C009S01H04: Ruru asks what it is. The messenger says he must give half of his own life to her. Ruru agrees gladly.
shots.B01C009S01H05: The messenger and the Gandharva king ask Dharma, judge of the dead, to let Pramadvara rise with half of Ruru's life. Dharma agrees.
shots.B01C009S02H01: Pramadvara wakes as if from sleep. Because Ruru gave half his lifespan, his own life is cut short.
shots.B01C009S02H02: Their fathers marry them. Ruru, now vowing to destroy snakes, kills every serpent he sees.
shots.B01C009S02H03: In a forest Ruru finds an old Dundubha snake and lifts a staff to kill it. The snake asks what harm it ever did him.
shots.B01C009S02H04: Closing line: the ninth section ends.

B01C010.summary: Ruru says his wife died of a snakebite so he has sworn to kill all snakes. The Dundubha answers that harmless Dundubhas are snakes only in name and should not be killed. Ruru spares it and asks who it is. The snake says it was once a sage named Sahasrapat and was cursed into this shape.

scenes.B01C010S01: Ruru explains his vow, the snake pleads for its kind, Ruru spares it, and the snake reveals it is a cursed sage.

shots.B01C010S01H02: Ruru says a snake killed his wife, so he has vowed to kill every snake and intends to kill this one.
shots.B01C010S01H03: The Dundubha says the snakes that bite men are different from Dundubhas, who are snakes in name only and share the sufferings but not the fortunes of other serpents.
shots.B01C010S01H04: Ruru sees the snake is terrified and does not kill it. He asks who it really is, and the snake says it was once a sage named Sahasrapat, cursed by a Brahmana. Ruru asks why and for how long.
shots.B01C010S01H05: Closing line: the tenth section ends.

B01C011.summary: Sahasrapat explains: as a joke he scared his friend, the ascetic Khagama, with a toy snake made of grass, and Khagama cursed him to become a harmless snake until he met Ruru. Seeing Ruru frees him and he regains his human form. He tells Ruru that sparing life is the highest duty of a Brahmana, that a Brahmana should not take life, and promises the story of the snake sacrifice and Astika.

scenes.B01C011S01: The story of the curse on Sahasrapat, his release at the sight of Ruru, and his lesson that Brahmanas must be gentle and not kill.

shots.B01C011S01H02: Sahasrapat tells how he frightened his friend Khagama at his fire rite with a grass snake. Khagama cursed him to be a snake until Ruru appeared, and the sage said sight of Ruru would end the curse.
shots.B01C011S01H03: Restored to human form, Sahasrapat tells Ruru that the highest duty is to spare life, Brahmanas should be gentle, and ruling and punishing are for kings. He promises to tell of the snake-sacrifice of Janamejaya and how Astika saved the serpents.
shots.B01C011S01H04: Closing line: the eleventh section ends.

B01C012.summary: Ruru asks why Janamejaya wanted to destroy the serpents and how Astika saved them. The sage says Brahmanas will tell him this, then vanishes. Ruru searches for him in vain, faints, recovers and asks his father, who tells him the story.

scenes.B01C012S01: Ruru asks for the Astika story, the sage disappears, and Ruru's father relates it.

shots.B01C012S01H02: Ruru asks why Janamejaya tried to destroy the serpents and how Astika saved them.
shots.B01C012S01H03: The sage replies that Brahmanas will tell him the story and disappears.
shots.B01C012S01H04: Ruru searches the woods, collapses, then goes home and asks his father, who tells him the story.
shots.B01C012S01H05: Closing line: the twelfth section ends.

B01C013.summary: The Astika section opens. Saunaka asks why Janamejaya wanted to kill snakes and how Astika saved them. Sauti begins with Astika's father, the ascetic Jaratkaru, who finds his ancestors hanging head down over a pit because he has no children. They tell him to marry and have a son. Jaratkaru agrees on the condition that the bride share his name and be offered freely.

scenes.B01C013S01: Saunaka's questions and Sauti's promise to tell the Astika story as he heard it from his father.
scenes.B01C013S02: The wandering ascetic Jaratkaru finds his ancestors hanging in a pit, eaten away by a rat, because he has no descendants.
scenes.B01C013S03: The ancestors urge him to marry. He promises to wed only a bride of his own name offered as alms.

shots.B01C013S01H02: Saunaka asks why Janamejaya wanted to kill the snakes, why Astika saved them, and whose sons they were.
shots.B01C013S01H03: Sauti says the story is long and promises to tell it fully.
shots.B01C013S01H04: Saunaka asks to hear it at length.
shots.B01C013S01H05: Sauti says Vyasa first told this Purana, his father Lomaharshana repeated it, and he will tell it as he heard it.
shots.B01C013S02H01: Jaratkaru is a strict celibate ascetic who travels the world. One day he sees his ancestors hanging head down in a hole.
shots.B01C013S02H02: He asks who they are, noting that the rope holding them is being gnawed by a rat.
shots.B01C013S02H03: They say they are sages hanging for lack of descendants, because their son Jaratkaru does only austerities and will not marry.
shots.B01C013S02H04: Jaratkaru says he is that son.
shots.B01C013S02H05: He asks how to help them.
shots.B01C013S03H01: They tell him to marry and have a son, because becoming a father is worth more than penance.
shots.B01C013S03H02: Jaratkaru promises to marry only for their sake, with a bride who shares his name, offered freely, and to have a child with her so they can reach heaven.
shots.B01C013S03H03: Closing line: the thirteenth section ends.

B01C014.summary: Jaratkaru searches for a wife and finds none. In the forest he prays aloud for a bride, and the serpent king Vasuki offers his sister, whose name is also Jaratkaru. The sage accepts and marries her.

scenes.B01C014S01: Jaratkaru's search, Vasuki's offer of his sister of the same name, and the marriage.

shots.B01C014S01H02: After wandering without success, Jaratkaru asks aloud in the forest for a bride. Vasuki appears with his sister. The sage asks her name because he will wed only one with his own name.
shots.B01C014S01H03: Vasuki says her name is Jaratkaru and gives her to him. They marry with proper rites.
shots.B01C014S01H04: Closing line (numbered thirteenth in the source, though it is the fourteenth section).

B01C015.summary: The serpents' mother had cursed them to be burnt in Janamejaya's sacrifice, and Vasuki married off his sister to prevent that. Their son Astika grew up wise and later saved the serpents at the sacrifice. Jaratkaru paid his debts to the gods, sages and ancestors, his ancestors went to heaven, and he later died. Sauti asks what to tell next.

scenes.B01C015S01: Why Vasuki married his sister to the sage, the birth of Astika, and a summary of how Astika saved the snakes and freed his father's ancestors.

shots.B01C015S01H02: The mother of the snakes had cursed them to burn in Janamejaya's sacrifice. Vasuki married his sister to the sage to counter it, and their son Astika was born, a wise Vedic scholar.
shots.B01C015S01H03: Later, at the snake sacrifice, Astika saved his brothers and uncles. By his austerities, sacrifices and offspring he paid his debts to the sages, gods and ancestors.
shots.B01C015S01H04: Jaratkaru's ancestors rose to heaven, and he too went there after many years. Sauti ends his summary and asks what to tell next.
shots.B01C015S01H05: Closing line: the fifteenth section ends.

B01C016.summary: Saunaka asks Sauti to retell the Astika story from the beginning. Sauti starts with Kasyapa's two wives, the sisters Kadru and Vinata. Kadru is granted a thousand snake sons and Vinata two stronger sons. After five hundred years, Vinata impatiently breaks one egg and the half-formed son Aruna curses her to become a slave, with the other son Garuda as her eventual rescuer. Aruna becomes the sun's charioteer, and Garuda hatches and flies off in search of food.

scenes.B01C016S01: Saunaka's request. The story of Kadru and Vinata, their boons from Kasyapa, the eggs, Vinata's mistake and Aruna's curse, and Garuda's birth.
scenes.B01C016S02: Closing line: the sixteenth section ends.

shots.B01C016S01H02: Saunaka praises Sauti's speech and asks him to tell Astika's story in full as his father did.
shots.B01C016S01H03: Sauti tells how Prajapati's daughters Kadru and Vinata marry Kasyapa. Kasyapa offers each a boon: Kadru asks for a thousand equal snakes, Vinata asks for two sons stronger than all of them. Both are granted.
shots.B01C016S01H04: Kadru lays a thousand eggs and Vinata two. After five hundred years Kadru's hatch but Vinata's do not. Vinata breaks one egg early and finds a half-formed son, who curses her to become a slave unless she waits for the second egg. He rises to the sky as Aruna, charioteer of the sun.
shots.B01C016S01H05: After five hundred years the second egg hatches and out comes Garuda, who leaves his mother at once and flies off to find food.
shots.B01C016S02H01: Closing line: the sixteenth section ends.

B01C017.summary: The two sisters see the splendid horse Uchchaihsravas, born when the gods churned the ocean. Saunaka asks why the ocean was churned. Sauti begins describing the golden Mount Meru, where the gods met, anxious for the nectar of immortality, and Narayana told Brahma that the gods and Asuras should churn the ocean.

scenes.B01C017S01: The sisters see Uchchaihsravas, the question about the churning, and the gods' assembly on Mount Meru where the churning is advised.

shots.B01C017S01H02: Kadru and Vinata see the beautiful horse Uchchaihsravas, who rose from the churning of the ocean.
shots.B01C017S01H03: Saunaka asks why the gods churned the ocean and how the horse arose.
shots.B01C017S01H04: Sauti describes shining Mount Meru, where the gods meet. Wanting nectar, they hear Narayana tell Brahma to churn the ocean with the gods and Asuras, to win nectar, herbs and jewels.
shots.B01C017S01H05: Closing line: the seventeenth section ends.

B01C018.summary: The gods prepare to churn the ocean. Ananta uproots Mount Mandara, a tortoise carries it on his back, and the serpent Vasuki serves as the rope, with Asuras at his head and gods at his tail. Destruction and fire follow, put out by Indra's rain. Tired, the gods ask Narayana for strength. The moon, Lakshmi, Soma, the white horse, the Kaustubha jewel, Dhanwantari with the nectar, and the elephant Airavata rise, then the deadly poison Kalakuta, which Siva swallows and so gets a blue throat. Narayana then takes the form of an enchanting woman and gets the nectar from the Asuras.

scenes.B01C018S01: Preparations: Mandara is uprooted, placed on the tortoise, and used as a churning staff with Vasuki as rope. The churning begins and creates chaos.
scenes.B01C018S02: The gods tire and Narayana renews their strength. Treasures rise from the ocean, the poison Kalakuta is swallowed by Siva, and Narayana, as an enchantress, takes the nectar.
scenes.B01C018S03: Closing line: the eighteenth section ends.

shots.B01C018S01H02: Mount Mandara is described. The gods cannot lift it as a churning rod and ask Vishnu and Brahma for a plan.
shots.B01C018S01H03: Vishnu has Ananta tear up the mountain. The ocean agrees to be churned if it gets a share, and the king of tortoises agrees to carry the mountain on his back.
shots.B01C018S01H04: With Mandara as staff and Vasuki as rope (Asuras at the head, gods at the tail), they churn. Vasuki's smoke becomes rain clouds that refresh the gods.
shots.B01C018S01H05: The ocean roars, creatures are crushed, trees burst into fire, and the mountain burns until Indra puts the fire out with rain.
shots.B01C018S02H01: Plant juices turn the water into butter, but no nectar appears. The gods tell Brahma they are spent.
shots.B01C018S02H02: Brahma asks Narayana to give the gods strength.
shots.B01C018S02H03: Narayana gives them strength and tells them to resume.
shots.B01C018S02H04: Churning resumes. The moon, Lakshmi, Soma, the white horse, the jewel Kaustubha and Dhanwantari with the nectar jar rise. The Asuras shout that the nectar is theirs.
shots.B01C018S02H05: The elephant Airavata rises and Indra takes him. Then the poison Kalakuta spreads, and Siva swallows it at Brahma's request and becomes blue-throated. The Asuras prepare to fight, and Narayana charms them as a beautiful woman and takes the nectar.
shots.B01C018S03H01: Closing line: the eighteenth section ends.

B01C019.summary: The Asuras attack, but Vishnu as the enchantress takes the nectar, and the gods drink it. The demon Rahu drinks among them in disguise, and Vishnu cuts off his head, which is why Rahu's head still swallows the sun and moon in eclipses. A huge battle follows on the sea shore; Vishnu's discus Sudarsana kills thousands, Nara breaks the hurled mountains with arrows, and the Asuras flee into the earth and sea. The gods put Mandara back and give the nectar to Narayana to keep.

scenes.B01C019S01: The gods drink the nectar, Rahu is beheaded, and the battle against the Asuras begins and is turned by Vishnu's discus.
scenes.B01C019S02: The Asuras hurl mountains but are driven into the earth and sea. The gods return Mandara and give the nectar to Narayana.

shots.B01C019S01H02: The Asuras attack the gods, but Vishnu, in female form with Nara, tricks them and takes the nectar.
shots.B01C019S01H03: The gods drink. Rahu drinks in disguise, the sun and moon warn the gods, and Narayana cuts off his head with a discus. Head and body fall, and the head's grudge against the sun and moon explains eclipses.
shots.B01C019S01H04: Narayana drops the disguise and the gods and Asuras battle on the shore. The field fills with blood, cries and fallen warriors.
shots.B01C019S01H05: Nara and Narayana join the fight. Narayana calls his discus Sudarsana, which arrives blazing and destroys Asuras by thousands.
shots.B01C019S02H01: The Asuras hurl mountains from the sky. Nara shatters them with golden arrows. Seeing the discus, the Asuras flee into the earth and the sea.
shots.B01C019S02H02: The gods return Mandara to its place, shout in victory, go home, and give the nectar to Narayana to guard.
shots.B01C019S02H03: Closing line: the nineteenth section ends.

B01C020.summary: Sauti finishes the churning story and returns to the sisters. Kadru and Vinata bet on the colour of the horse Uchchaihsravas: Vinata says it is white, Kadru says its tail is black, and the loser will be a slave. Kadru orders her snake sons to turn into black hairs on the tail, but they refuse, so she curses them to burn in Janamejaya's sacrifice. Brahma approves the curse, since the snakes are poisonous and harm creatures, and tells Kasyapa not to grieve, giving him the knowledge to neutralise poison.

scenes.B01C020S01: The wager of the sisters, Kadru's trick, her curse on her own sons, and Brahma's approval of it.

shots.B01C020S01H02: Sauti ends the churning story. Kadru and Vinata argue about the colour of the horse Uchchaihsravas and wager slavery: Vinata says it is all white, Kadru says the tail is black.
shots.B01C020S01H03: Kadru tells her snake sons to become black hairs on the tail. They refuse, so she curses them to burn at Janamejaya's snake sacrifice. Brahma and the gods approve, reasoning that deadly snakes deserve it, and Brahma comforts Kasyapa and teaches him how to cure poison.
shots.B01C020S01H04: Closing line: the twentieth section ends.

B01C021.summary: The next morning the sisters set out to see the horse and pass over the ocean. The chapter is a long poetic description of the sea: its depth, creatures, gems, rivers pouring in, its use as Vishnu's bed, and the place where the Asuras hide.

scenes.B01C021S01: The sisters' journey and a long poetic description of the ocean.

shots.B01C021S01H02: On their way the sisters see the ocean, described at length as vast, roaring, full of monsters, gems, Nagas and Asuras, and as the bed of Vishnu in his cosmic sleep.
shots.B01C021S01H03: They see rivers flowing into it, its waves dancing and its limitless expanse.
shots.B01C021S01H04: Closing line: the twenty-first section ends.

B01C022.summary: The snakes decide to obey their mother so as not to lose her favour and become hairs on the horse's tail. The sisters fly over the ocean to see the horse, with another description of the sea.

scenes.B01C022S01: The snakes decide to obey Kadru and turn into black tail hairs. The sisters cross the ocean.

shots.B01C022S01H02: The snakes reason it is safer to please their mother, hope she may lift the curse, and turn into black hairs in the horse's tail.
shots.B01C022S01H03: The two sisters fly across the sky and the ocean, described again in detail.
shots.B01C022S01H04: Closing line: the twenty-second section ends.
shots.B01C022S01H05: Heading of the next section (XXIII) printed here in the source.

B01C023.summary: Kadru and Vinata reach the horse. It is white except for black hairs in the tail, so Vinata loses and becomes Kadru's slave. Garuda hatches by himself, blazing so brightly that the gods fear him to be fire. Agni explains he is Vinata's son Garuda. The gods approach and praise Garuda at length as the supreme one, asking him to reduce his brilliance, and he does so.

scenes.B01C023S01: Vinata loses the wager and is enslaved. Garuda hatches and terrifies the gods, who are reassured by Agni and then praise Garuda until he calms down.
scenes.B01C023S02: Closing line: the twenty-third section ends.

shots.B01C023S01H02: The sisters reach the horse and see the black hairs in its tail. Kadru makes Vinata her slave, and Vinata is deeply sorry.
shots.B01C023S01H03: Meanwhile Garuda is born, shining like the fire at the end of the age. Frightened, the gods go to Agni, who says this is not fire but Garuda, Kasyapa's son, born to please Vinata and an enemy of the snakes.
shots.B01C023S01H04: The gods approach Garuda and praise him with a long hymn, calling him the creator, the lord of all, and asking him to be merciful and lessen his brightness.
shots.B01C023S01H05: Pleased by the praise, Garuda reduces his energy and splendour.
shots.B01C023S02H01: Closing line: the twenty-third section ends (the sentence continues in the next shot).

B01C024.summary: Garuda shrinks his body, carries his brother Aruna to the east and sets him in front of the sun. Sauti explains why: Surya had been angry at Rahu's enmity after he exposed Rahu, and resolved to burn the world. Brahma arranged for Aruna to be Surya's charioteer and shield the world from his heat.

scenes.B01C024S01: Garuda reduces his size and carries Aruna to the east. Saunaka asks why Surya was angry.
scenes.B01C024S02: Surya's anger at the gods after Rahu's enmity, the panic of the world, and Brahma's remedy of making Aruna his charioteer.

shots.B01C024S01H02: Garuda hears the praise, sees his own huge form, and shrinks it.
shots.B01C024S01H03: He tells all creatures not to be afraid, as he will lessen his fire.
shots.B01C024S01H04: Carrying his brother Aruna, Garuda goes to his mother across the ocean and sets Aruna in the east just as the sun was about to scorch the worlds.
shots.B01C024S01H05: Saunaka asks why Surya wanted to burn the worlds and what the gods did to anger him.
shots.B01C024S02H01: Surya had exposed Rahu to the gods. Rahu now wanted to devour him, and Surya, feeling abandoned by the gods, decided to destroy the worlds and went to the western mountains.
shots.B01C024S02H02: A great heat spreads at midnight and the gods and sages go to Brahma in alarm. Brahma says Surya will burn everything, but Aruna will stand before him as charioteer and take his heat away.
shots.B01C024S02H03: Aruna does so and the sun rises veiled by him. Sauti has answered the question and will now continue.
shots.B01C024S02H04: Closing line: the twenty-fourth section ends.

B01C025.summary: Garuda goes to his mother Vinata, who is Kadru's slave. Kadru orders Vinata to carry her to a snake island, and Garuda carries the snakes. As he flies up toward the sun, the heat scorches the snakes. Kadru prays to Indra with a long hymn, asking him to save them with rain.

scenes.B01C025S01: Kadru commands Vinata to carry her to the Nagas' island, Garuda carries the snakes toward the sun, and Kadru prays to Indra for help.

shots.B01C025S01H02: Vinata, enslaved, carries Kadru on her shoulders and Garuda carries the snakes. As he flies up toward the sun the heat makes the snakes faint, so Kadru prays to Indra at length, praising him as the source of rain, the creator and destroyer, and everything else, and asks him to protect her sons.
shots.B01C025S01H03: Closing line: the twenty-fifth section ends.

B01C026.summary: Indra answers Kadru's prayer and sends storm clouds that pour rain, shielding the snakes and cooling the earth. They reach the island of Ramaniyaka safely.

scenes.B01C026S01: Indra covers the sky with clouds and a great rain falls. The snakes and their mother reach Ramaniyaka.

shots.B01C026S01H02: Indra covers the sky with dark clouds and orders them to pour. The downpour is so heavy that the sky seems to dance and the sun and moon vanish.
shots.B01C026S01H03: The snakes rejoice. Water covers the earth and reaches the underworld. They arrive at the island Ramaniyaka.
shots.B01C026S01H04: Closing line: the twenty-sixth section ends.

B01C027.summary: The snakes enjoy the beautiful forested island, then order Garuda to take them to another island. Garuda asks his mother why he must serve the snakes, and Vinata tells him of her wager and enslavement. Garuda asks the snakes what price will free them. They say: bring the nectar of immortality by force.

scenes.B01C027S01: The snakes land on the island and enjoy it. Garuda learns why they are enslaved and asks the snakes the price of freedom. They demand amrita.
scenes.B01C027S02: End of the closing line of the twenty-seventh section.

shots.B01C027S01H02: Garuda carries the snakes to an island by the salt ocean, described as a lovely forest with flowers, lakes, bees and birds, which delights them.
shots.B01C027S01H03: The snakes then tell Garuda to take them to another island. Garuda asks his mother why he must serve them. Vinata tells him how she lost the wager by the snakes' deceit. Garuda asks the snakes what he can do to free them both.
shots.B01C027S01H04: The snakes answer: bring amrita by force and you will be free.
shots.B01C027S01H05: Closing line of the twenty-seventh section begins (it ends in the next shot).

B01C028.summary: Garuda tells his mother he will fetch the nectar and asks what to eat on the way. Vinata sends him to the Nishadas (fisher tribe) living by the sea, but warns him never to kill a Brahmana, whom she says is like fire, and gives him signs to recognise one: a Brahmana will burn his throat and not be digested. She blesses him. Garuda attacks the Nishadas, stirring up dust, and swallows thousands of them.

scenes.B01C028S01: Vinata's advice about Brahmanas and her blessing, and Garuda's attack on the Nishada fishermen.

shots.B01C028S01H02: Garuda asks his mother for food before he goes. She sends him to the Nishadas but warns him never to kill a Brahmana, who is dangerous when angry. Garuda asks how to recognise one. She says he will burn his throat like a fish-hook and not be digested. She blesses him with protection by the wind, sun, moon, fire and Vasus.
shots.B01C028S01H03: Garuda flies off and raids the Nishada town. He stirs up dust, blocks the roads with his open mouth, and the blinded people rush into it. He shuts his mouth, killing countless fishermen.
shots.B01C028S01H04: Closing line: the twenty-eighth section ends.

B01C029.summary: A Brahmana and his Nishada wife are swallowed in Garuda's throat and burn it. Garuda lets them out. He tells his father Kasyapa he is still hungry. Kasyapa shows him a lake where an elephant and a tortoise, who were once brothers named Supritika and Vibhavasu, fight each other because they cursed each other over a quarrel about inheritance. He tells Garuda to eat them and bless him for the fight with the gods. Garuda seizes them and lands on a huge banyan tree, whose branch breaks.

scenes.B01C029S01: The Brahmana escapes from Garuda's throat. Garuda meets his father Kasyapa and asks for more food.
scenes.B01C029S02: Kasyapa tells the story of the brothers cursed to be an elephant and a tortoise, blesses Garuda, and Garuda picks up both and lands on a giant banyan whose branch breaks.

shots.B01C029S01H02: A Brahmana with a Nishada wife burns Garuda's throat. Garuda tells him to come out. The Brahmana asks to bring his wife too, and Garuda agrees.
shots.B01C029S01H03: The couple leave and Garuda flies on. Kasyapa greets him and asks if he finds enough food.
shots.B01C029S01H04: Garuda says his mother is well but he is still hungry. He has eaten thousands of Nishadas and wants more food, enough to be strong to take the nectar.
shots.B01C029S01H05: Kasyapa points to a lake where an elephant keeps dragging a tortoise, and begins to tell why.
shots.B01C029S02H01: Two brothers, Vibhavasu and Supritika, quarrelled over dividing their inheritance. Vibhavasu warned against partition, and when Supritika insisted he cursed him to become an elephant. Supritika cursed him in turn to become a tortoise.
shots.B01C029S02H02: They now fight in the lake, the elephant six yojanas tall and the tortoise three. Kasyapa tells Garuda to eat both and then fetch the nectar.
shots.B01C029S02H03: Kasyapa blesses Garuda for the coming fight with the gods.
shots.B01C029S02H04: Garuda picks up the elephant and the tortoise, flies to a grove of gold and gem-bearing trees, and a huge banyan offers its branch. As he lands the branch breaks.
shots.B01C029S02H05: Closing line: the twenty-ninth section ends.

B01C030.summary: The broken branch holds the Valakhilya sages hanging head down. Garuda catches it in his beak to save them, gets his name for carrying such a load, and flies to Kasyapa on Mount Gandhamadana. Kasyapa persuades the sages to leave the branch and they go to the Himalayas. Garuda drops the branch on a deserted snowy peak and eats the elephant and tortoise. Meanwhile bad omens appear in heaven. Indra's teacher Vrihaspati explains that Garuda is coming for the nectar, and the gods arm and guard it.

scenes.B01C030S01: Garuda saves the Valakhilya sages, receives the name Garuda, and Kasyapa asks the sages to let go of the branch.
scenes.B01C030S02: Garuda drops the branch on an empty mountain and eats the elephant and tortoise. Omens appear in heaven, Vrihaspati explains them, and Indra and the gods prepare to defend the nectar.

shots.B01C030S01H02: The branch breaks and Garuda sees the Valakhilya sages hanging from it head down. To save them he holds the branch in his beak and rises. The astonished sages name him Garuda, the bearer of heavy weight.
shots.B01C030S01H03: He cannot find a place to put the branch and goes to Mount Gandhamadana, where his father Kasyapa is meditating. Kasyapa sees his huge form.
shots.B01C030S01H04: Kasyapa warns him not to act rashly, because the sages could burn him with their anger.
shots.B01C030S01H05: Kasyapa asks the Valakhilyas to let Garuda do his task, which is for the good of all.
shots.B01C030S02H01: The sages leave the branch and go to the Himalayas. Kasyapa directs Garuda to a mountain without people. He flies there and drops the giant branch, shaking the mountain.
shots.B01C030S02H02: Garuda sits on the peak, eats the elephant and tortoise, and flies up again.
shots.B01C030S02H03: Omens strike heaven: Indra's thunderbolt flares, meteors fall, weapons clash and blood rains. Indra asks Vrihaspati why. Vrihaspati says Garuda is coming to take the nectar, because of Indra's carelessness and the Valakhilyas' penance.
shots.B01C030S02H04: Indra warns the nectar's guards, and the gods put on armour and take up weapons and surround the nectar.
shots.B01C030S02H05: Closing line: the thirtieth section ends.

B01C031.summary: Saunaka asks how Garuda came to be born. Sauti tells how Indra, carrying logs for Kasyapa's sacrifice, laughed at the tiny Valakhilya sages struggling with a leaf-stalk. Angered, they performed a rite to create a rival Indra. Indra begged Kasyapa for help, and Kasyapa persuaded the sages to let the new Indra be a lord of birds, Kasyapa's own son. Vinata then bore Aruna and Garuda, and Indra was warned never to insult Brahmanas again.

scenes.B01C031S01: Saunaka's questions, and the story of how Indra mocked the Valakhilyas and they began a sacrifice to create a rival to him.
scenes.B01C031S02: Kasyapa mediates: the new Indra will be a bird king and his son. Vinata conceives and bears Aruna and Garuda.
scenes.B01C031S03: Closing line: the thirty-first section ends.

shots.B01C031S01H02: Saunaka asks what Indra's fault was, how the Valakhilyas' penance made Garuda, and why Garuda has such powers.
shots.B01C031S01H03: Sauti says the Purana tells it and promises a short account.
shots.B01C031S01H04: At Kasyapa's sacrifice Indra fetches fuel. He passes the thumb-sized Valakhilyas, weak and carrying one leaf-stalk, laughs and steps over them. They begin a rite to create another Indra. Frightened, Indra runs to Kasyapa, who asks the sages not to break Brahma's order that Indra rules.
shots.B01C031S01H05: The Valakhilyas begin to reply to Kasyapa (the speech continues in the next shot).
shots.B01C031S02H01: They say the rite was meant for an Indra and also for a son of Kasyapa's.
shots.B01C031S02H02: They leave the matter to Kasyapa to settle as he thinks right.
shots.B01C031S02H04: Vinata, after her penance, approaches Kasyapa. He says the sacrifice has borne fruit and she will have two mighty sons who will rule all winged creatures.
shots.B01C031S02H05: Kasyapa tells Indra that the two sons will be his helpers, not rivals, and warns him never to insult Brahmanas again. Vinata gives birth to Aruna, who is the forerunner of the sun, and Garuda, lord of birds.
shots.B01C031S03H01: Closing line: the thirty-first section ends.

B01C032.summary: Garuda fights the gods who guard the nectar. He defeats the craftsman god Viswakarma, blinds the gods with dust, and fights off Indra's attacks with talons and wings, causing them to flee in four directions. He kills several Yaksha guards, drinks rivers with many mouths to put out the fire ringing the nectar, and shrinks to enter.

scenes.B01C032S01: The battle of Garuda against the gods and Yakshas, and his quenching of the fire around the nectar.
scenes.B01C032S02: Closing line: the thirty-second section ends.

shots.B01C032S01H02: Garuda reaches the gods, who tremble. He crushes the guard Viswakarma in an instant and blinds the rest with the dust from his wings.
shots.B01C032S01H03: Indra orders the wind to clear the dust. The gods attack with swords, maces, lances and discuses. Garuda fights on, and the gods flee in all four directions.
shots.B01C032S01H04: Garuda fights ten named Yaksha guards and leaves them bleeding.
shots.B01C032S01H05: He finds the nectar ringed by flames. He takes ninety times ninety mouths, drinks many rivers, puts out the fire, and shrinks himself to enter.
shots.B01C032S02H01: Closing line: the thirty-second section ends.

B01C033.summary: Garuda passes through a razor-sharp spinning wheel, blinds and kills two fiery guardian snakes, and seizes the nectar without tasting it. Vishnu is pleased by his restraint and grants him the boons of immortality and a seat above him; Garuda becomes Vishnu's mount and emblem on his flag. Indra hurls his thunderbolt, but Garuda is unhurt and sheds a feather in respect, earning the name Suparna. Indra, impressed, asks for friendship and to know his strength.

scenes.B01C033S01: Garuda gets past the wheel and snakes, takes the nectar, meets Vishnu and gets boons, is struck by Indra's thunderbolt and sheds a feather, and Indra offers friendship.
scenes.B01C033S02: Closing line: the thirty-third section ends.

shots.B01C033S01H02: Garuda enters in a golden form, shrinks to slip between the spokes of the cutting wheel, blinds the two fire-breathing guard snakes with dust and tears them apart, shatters the machine and flies off with the nectar without drinking it.
shots.B01C033S01H03: Vishnu, pleased by Garuda's self-denial, offers a boon. Garuda asks to stay above him and to be immortal without the nectar. Vishnu agrees and asks Garuda to be his carrier, placing him on his chariot flag.
shots.B01C033S01H04: Indra hurls his thunderbolt at Garuda, who laughs and says he respects the thunderbolt, Indra and the sage Dadhichi whose bone made it, drops one feather as a sign of this, and is named Suparna for it.
shots.B01C033S01H05: Indra asks to know Garuda's strength and to be his friend.
shots.B01C033S02H01: Closing line: the thirty-third section ends.

B01C034.summary: Garuda and Indra become friends. Garuda boasts that he can carry the earth and all the worlds on a single feather. Indra asks for the nectar back, and Garuda says he will set it down so Indra can take it. As a favour Garuda asks that snakes become his food, which Indra grants. Garuda gives the snakes the nectar on kusa grass and tells them to bathe first; Indra takes it away. The snakes lick the grass and their tongues split. Garuda eats snakes, and Sauti closes with the blessing for hearing this tale.

scenes.B01C034S01: The friendship of Garuda and Indra, Garuda's boast, and the plan to return the nectar. Garuda asks that snakes be his food.
scenes.B01C034S02: The snakes lose the nectar, their tongues split, Garuda frees his mother, and the story ends with its benefit.

shots.B01C034S01H02: Garuda accepts the friendship and says he can carry the earth, mountains and oceans on one feather.
shots.B01C034S01H03: Indra agrees and asks for the nectar back, since those who drink it will oppose the gods. Garuda says he'll not give it to anyone but will set it down for Indra to take. Indra offers him a boon.
shots.B01C034S01H04: Garuda asks that snakes become his food. Indra agrees and Vishnu approves. Garuda returns to his mother.
shots.B01C034S01H05: Garuda puts the nectar on kusa grass and tells the snakes to wash first. While they bathe, Indra takes it. The snakes lick the grass and their tongues are split in two. The grass becomes sacred.
shots.B01C034S02H01: Garuda lives happily in the woods with his mother, eating snakes.
shots.B01C034S02H02: Sauti says whoever hears or recites this story goes to heaven.
shots.B01C034S02H03: Closing line: the thirty-fourth section ends.

B01C035.summary: Saunaka asks for the names of the snakes. Sauti gives a list of the chief ones, starting with Sesha and Vasuki and naming dozens more, and says the rest are too many to name.

scenes.B01C035S01: Saunaka's request and Sauti's introduction to the list. The list begins with Sesha, Vasuki and others.
scenes.B01C035S02: First part of the list of snake names.
scenes.B01C035S03: Second part of the list of snake names.
scenes.B01C035S04: Last names, and Sauti's remark that the rest are countless.

shots.B01C035S01H02: Saunaka asks for the names of the principal snakes.
shots.B01C035S01H03: Sauti agrees to give only the chief ones, to avoid length.
shots.B01C035S01H04: The list begins: Sesha first, then Vasuki, then Airavata.
shots.B01C035S01H05: Names continued: Takshaka, Karkotaka, Dhananjaya and others.
shots.B01C035S02H01: Names continued: Pinjaraka, Elapatra and others.
shots.B01C035S02H02: Names continued: Ugra, Kalasapotaka and others.
shots.B01C035S02H03: Names continued: Samkha, Valisikha, Nahusha and others.
shots.B01C035S02H04: Names continued: Hastipada, Kaliyaka and others.
shots.B01C035S02H05: Names continued: Padma, Mahapadma and others.
shots.B01C035S03H02: Names continued: Purnabhadra, Kauravya and others.
shots.B01C035S03H03: Names continued: Dhritarashtra, Sankhapinda and others.
shots.B01C035S03H04: Names continued: Kunjara, Kumuda and others.
shots.B01C035S03H05: Names continued: Kumudaksha, Karkara and others.
shots.B01C035S04H02: Sauti says the sons and grandsons of these snakes are countless, so he will not name them.
shots.B01C035S04H03: Closing line: the thirty-fifth section ends.

B01C036.summary: Saunaka asks what the snakes did after the curse. Sesha, the eldest, leaves his wicked brothers and performs severe penances. Brahma appears and offers a boon. Sesha asks only for a heart devoted to virtue. Brahma tells him to hold up the earth steady, and Sesha goes under the earth and bears it on his head. Brahma gives him Garuda as a helper.

scenes.B01C036S01: Sesha's penances and his talk with Brahma, in which he says he wants to avoid his brothers.
scenes.B01C036S02: Sesha asks only for virtue. Brahma tells him to support the earth, and he slides under it and holds it.
scenes.B01C036S03: Brahma praises Sesha as Dharma himself and gives him Garuda as helper.

shots.B01C036S01H02: Saunaka asks what the snakes did after hearing the curse.
shots.B01C036S01H03: Sesha leaves his mother and brothers and does hard penances in holy places. Brahma finds him thin and asks what he wants.
shots.B01C036S01H04: Sesha says his brothers are wicked and envy Garuda, so he wants to give up his body to escape them.
shots.B01C036S01H05: Brahma says he already provided a remedy for the snakes' danger and offers a boon.
shots.B01C036S02H01: Sesha asks that his heart always delight in virtue and penance.
shots.B01C036S02H02: Brahma praises him and tells him to hold the unsteady earth steady.
shots.B01C036S02H03: Sesha agrees and asks that the earth be placed on his head.
shots.B01C036S02H04: Brahma says the earth will open a passage for him under it.
shots.B01C036S02H05: Sesha enters the opening, goes under the earth, and holds it up with his head.
shots.B01C036S03H01: Brahma calls Sesha the god Dharma for supporting the earth alone.
shots.B01C036S03H02: Sesha, also called Ananta, stays under the earth supporting it. Brahma gives him Garuda to help.
shots.B01C036S03H03: Closing line: the thirty-sixth section ends.

B01C037.summary: Vasuki calls a council of snakes to find a way to cancel their mother's curse. Many plans are put forward: disguising themselves as Brahmana advisers, killing the priests, becoming rain clouds to put out the fire, stealing the sacrificial vessels, fouling the food, demanding fees, kidnapping or biting the king. The kinder snakes object that killing Brahmanas is wrong. Vasuki rejects all of them and says only the help of their father Kasyapa can save them.

scenes.B01C037S01: Vasuki's council: his speech, the many proposals of the snakes to stop Janamejaya's sacrifice, and his rejection of them.

shots.B01C037S01H02: Vasuki, hearing the curse, calls his brothers to a council.
shots.B01C037S01H03: He says no remedy exists for a mother's curse, and even the Lord did not stop it, so they must plan quickly to stop Janamejaya's sacrifice.
shots.B01C037S01H04: The snakes propose plans: pose as Brahmanas to beg the king to stop, become his advisers, kill the priests, send storm clouds, steal the soma vessels, foul the food, demand fees, carry off the king, or simply bite him. The kinder ones object to killing Brahmanas. Vasuki rejects them all and says only Kasyapa's grace can help.
shots.B01C037S01H05: Closing line: the thirty-seventh section ends.

B01C038.summary: The snake Elapatra tells the council that the sacrifice cannot be stopped, but he overheard the gods asking Brahma why he allowed the curse. Brahma said only the wicked snakes would die and foretold that a sage named Jaratkaru would have a son Astika by Vasuki's sister, of the same name, and that Astika would stop the sacrifice. Elapatra advises Vasuki to give his sister to that sage when he comes asking.

scenes.B01C038S01: Elapatra recalls what Brahma told the gods: Astika, son of Jaratkaru and Vasuki's sister, will stop the sacrifice. He advises Vasuki to prepare.

shots.B01C038S01H02: Elapatra says fate cannot be prevented. From his mother's lap he once heard the gods ask Brahma why he let Kadru curse her sons. Brahma replied that only the wicked snakes will die, and a sage Jaratkaru will have a son, Astika, with a wife of the same name, Vasuki's sister, and Astika will stop the sacrifice.
shots.B01C038S01H03: Elapatra urges Vasuki to give his sister as alms to the sage when he comes wandering for a bride.

B01C039.summary: The snakes cheer Elapatra's advice, and Vasuki raises his sister carefully. After the gods and Asuras churn the ocean using Vasuki as the rope, the gods ask Brahma to relieve his fear. Brahma confirms Elapatra's plan. Vasuki orders the snakes to watch Jaratkaru and report when he asks for a wife.

scenes.B01C039S01: Vasuki raises his sister, the gods plead for him to Brahma, Brahma confirms the plan, and Vasuki sets snakes to watch the sage.

shots.B01C039S01H02: The snakes approve Elapatra's counsel and Vasuki starts raising his sister Jaratkaru with great care.
shots.B01C039S01H03: Later, after the ocean churning in which he was the rope, Vasuki goes to Brahma with the gods, who ask Brahma to ease his sorrow.
shots.B01C039S01H04: Brahma says Elapatra's plan stands: only the wicked will die, Jaratkaru is performing penance, and Vasuki should give him his sister at the right time.
shots.B01C039S01H05: Vasuki orders the snakes to watch the sage Jaratkaru and tell him as soon as he asks for a wife.

B01C040.summary: Saunaka asks the meaning of the name Jaratkaru, and Sauti explains it: the sage wore down his large body by penance. Saunaka then asks how Astika was born. Sauti tells how King Parikshit, hunting a wounded deer, found a silent sage and, angered at his silence, hung a dead snake on his shoulder. The sage Samika did not curse him, but his young son Sringin hears of it from a companion, Krisa, and flares up in anger.

scenes.B01C040S01: Saunaka asks about the name Jaratkaru and Astika's birth.
scenes.B01C040S02: Vasuki's waiting, and the tale of Parikshit hunting a deer, meeting the silent sage Samika, and placing a dead snake on his shoulder. Samika's son Sringin comes home.
scenes.B01C040S03: Krisa taunts Sringin about his father's dead snake.

shots.B01C040S01H02: Saunaka asks why the sage was called Jaratkaru.
shots.B01C040S01H03: Sauti says Jara means waste and karu means huge: the sage had a huge body that he wore down with penance. Vasuki's sister had the same name.
shots.B01C040S01H05: Saunaka asks how Astika was born.
shots.B01C040S02H01: Sauti begins to answer according to the scriptures.
shots.B01C040S02H02: Vasuki waits, but the sage Jaratkaru wanders the earth without asking for a wife.
shots.B01C040S02H03: King Parikshit of the Kuru line, a great archer who loves hunting, loses a wounded deer in the forest. Tired and thirsty, he finds a sage in a cow-pen, silent and drinking the froth from calves. The sage does not answer, so the king puts a dead snake on his shoulder with his bow. The sage lets him and does not curse him, and the king goes home regretful.
shots.B01C040S02H04: The sage has a fierce young son, Sringin, who is studying with a teacher.
shots.B01C040S02H05: On his way home, Sringin's companion Krisa teases him about his father, and Sringin flares up.
shots.B01C040S03H01: Krisa mocks Sringin's pride: how can he boast when his own father carries a dead snake on his shoulders?

B01C041.summary: Sringin learns from Krisa what the king did. In rage he curses Parikshit to die within seven nights by Takshaka's bite. He tells his father, the sage Samika, who rebukes him: a king must be forgiven, as kings protect hermits and keep dharma. The king acted from hunger and ignorance of the vow of silence, so the curse was wrong.

scenes.B01C041S01: Sringin hears the story of the king and the snake from Krisa and curses the king.
scenes.B01C041S02: Sringin tells his father, who criticises him and explains the value of kings.

shots.B01C041S01H02: Sringin asks why his father carries a dead snake. Krisa says the king put it there.
shots.B01C041S01H03: Sringin asks what wrong his father did the king.
shots.B01C041S01H04: Krisa tells what happened: the king chased a stag, found Samika silent in his vow, and put the snake on his shoulder.
shots.B01C041S01H05: Furious, Sringin touches water to make a curse.
shots.B01C041S02H01: He curses the king: within seven nights Takshaka will take him to the realm of death.
shots.B01C041S02H02: Sringin goes to his father and tells him. Samika says he is displeased: sages should forgive kings, who protect dharma, sacrifices and rain, and the king acted from hunger and fatigue, not malice.

B01C042.summary: Sringin insists the curse cannot be unsaid. Samika advises peace and sends his pupil Gaurmukha to warn the king. Parikshit is sorry and builds a guarded tower on one pillar. On the seventh day, the physician Kasyapa heads to cure him if bitten. Takshaka, disguised as a Brahmana, meets him and says he will bite the king.

scenes.B01C042S01: Sringin insists on his curse; Samika counsels forgiveness and sends a disciple, Gaurmukha, to warn the king.
scenes.B01C042S02: Gaurmukha's message, the king's regret, his fortified tower, and Kasyapa meeting Takshaka on the road.

shots.B01C042S01H02: Sringin says his words are never false, whether his father likes it or not.
shots.B01C042S01H03: Samika agrees the curse will hold, but advises him to keep calm and forgiving, since anger drains an ascetic's merit, and says he will warn the king.
shots.B01C042S01H04: Samika sends his pupil Gaurmukha to the king with instructions to ask after his welfare and then give the message. Gaurmukha is announced at the palace.
shots.B01C042S01H05: The king honours him, and Gaurmukha repeats Samika's words to the king and ministers.
shots.B01C042S02H01: Gaurmukha says the sage forgave the king but his son cursed him: Takshaka will kill him in seven nights, and nobody can undo his son's curse. He was sent for the king's good.
shots.B01C042S02H02: The king is more distressed by his own act against the sage than by the curse of death.
shots.B01C042S02H03: He sends Gaurmukha away and, with his ministers, builds a mansion on a single pillar, guarded day and night by physicians, medicines and mantra-knowing Brahmanas, and rules from there.
shots.B01C042S02H04: On the seventh day, the Brahmana Kasyapa travels to cure the king after the bite, hoping for wealth and merit. Takshaka, disguised as an old Brahmana, meets him and asks where he is going.
shots.B01C042S02H05: Kasyapa says he is going to cure the king after Takshaka's bite. Takshaka reveals he is Takshaka and says Kasyapa cannot cure him. Kasyapa says he can.

B01C043.summary: Takshaka challenges Kasyapa to revive a banyan tree he burns with a bite. Kasyapa revives it from ashes. Takshaka then asks what Kasyapa wants from the king, offers more wealth, and warns that his skills may fail on a king cursed by a Brahmana. Kasyapa sees that the king's life has run out and takes the payment. Takshaka then sends snakes disguised as ascetics with gifts to the king. The king eats a fruit and finds a small worm in it, jokes that it should be Takshaka and puts it on his neck. It turns into Takshaka and bites him.

scenes.B01C043S01: The tree test: Takshaka burns a banyan with a bite, and Kasyapa revives it.
scenes.B01C043S02: Takshaka buys Kasyapa off, sends disguised snakes with fruit to the king, and bites the king when he puts a worm from the fruit on his neck.

shots.B01C043S01H02: Takshaka challenges Kasyapa to revive a banyan he will burn with a bite.
shots.B01C043S01H04: Takshaka bites the tree, which blazes up, and asks Kasyapa to revive it.
shots.B01C043S01H05: Kasyapa takes the ashes and, by his lore, brings back the sprout, leaves, stem, branches and full tree. Takshaka says reviving a tree is no surprise, offers him whatever he wants from the king, and warns that he may fail on a king whose life has ended.
