shots.B01C043S02H01: Kasyapa says he goes for wealth. Takshaka offers more and tells him not to go.
shots.B01C043S02H02: Kasyapa meditates, sees the king's life has run out, takes the wealth from Takshaka and goes back.
shots.B01C043S02H03: Takshaka enters Hastinapura and hears the king is protected by mantras and medicines.
shots.B01C043S02H04: Takshaka sends snakes disguised as ascetics with fruit, kusa grass and water as gifts to get past the guards.
shots.B01C043S02H05: The king accepts the gifts and eats a fruit with his ministers. A small worm is in it. The king jokes it can be Takshaka and puts it on his neck. It becomes Takshaka, coils around him and bites.

B01C044.summary: The ministers flee as the palace blazes with poison and the king dies. His minor son is crowned Janamejaya. His ministers arrange his marriage to Vapushtama, daughter of the king of Kasi, and the young king lives happily with her.

scenes.B01C044S01: The death of Parikshit, the crowning of Janamejaya, and his marriage to Vapushtama.

shots.B01C044S01H02: The councillors see the king in Takshaka's coils and flee in grief. They see Takshaka flying across the sky like a streak.
shots.B01C044S01H03: The mansion burns with Takshaka's poison and the king falls dead.
shots.B01C044S01H04: The ministers and royal priest perform the last rites and make the boy prince king as Janamejaya. They arrange his marriage to Vapushtama, daughter of Suvarnavarman of Kasi, and he spends his time happily with her.

B01C045.summary: The wandering sage Jaratkaru sees his ancestors hanging head down in a pit, held only by a thread of roots that a rat gnaws. He offers his merit to save them. They explain: they hang because they have no descendants; the thread is Jaratkaru himself, who practises only penance, and the rat is Time. They ask the stranger to tell Jaratkaru to marry and have a son, and ask who he is.

scenes.B01C045S01: Jaratkaru meets his ancestors in the pit, offers his merit, and they explain the rope, the rat and their plight.

shots.B01C045S01H02: Jaratkaru wanders the earth living on air and bathing in holy places. He finds his ancestors hanging head down by a single root thread that a rat is gnawing. He offers any part of his merit to save them.
shots.B01C045S01H03: The ancestors say his penance cannot help them, only a son can. They are Yayavara sages, and the only thread left is their son Jaratkaru, who lives alone in penance. The rope is their line, the eaten threads are lost descendants, the half-eaten root is Jaratkaru and the rat is Time. They ask the stranger to tell Jaratkaru to marry, and ask who he is.

B01C046.summary: Jaratkaru identifies himself as their son and asks what to do. He explains he had vowed to remain celibate but, after seeing them, will marry if he finds a bride of his own name who is offered freely and does not need support. He searches in vain, then calls out in the forest. The snakes watching him tell Vasuki, who brings his sister. Jaratkaru hesitates and asks her name and states he will not support her.

scenes.B01C046S01: Jaratkaru reveals who he is to his ancestors.
scenes.B01C046S02: He agrees to marry on his conditions, searches in vain, calls aloud in the forest, and Vasuki brings his sister.

shots.B01C046S01H02: Jaratkaru is stricken by their words.
shots.B01C046S01H03: Speaking through tears, he says the pitris are his own forefathers.
shots.B01C046S01H04: He asks how to help them and calls himself the sinful son.
shots.B01C046S01H05: He begs to be punished (the sentence continues in the next shot).
shots.B01C046S02H02: The ancestors ask why he has not married.
shots.B01C046S02H03: He says he had planned to remain celibate, but seeing them has changed his mind. He will marry a bride of his own name who is offered freely and whom he won't need to maintain, and her son will save them.
shots.B01C046S02H04: Now old, he cannot find a bride and weeps in the forest, then calls three times for one. The watching snakes tell Vasuki, who brings his sister. Jaratkaru does not accept right away. He asks her name and says he won't maintain her.

B01C047.summary: Vasuki says his sister bears the same name and he will maintain her. Jaratkaru marries her on the condition that he will leave if she ever does anything he dislikes. She conceives. One evening he sleeps with his head in her lap and sunset nears. Fearing the loss of his evening prayers, she wakes him. He is furious at the insult, says he will leave, and ignores her pleas, but tells her the child in her womb will be a great sage. He departs for more penance.

scenes.B01C047S01: Vasuki's offer, the marriage and its agreement, the conception, and the sunset dilemma while the sage sleeps.
scenes.B01C047S02: She wakes him, he is offended and leaves, with a prophecy about the son.

shots.B01C047S01H02: Vasuki says the bride has the same name, is his sister and he will maintain her. Jaratkaru agrees to marry, on the condition that she never does anything he dislikes.
shots.B01C047S01H03: They marry with proper rites and he lives in a chamber provided by Vasuki, repeating his condition: if she does anything against his wishes, he will leave.
shots.B01C047S01H04: She accepts, serves him with great care, and soon conceives a child as bright as fire.
shots.B01C047S01H05: One evening the sage sleeps with his head on her lap and the sun is about to set. She worries: if she wakes him he will be angry; if she lets the twilight pass he will lose his religious merit.
shots.B01C047S02H01: She decides to wake him gently and tells him it is time for the evening prayer.
shots.B01C047S02H02: He is angry and says she has insulted him, and that he will leave. She explains she woke him only to protect his merit.
shots.B01C047S02H03: He says he never lies, so he must go, and tells her to inform her brother and not to grieve.
shots.B01C047S02H04: She pleads with joined hands: the offspring her relatives need has not yet come, and she has done nothing wrong.
shots.B01C047S02H05: He says the child in her womb is a great Vedic sage like fire.
shots.B01C047S03H01: With that, Jaratkaru leaves to take up severe penance again.

B01C048.summary: Jaratkaru's wife tells Vasuki what happened. He asks about the child because the snakes' hopes rest on it. She says her husband told her that a son would be born. Vasuki is relieved and honours her. The boy is born, studies the Vedas with Chyavana, and is named Astika ("there is") for his father's words before leaving.

scenes.B01C048S01: She tells her brother about the sage's departure, and Vasuki is reassured by his words.
scenes.B01C048S02: The birth and upbringing of Astika.

shots.B01C048S01H02: She goes to her brother and tells him everything. Vasuki, even more distressed, asks her about the child.
shots.B01C048S01H03: Vasuki says the whole purpose of the marriage was a son who would save the snakes, and asks whether she conceived.
shots.B01C048S01H04: She says her husband told her, 'There is,' that a son would be born, and he never lies. She asks Vasuki to cast off his sorrow.
shots.B01C048S01H05: Vasuki accepts and honours her with gifts. The child begins to grow, bright as the waxing moon.
shots.B01C048S02H01: A son is born and raised in Vasuki's house. He studies with Chyavana and is known as Astika, from his father's word 'there is' when he was still in the womb. He grows up a delight to the snakes.

B01C049.summary: Saunaka asks to hear again what Janamejaya asked his ministers about his father. Janamejaya asks how his father died. The ministers praise Parikshit as a just king who protected all classes and ruled for sixty years. They then tell how, hunting as an old man, he put a dead snake on a silent sage's shoulders.

scenes.B01C049S01: Saunaka's request. Janamejaya's question to his ministers and their account of Parikshit's reign.
scenes.B01C049S02: Janamejaya asks for the full story of his father's death. The ministers describe the hunt and the dead snake.

shots.B01C049S01H02: Saunaka asks Sauti to tell again what Janamejaya asked his ministers.
shots.B01C049S01H04: Janamejaya asks his ministers to tell all that happened to his father and says he will act if it benefits the world.
shots.B01C049S01H05: The minister describes Parikshit as a virtuous king: son of Abhimanyu, born when the Kuru line was nearly extinct, a pupil of Saradwat, protector of the poor and the widows and of all four orders, who ruled sixty years before dying, after which Janamejaya was crowned as a child.
shots.B01C049S02H01: Janamejaya says no king of his line was disliked and asks how his father died.
shots.B01C049S02H02: The ministers agree to tell exactly what happened.
shots.B01C049S02H03: The ministers say Parikshit, an old man fond of hunting, pursued a wounded deer, grew tired and hungry, found a Rishi silent in a vow, and angrily put a dead snake on his shoulders. The Rishi did not respond.

B01C050.summary: The ministers report how the sage Utanka was insulted by King Janamejaya's father, and how the sage's son Sringin cursed the king to die by Takshaka's poison. Takshaka kills the king in his mansion after Kasyapa, sent to save him, is paid off and turns back. Janamejaya hears the whole story from his ministers and resolves to avenge his father, which sets up the snake-sacrifice.

scenes.B01C050S01: The ministers tell how the sage was insulted, how his son Sringin cursed the king, and how Takshaka killed the king after Kasyapa was paid off.
scenes.B01C050S02: Janamejaya asks his ministers for every detail, grieves, and declares his resolve to avenge his father on Takshaka.

shots.B01C050S01H02: The ministers resume: the king returns to his capital after placing a dead snake on the sage's shoulders, and the sage's son Sringin hears of the insult to his father.
shots.B01C050S01H03: Sringin curses the king's father, saying Takshaka will burn him with poison within seven nights, and the sage sends his disciple Gaurmukha to warn the king.
shots.B01C050S01H04: Takshaka bites a banyan tree and burns it to ashes, then offers Kasyapa wealth to turn back, and Kasyapa accepts and goes home.
shots.B01C050S01H05: Takshaka, in disguise, burns the king in his mansion, and the ministers ask Janamejaya to decide what follows, since the sage Utanka was insulted.
shots.B01C050S02H01: Janamejaya asks when the ministers learned these events and says he wants to know what passed in the forest.
shots.B01C050S02H02: The ministers describe a man who climbed a dry tree, was burned with it, and was revived by a Brahmana's power, and who then reported the exchange between Takshaka and Kasyapa.
shots.B01C050S02H03: Janamejaya, having heard all this, is overcome with grief, weeps, and breathes heavily.
shots.B01C050S02H04: Janamejaya declares his resolve to avenge his father on Takshaka, whom he blames for the death and for the insult to the sage.

B01C051.summary: Janamejaya, having heard that Takshaka killed his father, asks his priests for a way to burn the snake and his kin. The chief priest names the snake-sacrifice, a rite said to be known from the Puranas and possible only for the king to perform. Preparations begin with the sacrificial platform, but a builder warns that a Brahmana will obstruct the rite, so the king orders his gatekeepers to admit no one.

scenes.B01C051S01: Janamejaya decides on a snake-sacrifice, the priests explain it, the platform is built, and a builder warns of obstruction, so the king bars entry to all.

shots.B01C051S01H02: The ministers approve, and Janamejaya resolves on a snake-sacrifice, asking his priests how to burn Takshaka and his kin.
shots.B01C051S01H03: The chief priest says the gods devised a snake-sacrifice, known from the Puranas, that only the king can perform.
shots.B01C051S01H04: The king prepares for the rite, the priests measure the platform, and a Suta builder warns that a Brahmana will obstruct the sacrifice, so the king orders the gatekeepers to admit no one.

B01C052.summary: The snake-sacrifice begins with priests in black garments pouring butter into the fire while calling out the names of the snakes. Snakes of every kind, young and old, fall into the flames by the hundreds of thousands. The scene shows the terrible effect of the rite on the snake race.

scenes.B01C052S01: The priests start the sacrifice, and countless snakes of every kind fall into the fire.

shots.B01C052S01H02: The priests pour butter into the fire while naming the snakes, and snakes of all colours and sizes fall into the flames in great numbers.

B01C053.summary: Saunaka asks who served as priests and assembly members at the snake-sacrifice, and Sauti lists the famous sages. As the rite goes on, snakes keep falling into the fire, and Takshaka flees to Indra, who promises to protect him. Vasuki, seeing his family dwindling, sends for his sister so that her son Astika can stop the sacrifice.

scenes.B01C053S01: Saunaka asks about the priests, Sauti names them, and the snakes continue to fall into the fire while Takshaka seeks Indra's protection.
scenes.B01C053S02: Vasuki, grieving over the destruction of his race, calls his sister and asks her to send her son Astika to stop the sacrifice.

shots.B01C053S01H02: Saunaka asks which great sages served as priests and assembly members at the snake-sacrifice.
shots.B01C053S01H03: Sauti names the priests and sages, including Chandabhargava as Hotri, Kautsa as Udgatri, and Vyasa with his disciples as members.
shots.B01C053S01H04: Snakes continue to fall into the fire, their fat flows like rivers, and the air fills with stench and cries.
shots.B01C053S01H05: Takshaka goes to Indra's palace, confesses his fault, and Indra promises that Takshaka has nothing to fear from the sacrifice.
shots.B01C053S02H01: Vasuki, seeing his family reduced to a few, laments his fate and asks his sister to send her son Astika to end the sacrifice.

B01C054.summary: Jaratkaru tells her son Astika why she was given to his father: Kadru cursed her sons to burn in Janamejaya's sacrifice, and Brahman foretold that a Brahmana born of Jaratkaru would free the snakes. Astika promises Vasuki he will stop the sacrifice. He then enters the sacrificial compound and praises the king and the priests.

scenes.B01C054S01: Jaratkaru tells Astika that Kadru cursed the snakes to burn in the sacrifice, and that the gods asked Brahman how to undo the curse.
scenes.B01C054S02: Brahman says a Brahmana born of Jaratkaru will save the snakes, Jaratkaru reveals her son's role, and Astika promises to stop the sacrifice.
scenes.B01C054S03: Astika gets past the doorkeepers and enters the sacrificial compound, where he honours the king, priests, and sacred fire.

shots.B01C054S01H02: Jaratkaru calls her son and, on Vasuki's instruction, tells him that the time has come for the purpose for which she was given to his father.
shots.B01C054S01H03: Astika asks why his mother was given to his father by his uncle, and asks her to explain it truly.
shots.B01C054S01H04: Jaratkaru explains that Kadru cursed her sons to burn in Janamejaya's sacrifice, after they refused to lie about the horse Uchchaihsravas in a wager.
shots.B01C054S01H05: The gods, led by Vasuki, ask Brahman how the curse can be made ineffective.
shots.B01C054S02H01: Brahman replies that Jaratkaru will marry a wife also named Jaratkaru, and the Brahmana born of her will relieve the snakes.
shots.B01C054S02H02: Jaratkaru reminds her son that Vasuki gave her to his father for this purpose, and asks what he thinks.
shots.B01C054S02H03: Astika agrees and promises Vasuki that he will free him from the curse.
shots.B01C054S02H04: Vasuki says his head swims and his heart breaks under the curse.
shots.B01C054S02H05: Astika tells Vasuki to stop grieving, promising to extinguish the punishment of the sacrifice.
shots.B01C054S03H01: Astika goes to the sacrifice, is refused by the doorkeepers, wins them over, enters, and honours the king, the priests, and the fire.

B01C055.summary: Astika praises Janamejaya's sacrifice by comparing it with the great sacrifices of gods, sages and kings, and he praises the priests and Vyasa. The praise is the opening of his plea to stop the sacrifice. Janamejaya, noticing omens around him, turns to speak to the assembly.

scenes.B01C055S01: Astika praises the sacrifice and its priests with a long string of comparisons, and the king, noticing signs around him, addresses them.

shots.B01C055S01H02: Astika praises the king's sacrifice by comparing it with the rites of gods, sages and kings, and praises the priests and Vyasa with many comparisons.
shots.B01C055S01H03: Sauti says Astika has pleased the king, the priests and the sacred fire, and that the king, seeing the omens, speaks to them.

B01C056.summary: Janamejaya offers Astika a boon, but the priests say Takshaka has not yet come into the sacrifice. The Ritwiks report that Takshaka is hiding with Indra, and when Indra is forced to release him, Takshaka is drawn toward the fire. At that moment Astika asks that the sacrifice end, and the king, unwilling at first, is urged by the assembly to grant the request.

scenes.B01C056S01: Janamejaya offers Astika a boon, but the Sadasyas and the Hotri say Takshaka has not yet arrived, and the king urges the priests to finish the rite.
scenes.B01C056S02: The priests and the Suta Lohitaksha say Takshaka is hiding with Indra, and the Hotri's libations force Indra to release him toward the fire.
scenes.B01C056S03: Takshaka is about to fall into the fire when Astika asks that the sacrifice end, and the king offers gold and cattle instead.
scenes.B01C056S04: Astika refuses all gifts and asks only for the end of the sacrifice, and the assembly presses the king to grant it.

shots.B01C056S01H02: Janamejaya says the boy speaks like a wise old man and offers him a boon.
shots.B01C056S01H03: The Sadasyas say a Brahmana deserves respect and may have his wish, but only after Takshaka comes.
shots.B01C056S01H04: The king tells Astika to ask for a boon, but the Hotri objects that Takshaka has not yet come into the sacrifice.
shots.B01C056S01H05: Janamejaya urges the priests to complete the sacrifice and bring Takshaka, whom he calls his enemy.
shots.B01C056S02H01: The Ritwiks say the scriptures and the fire show that Takshaka is staying in Indra's abode, afraid.
shots.B01C056S02H02: The Suta Lohitaksha, learned in the Puranas, had said this before.
shots.B01C056S02H03: Asked again, Lohitaksha explains that Indra granted Takshaka a boon: hiding with Indra means Agni cannot burn him.
shots.B01C056S02H04: Indra arrives in his car with the gods, and Takshaka hides in his garment, so the king orders that Takshaka be cast into the fire with Indra.
shots.B01C056S02H05: The Hotri names Takshaka in his libations, Indra releases him and leaves, and the mantras draw Takshaka near the flames.
shots.B01C056S03H01: The Ritwiks tell the king the sacrifice is going well and that he should grant a boon to the Brahmana.
shots.B01C056S03H02: Janamejaya promises to grant any boon Astika asks for, even one that seems impossible.
shots.B01C056S03H03: The Ritwiks report that Takshaka, disabled by the mantras, is falling from the sky toward the fire.
shots.B01C056S03H04: As Takshaka falls, Astika asks that the sacrifice end and that no more snakes burn in the fire.
shots.B01C056S03H05: Janamejaya, sorry, offers gold, silver, cattle and other wealth, but not an end to the sacrifice.
shots.B01C056S04H01: Astika refuses wealth and asks that the sacrifice end so his maternal relatives can be saved.
shots.B01C056S04H02: The king repeatedly offers Astika another boon, Astika holds to his request, and the Sadasyas tell the king to grant it.

B01C057.summary: Saunaka asks for the names of the snakes burned in the sacrifice, and Sauti says the number is too great to count. He names the chief snakes of several families, including the lines of Vasuki, Takshaka, Airavata, Kauravya and Dhritarashtra. He adds that their sons and grandsons were burned too, which shows how vast the destruction was.

scenes.B01C057S01: Sauti names the principal snakes from several families, and says the rest are too many to count, all burned in the fire.
scenes.B01C057S02: Sauti adds that many other huge and powerful snakes were burned in the great sacrifice.

shots.B01C057S01H02: Saunaka asks for the names of all the snakes that fell into the sacrificial fire.
shots.B01C057S01H03: Sauti says the snakes are too many to count, and names the chief snakes of Vasuki's race, who fell into the fire like libations of butter.
shots.B01C057S01H04: Sauti names more chief snakes of the lines of Takshaka, Airavata, Kauravya and Dhritarashtra, all of whom fell into the fire.
shots.B01C057S01H05: Sauti says the sons and grandsons of these snakes were burned too, by the thousands.
shots.B01C057S02H01: Many other huge, swift snakes, able to take any shape and strength, were burned in the great sacrifice.

B01C058.summary: Janamejaya is puzzled that Takshaka still hangs in the air, though Astika had told him to stay. The king grants Astika's boon, ends the sacrifice, rewards the priests and Lohitaksha, and sends Astika home. The grateful snakes promise protection to anyone who recalls Astika's deed, and Astika later goes to heaven. Sauti closes by saying the recital banishes fear of snakes.

scenes.B01C058S01: The king grants Astika's boon, ends the sacrifice, rewards the priests, and sends Astika home to his family.
scenes.B01C058S02: The snakes thank Astika and promise safety to anyone who remembers his deed, and Astika later goes to heaven.
scenes.B01C058S03: Sauti closes the story, saying the recital is a charm against fear of snakes, and that he passes on Pramati's tale to Ruru.

shots.B01C058S01H02: Sauti tells how Takshaka hung in mid-air just as the king was about to grant Astika's boon, and how this puzzled Janamejaya.
shots.B01C058S01H03: Saunaka asks whether the priests' mantras failed, since Takshaka did not fall into the fire.
shots.B01C058S01H04: Sauti explains that Astika had three times told the falling Takshaka to stay, and the snake remained in the sky.
shots.B01C058S01H05: The king ends the sacrifice, rewards the priests and Lohitaksha, and sends Astika home, where he tells his uncle and mother what happened.
shots.B01C058S02H01: The pleased snakes, now saved, offer Astika a boon.
shots.B01C058S02H02: Astika asks that anyone who reads the account of his deed be free from fear of snakes, and the snakes agree and add their own protective words.
shots.B01C058S02H03: Gratified, the great Brahmana Astika prepares to leave.
shots.B01C058S02H04: Astika ascends to heaven when his time comes, leaving sons and grandsons behind.
shots.B01C058S02H05: Sauti says that this is the account of Astika exactly as it happened.
shots.B01C058S03H01: A closing line says that reciting this history removes all fear of snakes.
shots.B01C058S03H02: Sauti says he has recited the whole history of Astika as Pramati once told it to his son Ruru, and asks Saunaka to be satisfied.

B01C059.summary: Saunaka asks Sauti to recite the history composed by Vyasa, which Vyasa had recited at Janamejaya's sacrifice. Sauti says the Brahmanas spoke on many Vedic subjects in the intervals, but Vyasa recited the great Bharata. Sauti agrees to tell the Mahabharata from its beginning. This short chapter is the frame that opens the main epic.

scenes.B01C059S01: Saunaka asks for Vyasa's history, Sauti explains what Vyasa recited, and Sauti agrees to tell the Mahabharata from the start.

shots.B01C059S01H02: Saunaka thanks Sauti and asks him to recite the history composed by Vyasa, along with the stories told at the sacrifice.
shots.B01C059S01H03: Sauti says the Brahmanas spoke on many Vedic topics, but Vyasa recited the great Bharata.
shots.B01C059S01H04: Saunaka asks to hear the Mahabharata, which Vyasa recited at Janamejaya's request after the sacrifice, and says he is not satisfied yet.
shots.B01C059S01H05: Sauti agrees to recite the Mahabharata from its beginning and says he enjoys doing so.

B01C060.summary: Vyasa, the grandfather of the Pandavas, arrives at Janamejaya's sacrifice and is welcomed with honour. Janamejaya asks him why the Kurus and Pandavas fought their great war. Vyasa tells his disciple Vaisampayana to recite the whole history to the king and the assembly.

scenes.B01C060S01: Vyasa is introduced and welcomed with honour, and Janamejaya asks him about the Kurus, the Pandavas, and the cause of their war.
scenes.B01C060S02: At Vyasa's command, Vaisampayana begins the full recital of the history to the king and the assembly.

shots.B01C060S01H02: Vyasa, born of Kali to Parasara, is praised for his learning, his division of the Vedas, and his begetting of Pandu, Dhritarashtra and Vidura.
shots.B01C060S01H03: Vyasa enters the sacrificial pavilion, where Janamejaya greets him, offers him a golden seat and worship, and asks after his welfare.
shots.B01C060S01H04: Janamejaya asks Vyasa to tell him the history of the Kurus and Pandavas, and why the disunion and great battle happened.
shots.B01C060S01H05: Vyasa tells his disciple Vaisampayana to recount to the king the discord between the Kurus and Pandavas as he heard it.
shots.B01C060S02H01: Vaisampayana recites the whole history to the king, the Sadasyas and the chieftains, covering the hostility and destruction of the two houses.

B01C061.summary: Vaisampayana begins the history by explaining the quarrel, which started when Duryodhana plotted against the Pandavas after their father's death, using poison, drowning and a lac house. The Pandavas escape, win Draupadi, and settle Khandavaprastha, but a dice game with Duryodhana sends them into exile. The chapter ends with the great war, in which the Kauravas lose their kingdom and Duryodhana is slain.

scenes.B01C061S01: Vaisampayana explains why the Pandavas were driven out, with Duryodhana's plots: poison, drowning, and a lac house at Varanavata that Vidura had warned them about.
scenes.B01C061S02: The Pandavas escape the lac house, win Draupadi, settle Khandavaprastha, and are sent into exile after a dice game, and then the war ends the rivalry.

shots.B01C061S01H02: Vaisampayana bows to his preceptor and says he will recite what he heard from Vyasa.
shots.B01C061S01H03: Vaisampayana says he will explain why the disunion between the Kurus and Pandavas came about, and why the dice game led to exile.
shots.B01C061S01H04: After their father's death the Pandavas return home and grow skilled in archery, which makes Duryodhana and his allies jealous; they try poison and drowning against Bhima, and Vidura protects them.
shots.B01C061S01H05: Duryodhana and his council have a house of lac built, and Dhritarashtra sends the Pandavas to Varanavata, where Vidura warns them of the danger.
shots.B01C061S02H01: The Pandavas escape the lac house, slay Purochana, meet Hidimba and Ghatotkacha, kill the Rakshasa Vaka, win Draupadi, and receive Khandavaprastha, where they extend their power over the lands.
shots.B01C061S02H02: Arjuna is exiled to the forest, marries Subhadra, helps burn the Khandava forest, and receives Gandiva and a chariot; Duryodhana then wins the kingdom by dice and sends the Pandavas into exile for thirteen years.
shots.B01C061S02H03: When the Pandavas return and are refused their kingdom, war breaks out, the Kshatriyas are destroyed, Duryodhana is slain, and the Pandavas regain their ruined kingdom.
shots.B01C061S02H04: Closing line: this is the history of the Pandavas and the disunion that cost the Kurus their kingdom.

B01C062.summary: Janamejaya asks for the full story rather than a summary, and wants to know why the Pandavas endured the Kurus' wrongs without fighting back. Vaisampayana agrees, and before starting he praises the Bharata at length: its size, the merit it brings to those who recite or hear it, and Vyasa's purpose in composing it. He says the work also covers gods, sages and kings, so it is the place to learn about every subject worth knowing.

scenes.B01C062S01: Janamejaya asks for the full recital, and Vaisampayana agrees and describes the Mahabharata's size, merits, author's purpose, and range of subjects.

shots.B01C062S01H02: Janamejaya asks for the full story, not a short version, and wants to know why the Pandavas bore their persecution and why Bhima and Draupadi held back.
shots.B01C062S01H03: Vaisampayana agrees to recite the whole work, calls it a vast composition of about a hundred thousand verses, and lists the benefits of reading or hearing it.
shots.B01C062S01H04: Vaisampayana says Vyasa composed the work to honour the Pandavas and other Kshatriyas, and describes the merit gained by having it recited to Brahmanas.
shots.B01C062S01H05: Vaisampayana lists the subjects the work covers, including gods, sages, Krishna, Shiva and Kartikeya, and claims it is a mine of virtue and a complete guide to every topic of life.

B01C063.summary: Vaisampayana traces the origins of the great families, starting with King Vasu, whose seed, carried by a hawk, is swallowed by a fish and produces the twins Matsya and Satyavati. Satyavati later bears Vyasa to the sage Parasara, and Vyasa arranges the Vedas and teaches this history to his disciples. The chapter then lists the births of the heroes of both sides, including Bhishma, Vidura, the Pandavas, the Kauravas and their allies, who meet in the great battle.

scenes.B01C063S01: Indra blesses King Uparichara Vasu with a crystal car, a garland and a pole, and Vasu starts a festival in Indra's honour.
scenes.B01C063S02: Vasu's sons found kingdoms, his children are born from a river and a mountain, and Vasu sends his seed to his wife Girika through a hawk.
scenes.B01C063S03: The hawk drops the seed, a fish swallows it, and from the fish come the twins Matsya and Satyavati, the girl later courted by the sage Parasara.
scenes.B01C063S04: Satyavati, freed from her fishy smell, bears Vyasa, who arranges the Vedas, and the text lists the births of Bhishma, Vidura, the Pandavas, the Kauravas and their allies.
scenes.B01C063S05: The text says hundreds of thousands of kings fought in the great battle, and it names only the principal ones.

shots.B01C063S01H02: Vaisampayana introduces King Uparichara Vasu, a devoted and hunting-loving king of the Paurava line, who conquers Chedi and then takes up severe austerities.
shots.B01C063S01H03: The gods, led by Indra, come to Vasu and ask him to protect virtue, and Indra gives him a crystal car and a garland of lotuses that protects him in battle.
shots.B01C063S01H04: Indra gives Vasu a bamboo pole, and after a year Vasu plants it to worship Indra, starting a custom that other kings follow.
shots.B01C063S01H05: Indra blesses Vasu for his festival, and Vasu rules Chedi virtuously for a long time.
shots.B01C063S02H01: Vasu installs his five sons as governors of various provinces.
shots.B01C063S02H02: The text names the sons, including Vrihadratha in Magadha, who is also called Maharatha.
shots.B01C063S02H03: The five sons found kingdoms and towns named after themselves, which last for ages.
shots.B01C063S02H04: Riding his crystal car, Vasu is called Uparichara, and a river is freed from the mountain Kolahala, producing twin children who are given to Vasu.
shots.B01C063S02H05: Vasu's wife Girika is ready after her monthly course, but the Pitris ask Vasu to hunt deer for their rite, so he goes into a spring forest thinking of her, and a hawk is sent with his seed for her.
shots.B01C063S03H01: The hawk is attacked by another hawk, the seed falls into the Yamuna, and an Apsara turned into a fish swallows it, and the fish later yields a boy and a girl.
shots.B01C063S03H02: The Apsara is freed from her curse after giving birth, and rises back to her celestial form.
shots.B01C063S03H03: The king gives the girl to the fishermen, and she is named Satyavati, living with the fishermen and ferrying a boat on the Yamuna.
shots.B01C063S03H04: The sage Parasara sees Satyavati and asks her to accept his embraces, but she points out that the Rishis on both banks are watching.
shots.B01C063S03H05: Parasara creates a fog to hide them, Satyavati asks that her virginity be kept, and he grants her a boon that her body will smell sweet.
shots.B01C063S04H01: After the boon, Satyavati's season comes, she accepts Parasara, and she is known as Gandhavati and Yojanagandha for her scent.
shots.B01C063S04H02: Satyavati gives birth on an island in the Yamuna to a son, who sets out for asceticism and promises to appear when she calls.
shots.B01C063S04H03: The son is named Dwaipayana for being island-born, and then Vyasa for arranging the Vedas, and he teaches the Vedas, with the Mahabharata as the fifth, to his disciples.
shots.B01C063S04H04: Bhishma is born of Ganga and Santanu, and a sage cursed by Dharma as a thief is reborn as Vidura, while Kunti's son by Surya is born with armour and earrings, and Vishnu is born to Devaki and Vasudeva.
shots.B01C063S04H05: The births of Satyaki, Kritavarma, Drona, Kripa, Dhrishtadyumna, Draupadi, Sakuni, Duryodhana, the Pandavas, and Abhimanyu are listed, along with the sons of Draupadi and Ghatotkacha.
shots.B01C063S05H01: The text says that hundreds of thousands of kings fought in the great battle, too many to name, so only the principal ones are listed.

B01C064.summary: Janamejaya asks why these great warriors were born on earth. Vaisampayana explains that after Parasurama cleared the earth of Kshatriyas, a golden age returned, but then Asuras reborn as proud kings oppressed the world. The earth appealed to Brahman, who sent the gods down to be born on earth, and Narayana agreed to descend as well.

scenes.B01C064S01: Vaisampayana says that the Kshatriyas were restored after Parasurama, the earth prospered, and then Asuras were reborn as kings who oppressed the world, so the earth went to Brahman for help.
scenes.B01C064S02: Brahman tells the gods to be born on earth, and Indra goes to Narayana, who agrees to be incarnated.

shots.B01C064S01H02: Janamejaya asks for a detailed account of the named and unnamed kings, and of the purpose for which these great warriors were born.
shots.B01C064S01H03: Vaisampayana says Parasurama cleared the Kshatriyas twenty-one times, and Kshatriya women then had children by Brahmanas, so the Kshatriyas were restored and the four orders and the world thrived in a golden age.
shots.B01C064S01H04: The Asuras, driven out of heaven by the gods, are reborn on earth as proud kings and creatures, and they oppress Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and sages.
shots.B01C064S01H05: The earth, weighed down by the Asuras, goes to Brahman for protection, and Brahman says he will appoint the dwellers of heaven to help her.
shots.B01C064S02H01: Brahman bids the earth farewell and tells the gods to be born on earth to ease her burden and fight the Asuras there.
shots.B01C064S02H02: Indra goes to Narayana in Vaikuntha and asks him to be incarnated, and Narayana agrees.

B01C065.summary: Vaisampayana describes the births of gods and other beings, starting with Brahman's sons, Kasyapa, and the daughters of Daksha who became the mothers of most creatures. He names the Adityas, the sons of Diti and Danu who became Asuras, the children of Sinhika, Krodha, Kala, Vinata and Kadru, including Garuda and the Nagas, and the Gandharvas and Apsaras. He ends by saying that reading this account brings long life, progeny and fame.

scenes.B01C065S01: Vaisampayana says the gods were reborn among royal and Brahmarshi families and slew the Danavas and Rakshasas, then begins the genealogy that Janamejaya requested.
scenes.B01C065S02: He recites the lines of Kasyapa's children and says that the account brings long life, progeny and fame to those who read it.

shots.B01C065S01H02: Indra consults Narayana, returns to heaven, and the gods are reborn among Brahmarshis and royal sages to destroy the Danavas, Rakshasas, Gandharvas and Snakes.
shots.B01C065S01H04: Janamejaya asks for the births of the gods, Danavas, Gandharvas, Apsaras, men, Yakshas and Rakshasas, from the beginning.
shots.B01C065S01H05: Vaisampayana starts the genealogy: Brahman's sons, Kasyapa, Daksha's thirteen daughters, the twelve Adityas, Hiranyakasipu and Prahlada of the Daityas, the forty sons of Danu, and the children of Sinhika, Krodha, Kala and Sukra.
shots.B01C065S02H01: Vaisampayana says the descendants of these beings are too many to count, and he has recited only what is known from the Purana.
shots.B01C065S02H02: He names the sons of Vinata, including Garuda and Aruna, the sons of Kadru, including Vasuki and Takshaka, and the lines of Muni, Pradha, and Kapila, which include Gandharvas, Apsaras and kine.
shots.B01C065S02H03: He closes the list of creatures, saying that this account is sacred and that it should be heard and recited in a proper frame of mind.
shots.B01C065S02H04: He promises that anyone who reads this account before gods and Brahmanas gains progeny, good fortune, fame and excellent worlds.

B01C066.summary: Vaisampayana continues the genealogy of creation, naming Brahman's sons, the Rudras, the Vasus, Dharma's sons, and Daksha's daughters, who were married to Dharma, Soma and Kasyapa. He traces the Bhrigu line through Sukra, Chyavana, Aurva and Parasurama, and lists the animals and beings born of Tamra, Krodha, Surabhi and others. The chapter closes by saying that hearing this genealogy cleanses sins and brings knowledge.

scenes.B01C066S01: Vaisampayana names Brahman's sons and their lines, including the Rudras, Daksha's daughters, the Vasus, Dharma's sons, and the Adityas, with Kasyapa as father of gods and Asuras.
scenes.B01C066S02: He traces the Bhrigu descendants, including Sukra, Chyavana, Aurva and Parasurama, and lists the animals and beings born of Tamra, Krodha, Surabhi and others.

shots.B01C066S01H02: Vaisampayana names Brahman's six great Rishis, the eleven Rudras, and the lines of Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu, then describes how Daksha's daughters were given to Dharma, Soma and Kasyapa.
shots.B01C066S01H03: He names the eight Vasus and their sons and descendants, including Kartikeya, and Viswakarman, the craftsman and maker of the gods' cars.
shots.B01C066S01H04: Dharma comes out of Brahman's breast in human form, and his three sons, Sama, Kama and Harsha, support the worlds.
shots.B01C066S01H05: Kasyapa, son of Marichi, is the father of gods and Asuras, and the twelve Adityas are led by Indra, with Vishnu the youngest.
shots.B01C066S02H01: He lists the thirty-three gods and the groups they form, including the Rudras, Maruts, Vasus and Adityas.
shots.B01C066S02H02: He says that reciting this list of the gods' groups washes men of all sins.
shots.B01C066S02H03: He traces Bhrigu's line: Sukra, Chyavana, Aurva, Richika, Jamadagni, and Parasurama, the slayer of Kshatriyas, and Aurva's hundred sons.
shots.B01C066S02H04: He lists the offspring of Brahman's other children, of Lakshmi, Divi, Adharma, Tamra's daughters, Krodha's daughters, Surabhi, Surasa, Kadru, and Vinata, covering birds, deer, elephants, cattle, horses and Nagas.

B01C067.summary: Vaisampayana lists the earthly rebirths of gods, Asuras and other beings, naming kings such as Jarasandha, Sisupala and Salya, and the heroes of the story, including Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Sakuni, Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura. He then names the hundred sons of Dhritarashtra and their sister, and describes the Pandavas and Draupadi as portions of gods and goddesses, with Soma's prophecy about Abhimanyu. The chapter closes with the birth of Karna to Kunti and Surya and the births of the Yadu family, so the cast of the story is set.

scenes.B01C067S01: Vaisampayana names the earthly rebirths of Asuras, Danavas and other beings, from kings like Jarasandha to heroes like Bhishma, Drona and Duryodhana, and Janamejaya asks for the sons of Dhritarashtra.
scenes.B01C067S02: Vaisampayana lists Dhritarashtra's children, then explains how the Pandavas, Draupadi, Abhimanyu and Karna were born as portions of gods and other beings.

shots.B01C067S01H02: Janamejaya asks for the births among men of gods, Danavas, Gandharvas, Rakshasas, animals, snakes and birds, and for their deeds after they took human form.
shots.B01C067S01H03: Vaisampayana names Asuras reborn as kings, such as Viprachitti as Jarasandha and Hiranyakasipu as Sisupala, along with the Kaleya brothers and the Krodhavasa line.
shots.B01C067S01H04: He names the rebirths of Kansa, Devaka, Drona, Ashwatthama, Bhishma, Kripa, Sakuni, Satyaki, Drupada, Virata, Dhritarashtra, Pandu, Vidura and Duryodhana, along with their portions of divine beings.
shots.B01C067S01H05: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana to name Dhritarashtra's sons in the order of their birth.
shots.B01C067S02H01: Vaisampayana lists the hundred sons of Dhritarashtra, Duhsala the daughter, and Yuyutsu born of a Vaisya wife, and says all were skilled warriors and learned men.
shots.B01C067S02H02: The Pandavas are portions of Dharma, Vayu, Indra and the Aswins, and Abhimanyu is the son of Soma, who had asked the gods to let his son go to earth for a limited time.
shots.B01C067S02H03: Dhrishtadyumna is a portion of Agni, Sikhandin was a Rakshasa, and Draupadi's five sons are portions of the Viswas.
shots.B01C067S02H04: Pritha, after receiving a mantra from Durvasa, has Surya's son Karna, who is adopted by Radha's husband and later gives his armour to Indra, and the account then gives the divine births of Krishna and Balarama, Rukmini and Draupadi.
shots.B01C067S02H05: Closing: the account of these incarnations brings wealth, fame and long life to those who hear it, and gives wisdom about creation and destruction.

B01C068.summary: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana to tell the Kuru dynasty from its beginning. Vaisampayana starts with King Dushmanta, founder of the Paurava line, who rules the four quarters of the earth. His reign is described as prosperous and virtuous, with no fear of theft, famine or disease.

scenes.B01C068S01: Janamejaya asks for the Kuru line from its beginning, and Vaisampayana starts with King Dushmanta and describes his prosperous, virtuous reign.

shots.B01C068S01H02: Janamejaya asks to hear the dynasty of the Kurus from the very beginning, in front of the Rishis.
shots.B01C068S01H03: Vaisampayana says Dushmanta founded the Paurava line and ruled the earth bounded by the four seas, and even the lands of the Mlechchhas.
shots.B01C068S01H04: Under Dushmanta there were no mixed castes or sinful men, no fear of theft, famine or disease, and the rains came on time, and the king was strong, skilled in arms, and loved by his people.

B01C069.summary: Janamejaya asks for the story of Bharata's birth, Sakuntala's origin, and how Dushmanta won her. Vaisampayana describes Dushmanta setting out for the forest with a great army, cheered by the women of the city. His hunt there drives away the animals, and the forest is left empty.

scenes.B01C069S01: Dushmanta marches into the forest with a great army and hunts until the forest is emptied of its animals.

shots.B01C069S01H02: Janamejaya asks to hear about Bharata's birth, Sakuntala's origin, and how Dushmanta won her.
shots.B01C069S01H03: Dushmanta sets out with a four-fold army, the women of the city praise and bless him, and the citizens follow him to the edge of the forest.
shots.B01C069S01H04: Dushmanta hunts in the forest, killing and wounding tigers and other beasts with bow, sword and mace.
shots.B01C069S01H05: The lions and herds flee in panic, many animals and elephants die, and the forest is stripped of its wild beasts.

B01C070.summary: After his hunt, Dushmanta crosses a barren plain and reaches a lovely forest beside the river Malini. He finds a hermitage of the sage Kanwa, of the race of Kasyapa, filled with Vedic chanting and learned Brahmanas. He leaves his army at the forest edge and enters with only his minister and priest, which sets up his meeting with Sakuntala.

scenes.B01C070S01: Dushmanta crosses a barren plain, reaches a beautiful forest by the Malini, and resolves to visit the hermitage of Kanwa.
scenes.B01C070S02: He enters the hermitage with only his minister and priest, and is amazed by the chanting and learning of its Brahmanas.

shots.B01C070S01H02: Dushmanta, with a single follower and exhausted, crosses a barren plain and comes to another forest full of hermitages.
shots.B01C070S01H03: The forest is described in detail, with flowering trees, bees, birds, cool breezes, and spots of grass, and the king is charmed.
shots.B01C070S01H04: In the forest the king finds a retreat with a sacred fire, flowing by the Malini river, and worships it.
shots.B01C070S01H05: The king goes to the bank of the river, then decides to visit Kanwa of the race of Kasyapa, halting his army at the forest entrance.
shots.B01C070S02H01: He enters the hermitage with only his minister and priest, hears the Vedas chanted and the learning of its Brahmanas, and wishes to stay longer.

B01C071.summary: Dushmanta finds Kanwa's hermitage empty, and a maiden appears who says she is Kanwa's daughter and that her father has gone to fetch fruit. Dushmanta is struck by her beauty, but doubts that a sage who has kept his vows could have a child. Sakuntala replies that she will explain, and begins with the story of her birth, which starts with Indra's fear of the sage Viswamitra and his sending of Menaka.

scenes.B01C071S01: In the empty hermitage Dushmanta meets Sakuntala, who says she is Kanwa's daughter, and he questions her about her birth.
scenes.B01C071S02: Sakuntala starts to explain her birth, quoting her father's account of Indra's fear of Viswamitra and his sending of Menaka to tempt him.

shots.B01C071S01H02: Dushmanta enters the hermitage alone, finds it empty, and calls out, and a maiden as lovely as Sri comes out and welcomes him.
shots.B01C071S01H03: Sakuntala says her father has gone to fetch fruit and asks the king to wait.
shots.B01C071S01H04: Dushmanta admires her beauty and asks who she is, whose daughter she is, and why she is in the woods.
shots.B01C071S01H05: Dushmanta points out that a sage who has kept his vows could not have fathered a child, and asks her to explain how she came to be his daughter.
shots.B01C071S02H01: Sakuntala says she will tell what she learned about her birth, including the question a visiting Rishi once asked her father.
shots.B01C071S02H02: Kanwa's account begins: Indra, fearing Viswamitra's penances, sends Menaka to tempt him, and Menaka lists his feats and voices her fear of him.

B01C072.summary: Sakuntala reports the rest of Kanwa's account. Menaka tempts Viswamitra, and their union produces a daughter, whom Menaka leaves on a river bank. Vultures guard the infant until Kanwa finds her, adopts her, and names her Sakuntala after the birds, and Sakuntala says she regards Kanwa as her father.

scenes.B01C072S01: Kanwa's account continues with the union of Viswamitra and Menaka, the abandoned infant guarded by vultures, and her adoption by Kanwa.

shots.B01C072S01H02: Marut strips Menaka, Viswamitra desires her, and their daughter is left on a river bank, where vultures guard her until Kanwa adopts her and names her Sakuntala.
shots.B01C072S01H03: Sakuntala closes by saying Kanwa is her father, though she does not know her real one.

B01C073.summary: Dushmanta proposes marriage to Sakuntala in the Gandharva form, a union by mutual consent, and lists the eight forms of marriage. She agrees on the condition that the son born of their union becomes heir-apparent, and they marry before he returns to his capital. Kanwa, returning, knows all and approves the union, blessing the son to come, and Sakuntala asks for a boon that the Paurava kings stay virtuous and keep their thrones.

scenes.B01C073S01: Dushmanta proposes a Gandharva marriage and argues for it from the rules of marriage, and Sakuntala agrees on condition that her son becomes heir.
scenes.B01C073S02: They marry, Dushmanta promises to send an escort, and Kanwa, returning home, approves the union and blesses the coming son.
scenes.B01C073S03: Sakuntala asks Kanwa for a boon that the Paurava monarchs stay virtuous and keep their thrones.

shots.B01C073S01H02: Dushmanta asks Sakuntala to be his wife and offers her gold, robes, pearls and his whole kingdom, and asks her to marry him in the Gandharva form.
shots.B01C073S01H03: Sakuntala says her father has gone to fetch fruit and will give her in marriage when he returns.
shots.B01C073S01H04: Dushmanta argues that a marriage in the Gandharva form is lawful for a Kshatriya, and he lists the eight forms of marriage and which are proper for each class.
shots.B01C073S01H05: Sakuntala agrees to the marriage on one condition: the son born of it must become the heir-apparent.
shots.B01C073S02H01: Dushmanta agrees, marries Sakuntala, and promises to send his troops to escort her to his capital, then leaves.
shots.B01C073S02H02: On his way home Dushmanta wonders what the ascetic will say once he knows all.
shots.B01C073S02H03: Kanwa returns, knows what has happened through his spiritual sight, and approves the Gandharva union, saying the son will be mighty and rule the sea.
shots.B01C073S02H04: Sakuntala washes her father's feet and asks him to bless Dushmanta and his ministers.
shots.B01C073S02H05: Kanwa agrees to bless the king for Sakuntala's sake and offers her a boon.
shots.B01C073S03H01: Sakuntala asks for the boon that the Paurava monarchs may always be virtuous and never lose their thrones.

B01C074.summary: Sakuntala brings her grown son to Dushmanta and asks him to keep his promise and install the boy as heir. Dushmanta denies knowing her and insults her birth, and Sakuntala answers with a long speech on the duties of husbands and fathers and on the power of truth, before threatening to leave. A voice from heaven then declares the boy to be Dushmanta's son, the king names him Bharata and installs him, and the Bharata line begins its glory.

scenes.B01C074S01: Sakuntala brings her son to Dushmanta and asks him to honour his promise, but he denies knowing her, and she answers with a long speech on a father's duty and on truth.
scenes.B01C074S02: A voice from heaven declares the boy to be Dushmanta's son, the king names him Bharata and installs him as heir, and the text describes Bharata's conquests and sacrifices.

shots.B01C074S01H02: The boy grows up strong and is named Sarvadamana, and Kanwa sends Sakuntala and her son to Hastinapura, where she presents the boy and reminds Dushmanta of his promise.
shots.B01C074S01H03: Dushmanta says he remembers nothing, and Sakuntala, angry, answers with a long speech on the gods who witness every deed and on a wife's and a son's place in the family.
shots.B01C074S01H04: Dushmanta replies that women speak untruths, that Menaka and Viswamitra are unworthy parents, and he calls Sakuntala a lewd woman and refuses the child.
shots.B01C074S01H05: Sakuntala answers that she is of higher birth than the king, that the wicked slander the good, and that truth outweighs a hundred horse-sacrifices, and she offers to leave.
shots.B01C074S02H01: After Sakuntala leaves, a voice from heaven tells Dushmanta to acknowledge his son, and says the boy shall be called Bharata; the king says he already knew the boy was his.
shots.B01C074S02H02: Dushmanta welcomes Sakuntala back with honour, installs Bharata as heir, and Bharata's conquests, sacrifices and gifts to Kanwa are described.

B01C075.summary: Vaisampayana recites the royal genealogy from Daksha through Manu and Pururavas, whose arrogance toward the Brahmanas brings his destruction by their curse. He then tells of Nahusha and his son Yayati, who asks his sons to take his old age, and only the youngest, Puru, agrees. Yayati enjoys Puru's youth but finds his desires unsatisfied, so he returns the youth and names Puru his heir, then retires to the mount of Bhrigu and dies.

scenes.B01C075S01: Vaisampayana recites the genealogy from Daksha through Manu, Pururavas and Nahusha to Yayati, who exchanges his old age for Puru's youth and returns it again.
scenes.B01C075S02: Yayati crowns Puru, goes to the mount of Bhrigu, and after long years of asceticism dies and ascends to heaven with his wives.

shots.B01C075S01H02: Vaisampayana says he will recite the sacred genealogy of Daksha, Manu, Bharata, Ruru, Puru and Ajamidha, and of the Yadavas, Kurus and Bharatas.
shots.B01C075S01H03: He recounts Prachetas's sons, Daksha's daughters married to Dharma, Kasyapa and Chandra, Manu's sons, and Pururavas, who robbed Brahmanas and was destroyed by their curse.
shots.B01C075S01H04: Pururavas brings the sacred fires and Urvasi from the Gandharvas, Nahusha rules well but humbles the Rishis, and Yayati, grown old, asks his sons to take his old age, and only Puru agrees.
shots.B01C075S01H05: Yayati enjoys Puru's youth for a thousand years, finds his desires unsatisfied, returns the youth to Puru, and names him his true heir.
shots.B01C075S02H01: Yayati crowns Puru, goes to the mount of Bhrigu for asceticism, and after long years dies and ascends to heaven with his wives.

B01C076.summary: Janamejaya asks how Yayati won Sukra's daughter, and Vaisampayana turns to the war between gods and Asuras. The gods send Kacha, son of Vrihaspati, to learn the reviving science from Sukra, and Kacha wins Devayani's affection, but the Danavas kill him three times. After the last killing, Kacha escapes from Sukra's stomach, revives Sukra, and Sukra then curses Brahmanas who drink wine.

scenes.B01C076S01: Janamejaya asks about Yayati's marriage, and the gods send Kacha to Sukra to learn the reviving science, and Kacha becomes his disciple.
scenes.B01C076S02: Kacha serves Sukra and Devayani for five hundred years, the Danavas kill him, Sukra revives him, and they kill him again.
scenes.B01C076S03: Kacha is hidden inside Sukra's stomach, is brought out by a rip in his belly, and revives Sukra, who then curses wine-drinking Brahmanas.
scenes.B01C076S04: Kacha, after a thousand years of study, takes his leave to return to heaven.

shots.B01C076S01H02: Janamejaya asks how Yayati obtained Sukra's daughter and asks for the founders of the dynasties in order.
shots.B01C076S01H03: Vaisampayana says Sukra and Vrishaparvan gave their daughters in marriage to Yayati, and that Yayati's union with Devayani is the subject.
shots.B01C076S01H04: In the war between gods and Asuras, Sukra revives the slain Asuras, Vrihaspati cannot, so the gods send his son Kacha to learn the science from Sukra.
shots.B01C076S01H05: Kacha asks Sukra to accept him as a disciple, and Sukra welcomes him, saying it honours Vrihaspati.
shots.B01C076S02H01: Kacha takes his vow, wins Devayani's affection by serving her, and after five hundred years the Danavas kill him while he herds the kine.
shots.B01C076S02H02: Devayani tells her father that Kacha is lost and that she will not live without him.
shots.B01C076S02H03: Sukra revives Kacha, who explains that the Danavas killed him under a banyan tree when they learned his purpose.
shots.B01C076S02H04: The Danavas kill Kacha a second time, grind his body into the ocean, then kill him a third time and mix his ashes into Sukra's wine.
shots.B01C076S02H05: Sukra says he can revive Kacha but he will keep being killed, and Devayani says she will starve if Kacha is lost.
shots.B01C076S03H01: Sukra realises the Danavas have killed his disciple, and Kacha calls from inside Sukra's stomach, asking for mercy.
shots.B01C076S03H02: Sukra asks how Kacha got inside him, and Kacha says he was given to Sukra in the wine and has kept his memory.
shots.B01C076S03H03: Devayani says she cannot live without Kacha, and Sukra teaches Kacha the science, since Kacha can only come out by Sukra's death.
shots.B01C076S03H04: Kacha tears open Sukra's stomach, comes out, and revives Sukra with the science, and thanks him as a father and mother.
shots.B01C076S03H05: Sukra, ashamed after drinking wine with Kacha inside him, curses any Brahmana who drinks wine, and tells the Danavas that Kacha will live with him.
shots.B01C076S04H01: The Danavas go home, and after a thousand years of study Kacha takes his leave to return to the gods.

B01C077.summary: Kacha's vow ends and he prepares to return to the gods, but Devayani asks him to marry her. He refuses, saying she is his preceptor's daughter and that he regards her as a sister. Devayani curses that his knowledge will not bear fruit, and he answers that no son of a Rishi will marry her, and that his knowledge will bear fruit only in those he teaches. The gods praise his achievement on his return.

scenes.B01C077S01: Devayani asks Kacha to take her hand, he refuses, and each curses the other.
scenes.B01C077S02: Kacha returns to heaven, and the gods praise his deed and grant him a share in sacrificial offerings.

shots.B01C077S01H02: Devayani, now that his vow is over, praises Kacha and asks him to take her hand with the proper mantras.
shots.B01C077S01H03: Kacha says she is dearer than life to his preceptor and is to be honoured as his daughter, and Devayani answers that he is the son of her father's preceptor's son.
shots.B01C077S01H04: Kacha refuses her, calls her his sister, asks her blessing for his journey, and Devayani says his knowledge will then not bear fruit.
shots.B01C077S01H05: Kacha says he refused only because she is his preceptor's daughter, and curses her that no son of a Rishi will ever marry her, and that his knowledge will bear fruit only in those he teaches.
shots.B01C077S02H01: Kacha goes to heaven, and the gods, led by Indra, praise him and promise him a share in sacrificial offerings.

B01C078.summary: After Kacha brings back his science, Indra, as wind, mixes up the clothes of bathing maidens, and Sarmishtha takes Devayani's garment by mistake. Their quarrel ends with Sarmishtha throwing Devayani into a well, where King Yayati finds her and raises her out. Devayani sends for her father Sukra, who is told of the insult and calms her with words about his own power.

scenes.B01C078S01: Indra's trick sets off the quarrel between Devayani and Sarmishtha, Sarmishtha throws Devayani into a well, and Yayati finds her and asks who she is.
scenes.B01C078S02: Yayati lifts Devayani out and returns to his capital, and Devayani's father Sukra is told of the insult and soothes her.

shots.B01C078S01H02: The gods celebrate Kacha's science, and Indra, as wind, mixes up the clothes of bathing maidens, so Sarmishtha takes Devayani's garment and insults her.
shots.B01C078S01H03: Devayani tries to pull her clothes back, and Sarmishtha throws her into a well and goes home, thinking she is dead.
shots.B01C078S01H04: Yayati, out hunting with thirsty horses, finds the well dry and sees a maiden shining inside it, and asks who she is.
shots.B01C078S01H05: Devayani says she is Sukra's daughter and asks Yayati to take her by the hand and lift her out.
shots.B01C078S02H01: Yayati takes her by the right hand, lifts her from the well, and returns to his capital.
shots.B01C078S02H02: Devayani sends her maid Ghurnika to tell her father what happened, and refuses to enter the city of Vrishaparvan.
shots.B01C078S02H03: Ghurnika tells Sukra, who finds Devayani in the woods, and she repeats Sarmishtha's insult that Sukra is only a hired chanter of praise.
shots.B01C078S02H04: Sukra says his daughter is the child of one who is adored by all, and that he is the lord who sends rain and makes the crops grow.
shots.B01C078S02H05: Sukra soothes his grieving, angry daughter with these words.

B01C079.summary: Sukra counsels Devayani that the man who controls his anger and forgives insults is the true victor. Devayani replies that a disciple's insolence should never be forgiven and that she will not live in a land where bad conduct is tolerated. She says the insults burn her like fire, and that for her death would be better than such shame.

scenes.B01C079S01: Sukra urges forgiveness over anger, and Devayani refuses, saying she will not stay among those who speak ill of good behaviour.

shots.B01C079S01H02: Sukra urges Devayani to forgive and hold her anger, and Devayani replies that she will not live where bad conduct is tolerated and that she would rather die than be insulted.

B01C080.summary: Sukra, angered by the mistreatment of his daughter, announces he will leave the Asuras. Vrishaparvan begs him to stay and offers him all the Asura wealth, but Sukra says he cannot bear his daughter's grief. Devayani then demands that Sarmishtha and a thousand maids serve her, and Sarmishtha, though insulted, agrees, so Sukra returns to the Asura capital.

scenes.B01C080S01: Sukra, angered at the insult, prepares to leave the Asuras, and Vrishaparvan begs him to stay and offers him all the Asura wealth.
scenes.B01C080S02: Devayani demands that Sarmishtha and a thousand maids attend her, and Vrishaparvan orders Sarmishtha to comply.
scenes.B01C080S03: Sarmishtha agrees to become Devayani's attendant and to follow her wherever she is given away, and Sukra returns to the Asura capital.

shots.B01C080S01H02: Sukra, angered, goes to Vrishaparvan and says that sinful acts bear fruit in time, and that he will leave the Asuras because of the slaying of Kacha and the mistreatment of his daughter.
shots.B01C080S01H03: Vrishaparvan says Sukra has never been false and begs him not to go, saying the Asuras would then go into the ocean.
shots.B01C080S01H04: Sukra says he cannot bear his daughter's grief and asks the Asuras to please her, as Vrihaspati works for Indra.
shots.B01C080S01H05: Vrishaparvan says Sukra is lord of all the wealth of the Asura chiefs, including their herds and horses and himself.
shots.B01C080S02H01: Sukra tells Vrishaparvan that if he is lord of Asura wealth, he should go and gratify Devayani.
shots.B01C080S02H02: Devayani says the king must come himself and promise, and then asks for Sarmishtha with a thousand maids to wait on her and follow her wherever she is given away.
shots.B01C080S02H03: Vrishaparvan orders a maid to bring Sarmishtha quickly.
shots.B01C080S02H04: The order continues: Sarmishtha is to be brought, and she is to do what Devayani wishes.
shots.B01C080S02H05: The order closes with the same instruction, so that Devayani's wish is carried out.
shots.B01C080S03H01: The maid tells Sarmishtha that Sukra is about to leave the Asuras because of Devayani, and Sarmishtha says she will do what Devayani wishes.
shots.B01C080S03H02: Sarmishtha comes with a thousand maids in a palanquin and offers to be Devayani's attendant, but Devayani reminds her that she is the daughter of a beggar.
shots.B01C080S03H03: Sarmishtha replies that one must help afflicted relatives, and says she will follow Devayani wherever she is given away.
shots.B01C080S03H04: Devayani, now satisfied, tells her father that she will enter the Asura capital, since his power has not been in vain.
shots.B01C080S03H05: Sukra enters the Asura capital in gladness, and the Danavas worship him with great reverence.

B01C081.summary: Devayani and Sarmishtha, with a thousand maids, are in the woods when Yayati comes by, tired and thirsty. After the two women tell him who they are, Devayani chooses Yayati as her husband, though he says a Brahmana must be feared more than a snake or fire. Sukra arrives and gives Devayani to Yayati, absolving him of the sin of a mixed marriage and forbidding him to take Sarmishtha to his bed, and the marriage is performed.

scenes.B01C081S01: Devayani and Sarmishtha meet Yayati in the woods, and he asks their names and their stations.
scenes.B01C081S02: Devayani chooses Yayati, he resists on grounds of caste, Sukra arrives and gives Devayani to him, and absolves him of the sin of a mixed marriage.
scenes.B01C081S03: Yayati marries Devayani with the proper rites, receives Sarmishtha and the maids, and returns to his capital.

shots.B01C081S01H02: Devayani and Sarmishtha, with a thousand maids, drink flower-honey in the woods, when Yayati arrives, thirsty and tired from hunting, and sees them.
shots.B01C081S01H03: Yayati asks their names and parentage, and Devayani says she is Sukra's daughter and Sarmishtha her attendant.
shots.B01C081S01H04: Yayati asks why Sarmishtha, a daughter of the Asuras, serves Devayani, and Devayani says it is fate and asks his name.
shots.B01C081S01H05: Yayati names himself, a king's son, and says he came in search of water after hunting.
shots.B01C081S02H01: Devayani says she waits on his commands and wishes him well as her lord.
shots.B01C081S02H02: Yayati says he is unworthy of her, Devayani insists on marrying him, and Yayati says a Brahmana is to be feared more than a snake, so he needs her father's consent.
shots.B01C081S02H03: Sukra comes to meet Yayati, who worships him and waits for his commands.
shots.B01C081S02H04: Devayani asks her father to give her to Yayati, and Sukra agrees.
shots.B01C081S02H05: Yayati asks to be absolved from the sin of begetting mixed offspring, and Sukra grants absolution and tells him not to summon Sarmishtha to his bed.
shots.B01C081S03H01: Yayati marries Devayani with the rites, receives her with Sarmishtha and two thousand maids, and returns to his capital.

B01C082.summary: Yayati brings Devayani home and sets up Sarmishtha in a separate mansion. When Devayani bears a son, Sarmishtha, anxious to have a child herself, approaches the king. She argues that a lie is excusable in such matters and that Yayati is her husband too, and he, bound by his vow to grant requests, yields, and she bears a son.

scenes.B01C082S01: Yayati installs Devayani and Sarmishtha, Devayani bears a son, and Sarmishtha, anxious to have a child, approaches the king with her request.
scenes.B01C082S02: Yayati yields to Sarmishtha, and she bears a son.

shots.B01C082S01H02: Yayati puts Devayani in his inner rooms and Sarmishtha in a separate mansion with a thousand maids; Devayani has a son, and Sarmishtha, reaching puberty, worries that she has no husband and wants a child.
shots.B01C082S01H03: Sarmishtha approaches the king in the Asoka grove, when no one can see them, and asks him to give her a child.
shots.B01C082S01H04: Yayati refuses, saying he knows she is of noble birth but Usanas forbade him to summon her to his bed.
shots.B01C082S01H05: Sarmishtha argues that a lie is excusable on certain occasions, and that as Devayani's husband he is her husband too; Yayati, bound by his vow to grant requests, yields.
shots.B01C082S02H01: Yayati honours Sarmishtha by keeping her virtue, and after a time they part.
shots.B01C082S02H02: Sarmishtha conceives from the king and bears a lotus-eyed son who shines like a celestial child.

B01C083.summary: Devayani learns that Sarmishtha has a child and is jealous. Sarmishtha claims the father is a Rishi, but Devayani later finds Sarmishtha's three sons playing with Yayati in the woods and learns the truth. Devayani angrily goes to her father Sukra, who curses Yayati with sudden old age, and Yayati begs for relief.

scenes.B01C083S01: Devayani learns of Sarmishtha's child and is told a Rishi is the father, then finds Sarmishtha's three sons with Yayati in the woods and learns the truth.
scenes.B01C083S02: The boys run to their mother, Devayani accuses Sarmishtha, and she leaves for her father Sukra, who curses Yayati with decrepitude.
scenes.B01C083S03: Yayati begs Sukra to remove the curse, and Sukra says he can pass it to a son willing to take it.

shots.B01C083S01H02: Devayani, jealous of Sarmishtha's child, asks what sin she has committed, and Sarmishtha says a Rishi is the father, which Devayani accepts if it is true.
shots.B01C083S01H03: Devayani has two sons by Yayati and Sarmishtha has three, and they part on friendly terms.
shots.B01C083S01H04: Devayani finds three boys of celestial beauty playing with perfect trust in the king's park, and asks whose children they are.
shots.B01C083S01H05: The boys point at Yayati and name Sarmishtha as their mother.
shots.B01C083S02H01: The boys run to their mother, Yayati, abashed, does not caress them, and Devayani accuses Sarmishtha of wronging her.
shots.B01C083S02H02: Sarmishtha says she chose the king as her friend's husband, and holds him in higher esteem than Devayani's father.
shots.B01C083S02H03: Devayani says Yayati has wronged her and leaves, weeping and angry, and goes to her father Usanas, ignoring the king's pleas.
shots.B01C083S02H04: Devayani tells Sukra that Yayati has deviated from virtue and that Sarmishtha has three sons by him.
shots.B01C083S02H05: Sukra curses Yayati with decrepitude, Yayati defends his action as a duty, and Sukra calls it theft.
shots.B01C083S03H01: Yayati begs for relief, and Sukra says he can pass the decrepitude to a son who will give him his youth, and that son will become king.

B01C084.summary: Yayati, aged by Sukra's curse, asks his eldest son Yadu to exchange youth for his decrepitude. Yadu refuses and is cursed, and Turvasu, Drahyu and Anu do the same. Only Puru agrees to take his old age, and Yayati transfers his decrepitude to him.

scenes.B01C084S01: Yayati asks Yadu and Turvasu to exchange youth for his old age, and both refuse and are cursed.
scenes.B01C084S02: Yayati asks Drahyu and Anu, who refuse and are cursed, and then Puru agrees and takes the decrepitude.

shots.B01C084S01H02: Yayati, aged by the curse, asks his eldest son Yadu to take his decrepitude for a thousand years in exchange for his youth.
shots.B01C084S01H03: Yadu refuses, listing the miseries of old age, and asks his father to ask another son.
shots.B01C084S01H04: Yayati curses Yadu's line and asks Turvasu to take the decrepitude.
shots.B01C084S01H05: Turvasu refuses, and Yayati curses him to rule over impure peoples.
shots.B01C084S02H01: Drahyu and Anu each refuse, and Yayati curses them with the loss of their desires and of their progeny.
shots.B01C084S02H02: Yayati asks his youngest son Puru to take his decrepitude.
shots.B01C084S02H03: Puru agrees humbly, and Yayati promises that his people will have their desires fulfilled.
shots.B01C084S02H04: Yayati transfers his decrepitude to Puru.

B01C085.summary: With Puru's youth, Yayati enjoys life for a thousand years, then realises that desire is never satisfied and returns the youth. The four orders object to passing over the elder sons, but Yayati explains that Puru alone obeyed him, and the people agree to crown Puru. Yayati then retires to the forest, and the peoples descended from his sons are named.

scenes.B01C085S01: Yayati enjoys Puru's youth for a thousand years, renounces desire, returns the youth, and, after the four orders object, is backed by the people in crowning Puru.
scenes.B01C085S02: Puru is crowned, Yayati goes to the forest, and the peoples descended from his sons are named.

shots.B01C085S01H02: Yayati enjoys Puru's youth, honours gods, ancestors and Brahmanas, and after a thousand years concludes that desire is never satisfied and resolves to renounce it.
shots.B01C085S01H03: Yayati takes back his decrepitude and offers the kingdom to Puru, but the four orders object to passing over the elder sons.
shots.B01C085S01H04: Yayati explains that his elder sons disobeyed him, that Puru alone obeyed, and that Sukra said the obedient son would rule.
shots.B01C085S01H05: The people agree that Puru deserves the crown, since he did his father good.
shots.B01C085S02H01: Yayati has Puru crowned, performs the rites for retiring to the woods, and leaves his capital with Brahmanas and ascetics.
shots.B01C085S02H02: The peoples descended from his sons are named: the Yadavas, Yavanas, Bhojas, Mlechchhas, and the Pauravas, to which Janamejaya belongs.

B01C086.summary: Yayati, having crowned Puru, lives in the forest, ascends to heaven, and is later hurled down by Indra, though he remains in the sky and later returns to the celestials. Janamejaya asks why Yayati fell and how he regained heaven, and Vaisampayana agrees to tell the full story.

scenes.B01C086S01: Yayati withdraws to the forest, ascends to heaven and is hurled down, and Janamejaya asks for the whole story, which Vaisampayana agrees to tell.

shots.B01C086S01H02: Yayati lives in the forest with Brahmanas, then ascends to heaven, is hurled down by Indra, stays in the sky, and later returns to the celestials with several other kings.
shots.B01C086S01H03: Janamejaya asks why Yayati was hurled from heaven, how he regained admission, and for the full story of his life on earth and in heaven.
shots.B01C086S01H04: Vaisampayana agrees to recite Yayati's adventures on earth and in heaven, which destroy the sins of those who hear them.
shots.B01C086S01H05: Yayati lives the forest life, feeding guests, gratifying gods and ancestors, keeping vows, and performing austerities, before ascending to heaven.

B01C087.summary: Yayati lives in heaven, honoured by the gods, and visits the region of Brahman. When Indra asks what he told Puru on handing over the kingdom, Yayati recites his counsel: rule the land between the Ganga and Yamuna, be forgiving, avoid harsh speech, and follow the wise.

scenes.B01C087S01: Yayati dwells in heaven, and Indra asks him what he said to Puru when he gave up the kingdom.
scenes.B01C087S02: Yayati recites his counsel to Puru on kingship, forgiveness and speech.

shots.B01C087S01H02: Yayati lives in heaven, honoured by the gods, and sometimes goes to the region of Brahman.
shots.B01C087S01H03: One day Yayati talks with Indra, who asks him a question.
shots.B01C087S01H04: Indra asks what Yayati said when Puru took his decrepitude and he gave up the kingdom.
shots.B01C087S01H05: The question continues, asking what Yayati said when he handed over the earth to Puru.
shots.B01C087S02H01: Yayati says he told Puru the land between the Ganga and Yamuna was his, that the forgiving and the wise are superior, and that he should speak kindly and follow the virtuous.

B01C088.summary: Indra tells Yayati that his virtue has diminished because he disregards his superiors and equals, so he must fall from heaven. Yayati asks to fall among the virtuous, and Indra agrees. As Yayati falls, the royal sage Ashtaka sees him and welcomes him into a gathering of the wise, where he is safe.

scenes.B01C088S01: Indra tells Yayati he must fall for disregarding others, Yayati asks to fall among the virtuous, and as he falls the royal sage Ashtaka welcomes him.

shots.B01C088S01H02: Indra asks Yayati to whom he is equal in austerities, Yayati says he knows no equal, and Indra says his virtue has diminished from disregarding others, so he must fall, and Yayati asks to fall among the virtuous.
shots.B01C088S01H03: Yayati falls from heaven, and the royal sage Ashtaka sees him, asks who he is, and tells him he is safe among the virtuous and the wise.

B01C089.summary: Falling from heaven, Yayati introduces himself to the sages and explains that he did not greet them first because he is older. He reflects that destiny rules all, that the wise should neither exult nor grieve, and that all beings return to the Supreme Soul. When Ashtaka, his grandson through a daughter, asks where he has been, Yayati recounts his long stay in the heavens and the celestial warning that brought his fall.

scenes.B01C089S01: Yayati, falling from heaven, introduces himself, speaks on destiny and humility, and recounts his stay in the heavens and his fall.

shots.B01C089S01H02: Yayati introduces himself as Puru's father, says he is falling for having disregarded others, and explains that he did not greet Ashtaka first because he is older.
shots.B01C089S01H03: Ashtaka replies that a man deserves honour for learning and ascetic merit rather than for age.
shots.B01C089S01H04: Yayati says vanity destroys merit, destiny rules all, and all created things return to the Supreme Soul when freed from their acts.
shots.B01C089S01H05: Ashtaka asks about the regions Yayati has visited, and Yayati describes his long stay in the heavens, the messenger's cry of ruin, and the fall that brought him here.

B01C090.summary: Ashtaka questions Yayati about the afterlife. Yayati says that boasters suffer in the earth-hell, that a fallen being is reborn through the womb from a subtle seed of water, and that the dead keep their memories and enter new forms. He ends by listing the seven gates to heaven, all of which vanity destroys, and says that knowledge without humility does not lead to Brahma.

scenes.B01C090S01: Ashtaka asks why Yayati was cast out, and Yayati describes the earth-hell of self-praise and the sufferings of rebirth.
scenes.B01C090S02: Ashtaka asks how fallen beings are reborn, and Yayati explains rebirth from a subtle seed through the womb.
scenes.B01C090S03: Yayati lists the seven gates to heaven and says vanity destroys them.

shots.B01C090S01H02: Ashtaka asks why Yayati left Nandana and how one loses virtue in the other world, and Yayati says the celestials forsake one who has lost righteousness.
shots.B01C090S01H03: Yayati says that those who boast of their merits go to the earth-hell called Bhauma, where they are consumed by their own descendants.
shots.B01C090S01H04: Ashtaka asks where man goes after death, and says he has never heard of the earth-hell.
shots.B01C090S01H05: Yayati describes rebirth through the mother's womb, and says the fallen are tormented by Rakshasas in the form of sons and kin.
shots.B01C090S02H01: Ashtaka asks why the fallen are attacked and how they enter the womb again.
shots.B01C090S02H02: Yayati explains that the fallen being becomes a subtle substance in water, then seed, then embryo, and finally takes visible form.
shots.B01C090S02H03: Ashtaka asks how the body and senses form, and Yayati says the subtle being is drawn to the seed according to its merits and gains its senses at birth.
shots.B01C090S02H04: Ashtaka asks how one is revived after death, and Yayati says the dead keep their memory and enter new forms, with the virtuous rising and the vicious sinking.
shots.B01C090S02H05: Ashtaka asks whether the regions of no return are reached by asceticism or by knowledge.
shots.B01C090S03H01: Yayati lists seven gates to heaven, which vanity destroys, and says learning without humility does not lead to Brahma.

B01C091.summary: Ashtaka asks how the four stages of life should be lived, and Yayati outlines the duties of the student, householder, mendicant and forest-dweller. Ashtaka then asks how many kinds of Munis there are, and Yayati explains that a Muni is one who is detached and content, whether he lives in the woods or in a village.

scenes.B01C091S01: Ashtaka asks how the four stages of life should be lived, and Yayati outlines the duties of each, then the number of kinds of Munis.
scenes.B01C091S02: Yayati explains what a Muni is, wherever he lives, and describes the silent, detached ascetic.

shots.B01C091S01H02: Ashtaka says the learned differ on how the four stages of life should be followed for religious merit.
shots.B01C091S01H03: Yayati describes the duties of the student, the householder, the mendicant and the forest-dweller.
shots.B01C091S01H04: Ashtaka asks how many kinds of Munis there are.
shots.B01C091S01H05: Yayati says a Muni may live in the woods with a village near, or in a village with the woods near.
shots.B01C091S02H01: Ashtaka asks what a Muni is, and Yayati says he is one who has withdrawn from worldly objects and remains content, whether he lives in woods or in a hamlet.
shots.B01C091S02H02: Yayati praises the silent, pure and detached ascetic who takes only what comes to him, and says he attains salvation.

B01C092.summary: Ashtaka asks whether the ascetic or the man of knowledge first reaches Brahman, and Yayati says the wise attain it first by knowledge. Yayati then says he is falling into the earth-hell, and Ashtaka offers him the heavenly regions he has earned. Yayati refuses to accept gifts he has not earned, and Pratardana then offers his worlds too.
