scenes.B01C092S01: Ashtaka asks whether the ascetic or the knower reaches Brahman first, and Yayati says the wise do, and then reveals that he is falling to the earth-hell.
scenes.B01C092S02: Ashtaka offers Yayati the regions he has earned, Yayati refuses, and Pratardana asks whether he too has regions.
scenes.B01C092S03: Pratardana offers his worlds, and Yayati refuses, saying a king should not take another's merit.

shots.B01C092S01H02: Ashtaka asks whether the ascetic or the man of knowledge reaches communion with Brahma first.
shots.B01C092S01H03: Yayati says the wise attain it through knowledge, while yogis take longer, and that sacrifices done for reward bear no fruit.
shots.B01C092S01H04: Ashtaka notes that Yayati looks young and asks where he is going.
shots.B01C092S01H05: Yayati says he is falling into the earth-hell, but Indra granted that he would fall among the wise.
shots.B01C092S02H01: Ashtaka asks whether there are regions in heaven for him to enjoy, so that Yayati need not fall.
shots.B01C092S02H02: Yayati says there are as many regions for Ashtaka as there are cows and horses on earth.
shots.B01C092S02H03: Ashtaka offers Yayati all the regions his merits have earned, so that Yayati will not fall.
shots.B01C092S02H04: Yayati refuses, saying only a Brahmana who knows Brahma may take gifts, and that he has never accepted one.
shots.B01C092S02H05: Pratardana asks whether there are regions in heaven for him to enjoy as the fruit of his merit.
shots.B01C092S03H01: Yayati says numberless blissful worlds await Pratardana, enough to last seven days in each.
shots.B01C092S03H02: Pratardana offers Yayati all the worlds he has earned, so that Yayati will not fall.
shots.B01C092S03H03: Yayati refuses, saying a king should not take another king's merit, and that he will not accept what others do not.

B01C093.summary: Vasumat and Sivi each offer Yayati the heavenly worlds they have earned, and Yayati refuses to take gifts he has not earned, although Vasumat offers to let him buy them for a straw. Ashtaka and the others then board five golden cars, and the company sets out for heaven, with Sivi ahead as the most generous. Yayati identifies himself and recounts his gifts and truthfulness, and the chapter closes with his ascent, rescued by his descendants.

scenes.B01C093S01: Vasumat asks for heavenly worlds, offers them to Yayati, and proposes that he buy them, which Yayati declines.
scenes.B01C093S02: Sivi offers his worlds too, Yayati refuses, and Ashtaka says they will descend if Yayati does not take them.
scenes.B01C093S03: Yayati says he will take only what he has earned, and the others point him to five golden cars.
scenes.B01C093S04: The company sets out for heaven together, and Ashtaka asks why Sivi has gone ahead, and Yayati explains and identifies himself.
scenes.B01C093S05: Vaisampayana closes the episode, saying Yayati ascends to heaven, rescued by his descendants.

shots.B01C093S01H02: Vasumat, son of Oshadaswa, asks whether there are worlds for him to enjoy as fruit of his merit.
shots.B01C093S01H03: Yayati says there are as many regions for Vasumat as there are places in the sky, the earth and the ten directions.
shots.B01C093S01H04: Vasumat offers his regions to Yayati, and if a gift is improper, suggests Yayati buy them for a straw.
shots.B01C093S01H05: Yayati says he has never bought or sold anything unfairly, and that other kings have not done so either.
shots.B01C093S02H01: Vasumat says that if buying is improper, Yayati should take the regions as a gift, since he will never go to them.
shots.B01C093S02H02: Sivi, son of Usinara, asks whether there are worlds in heaven for him to enjoy.
shots.B01C093S02H03: Yayati says Sivi has never disregarded the virtuous and that infinite worlds await him; Sivi offers to give Yayati all of them.
shots.B01C093S02H04: Yayati declines, saying he does not want regions given by others.
shots.B01C093S02H05: Ashtaka says each of them has offered Yayati their worlds, and that if he refuses they will descend to the earth-hell.
shots.B01C093S03H01: Yayati says he will receive only what he deserves, and that he cannot do what he has never done.
shots.B01C093S03H02: Ashtaka asks whose five golden cars these are, and whether men ride them to the regions of bliss.
shots.B01C093S03H03: Yayati says the five golden cars would carry them to the regions of bliss.
shots.B01C093S03H04: Ashtaka asks Yayati to ride ahead in one of the cars.
shots.B01C093S03H05: Ashtaka says they can wait and will follow him later.
shots.B01C093S04H01: Yayati says they can all go together, since they have conquered heaven, and the path is now visible.
shots.B01C093S04H02: Vaisampayana says the monarchs ride toward heaven, lighting the sky with the glory of their virtues.
shots.B01C093S04H03: Ashtaka asks why Sivi, son of Usinara, has gone ahead of him, since he thought Indra was his friend.
shots.B01C093S04H04: Yayati answers that Sivi gave all he had for the region of Brahma, and that his generosity and virtues are unmatched.
shots.B01C093S04H05: Ashtaka asks who Yayati is, and Yayati identifies himself as Nahusha's son and Puru's father, recounts his gifts of land and cattle, and says truth sustains the world.
shots.B01C093S05H01: Vaisampayana says Yayati ascends to heaven, rescued by his collateral descendants, and covers the three worlds with his fame.

B01C094.summary: Janamejaya asks for the histories of the kings descended from Puru, and Vaisampayana traces the line from Puru's sons through Dushmanta and Bharata. The Panchalas defeat the Bharatas and drive Samvarana into exile until the sage Vasishtha restores him. The line then runs through Kuru, Kurukshetra, Pratipa and Santanu.

scenes.B01C094S01: Vaisampayana traces Puru's line through Dushmanta and Bharata to Samvarana, whose defeat by the Panchalas is reversed by Vasishtha, and on through Kuru, Pratipa and Santanu.
scenes.B01C094S02: Vaisampayana says many more excellent monarchs were born in the lines of Bharata and Manu.

shots.B01C094S01H02: Janamejaya asks for the histories of the kings of Puru's line, none of whom lacked virtue, prowess or sons.
shots.B01C094S01H03: Vaisampayana promises to tell of the heroic kings of Puru's line, all equal to Indra in prowess.
shots.B01C094S01H04: The line runs from Puru's sons through Manasyu, Kaudraswa's ten sons, Matinara, Tansu, Ilina, Dushmanta, Bharata and Suhotra to Ajamidha, and the Panchalas defeat Samvarana until Vasishtha restores him.
shots.B01C094S01H05: Samvarana's son Kuru, after whom Kurukshetra is named, is followed by Janamejaya, Parikshit, Dhritarashtra, Pratipa and Santanu.
shots.B01C094S02H01: Many more excellent monarchs were born in the lines of Bharata and Manu, and the Aila dynasty grew great.

B01C095.summary: Janamejaya asks for the full genealogy from Manu, and Vaisampayana recites it from Daksha and Aditi through Yayati, Puru and Janamejaya's own line. The line runs through Dushmanta and his son Bharata, who gave the family its name, to Hastinapura, Kuru and Santanu. The chapter gives Janamejaya a full account of his ancestry.

scenes.B01C095S01: Vaisampayana starts the genealogy from Daksha and Aditi and runs through Yayati and the descendants of Puru to Tansu.
scenes.B01C095S02: The genealogy passes through Ilina and Dushmanta to Sakuntala and her son Bharata, with verses on Dushmanta's descendants.
scenes.B01C095S03: The name of Bharata is explained, and the line runs through Hastinapura and its kings to Santanu.

shots.B01C095S01H02: Janamejaya says the earlier account was too short and asks for the full genealogy from Manu, the lord of creation.
shots.B01C095S01H03: Vaisampayana says he will recite the genealogy of Janamejaya's own race as he heard it from Dwaipayana.
shots.B01C095S01H04: The line runs from Daksha and Aditi through Vivaswat, Manu, Pururavas, Nahusha, Yayati and Puru, then through Janamejaya, Prachinwat, Sanyati, Ahayanti, Sarvabhauma and Ayutanayi, down to Tansu.
shots.B01C095S01H05: A verse says Tansu was born of Saraswati by Matinara, and that Tansu begot Ilina on Kalingi.
shots.B01C095S02H01: Ilina begets five sons with Rathantari, and Dushmanta is the eldest.
shots.B01C095S02H02: Dushmanta takes Sakuntala, the daughter of Viswamitra, as his wife.
shots.B01C095S02H03: They have a son, Bharata, and the text introduces two verses about Dushmanta's descendants.
shots.B01C095S02H04: The text completes the introduction of the verses on Dushmanta's descendants.
shots.B01C095S02H05: A verse says the father is reborn as the son, and urges Dushmanta to support his son and not insult Sakuntala.
shots.B01C095S03H01: Bharata is so called because he was supported, and the line runs through Bhumanyu, Suhotra, Hasti, who founded Hastinapura, Ajamidha, Samvarana, Kuru, Parikshit and Santanu.

B01C096.summary: The chapter traces Santanu's line through his son Bhishma and Satyavati's sons, then through Pandu's curse and the birth of the five Pandavas to Kunti and Madri. It lists the Pandavas' troubles with Duryodhana, their marriages and children, and ends with the rebirth of Parikshit. It then turns to King Mahabhisha, cursed by Brahman for staring at Ganga, who asks to be reborn to Pratipa, while Ganga agrees to bear the Vasus as her children.

scenes.B01C096S01: The text traces the line from Santanu through Bhishma, Satyavati's sons and Pandu's curse to the Pandavas, their marriages, and the rebirth of Parikshit, and ends with the recital's benefits.
scenes.B01C096S02: Mahabhisha is cursed for staring at Ganga, asks to be reborn to Pratipa, and Ganga agrees to bear the Vasus, cursed by Vasishtha, as her children.

shots.B01C096S01H01: An opening verse says the old men touched by Santanu regained their youth, which is why he was named Santanu.
shots.B01C096S01H02: The text traces the line from Santanu and Ganga's son Bhishma through Satyavati's sons Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura, Pandu's curse, the five Pandavas, their rivalry with Duryodhana, their marriages and children, and the rebirth of Parikshit.
shots.B01C096S01H03: The narrator says this history should be heard by all four orders with reverence, that it brings heaven to those who hear it, and quotes a verse in its praise.
shots.B01C096S02H01: King Mahabhisha of Ikshvaku's line wins heaven through a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred Rajasuyas.
shots.B01C096S02H02: When Ganga's garment is blown aside before the gods, Mahabhisha stares at her, and Brahman curses him to be reborn and to face Ganga again.
shots.B01C096S02H03: Mahabhisha chooses to be born as the son of Pratipa, and Ganga, meeting the Vasus, learns they were cursed by Vasishtha to be born among men and asks them how they will be her children.
shots.B01C096S02H04: The Vasus ask Ganga to drown their children at birth so they can return quickly, and Ganga agrees on condition that one son lives.
shots.B01C096S02H05: The Vasus make their arrangement with Ganga and go their way.

B01C097.summary: Ganga appears to the ascetic-king Pratipa as a maiden and asks him to take her as his wife. Pratipa refuses on grounds of his vow, but offers her as wife to his future son, and she agrees on condition that Santanu never judge her acts. Pratipa later retires to the woods, and Santanu, out hunting by the Ganges, falls in love with Ganga and asks her to marry him.

scenes.B01C097S01: Ganga comes to Pratipa as a maiden, is refused and offered as a wife to his son, agrees on conditions, and Santanu later meets and asks to marry her.

shots.B01C097S01H02: Ganga comes to the ascetic-king Pratipa as a beautiful maiden and sits on his right thigh, asking him to take her, but he refuses on grounds of his vow and offers to accept her as his son's wife.
shots.B01C097S01H03: Ganga agrees to become a wife of Bharata's race, and asks that Santanu never judge the propriety of her acts.
shots.B01C097S01H04: Ganga disappears, and Pratipa waits for the birth of the son to fulfil his promise.
shots.B01C097S01H05: Santanu is born after Pratipa's penance, Pratipa tells him to accept the damsel as his wife, and Pratipa then retires to the woods; later Santanu sees Ganga on the riverbank and asks her to marry him.

B01C098.summary: Ganga agrees to marry Santanu on condition that he never interfere with her acts or speak to her harshly, and he keeps his promise. She drowns each of their first seven sons at birth, and the king's silence breaks only when the eighth is threatened. Ganga reveals that she bore the eight Vasus and freed them from their curse, then leaves, giving the eighth child to Santanu to rear as Gangadatta.

scenes.B01C098S01: Ganga marries Santanu under conditions, drowns their sons one by one until the king protests, and leaves after revealing who she is, giving the eighth child to Santanu to rear.

shots.B01C098S01H02: Ganga marries Santanu on the conditions that he never interfere with her, and she drowns the first seven sons; when the eighth is threatened, Santanu protests and she reveals she is the Ganga, bore the Vasus, and will leave, giving the child to him to rear as Gangadatta.

B01C099.summary: Santanu asks why the Vasus were cursed to be born among men, and Ganga explains that the sage Vasishtha, also called Apava, cursed them after they stole his wish-granting cow Nandini. Dyu, who took the cow to please his wife, must live on earth for a time and remain childless, and the Vasus were freed when Ganga drowned them at birth. Ganga then takes her son away, and Santanu returns home sorrowful.

scenes.B01C099S01: Santanu asks why the Vasus were cursed, and Ganga describes Vasishtha's asylum and the cow Nandini, and how the Vasus, led by Dyu, stole her.
scenes.B01C099S02: Vasishtha curses the Vasus, softens the curse for Dyu, Ganga disposes of the children, and she leaves with her son while Santanu returns home.

shots.B01C099S01H02: Santanu asks Ganga why the Vasus were cursed to be born among men, who Apava was, and what his son Gangadatta has done.
shots.B01C099S01H03: Ganga says the sage Vasishtha, also called Apava, lived in a sacred asylum on Mount Meru, where he performed his austerities.
shots.B01C099S01H04: Ganga describes Nandini, the cow of plenty, born to Surabhi and Kasyapa, who was given to the sage for his sacrifices.
shots.B01C099S01H05: The Vasus come to the sage's woods, and Dyu's wife, seeing Nandini, asks her husband to steal the cow for her friend, and he does so.
shots.B01C099S02H01: When the sage returns and finds the cow gone, he sees by his power that the Vasus took her and curses them to be born on earth.
shots.B01C099S02H02: The Vasus beg for mercy; the sage says they will be freed within a year of birth, but Dyu must live on earth for a time, childless.
shots.B01C099S02H03: Ganga says the Vasus asked her to drown them at birth, which she agreed to do, and that only Dyu must remain on earth for a time.
shots.B01C099S02H04: Ganga disappears with the child, who is named Gangeya and Devavrata, and excels his father in all skills.
shots.B01C099S02H05: Santanu returns to his capital sorrowful, and the narrator says he will now recount Santanu's virtues.

B01C100.summary: Santanu's virtuous reign is praised, and Ganga returns his grown son Devavrata, who becomes heir. Santanu falls in love with a fisherman's daughter, but the fisherman demands that her son be made heir, which Santanu cannot promise. Devavrata renounces the throne and vows lifelong celibacy, earns the name Bhishma, and Santanu grants him the power to choose the time of his death.

scenes.B01C100S01: Santanu's virtues and peaceful reign are praised, and Ganga presents his grown son Devavrata, whom Santanu makes heir.
scenes.B01C100S02: Santanu meets the fisherman's daughter, the fisherman demands a pledge about her son, and Devavrata goes to win her for his father.
scenes.B01C100S03: Devavrata renounces the throne and vows celibacy, the fisherman gives his daughter, and Devavrata is named Bhishma and granted the choice of his death.

shots.B01C100S01H02: Santanu is praised for his wisdom, virtue and truthfulness, his peaceful reign, and his kindness to all creatures, and he retires to the woods after thirty-six years.
shots.B01C100S01H03: Santanu's son Devavrata, born to Ganga, grows into a skilled and mighty warrior like his father.
shots.B01C100S01H04: Santanu, chasing a deer, finds the Ganges run shallow and sees a youth stop its flow with a celestial weapon.
shots.B01C100S01H05: Ganga presents the grown youth to Santanu as his eighth son, and Santanu takes him home and makes him heir.
shots.B01C100S02H01: Santanu meets a fragrant fisherman's daughter by the Yamuna and asks her father for her hand.
shots.B01C100S02H02: The fisherman says the match depends on a pledge that the son of his daughter will be the next king.
shots.B01C100S02H03: Santanu, unwilling to make the pledge, grows melancholy, and when Devavrata asks why, he explains his fear of having no heir.
shots.B01C100S02H04: Devavrata learns of the pledge from the old minister and goes with elder chiefs to ask for the maiden, and the fisherman says the only objection is the rivalry his own sons might pose to her son.
shots.B01C100S02H05: Devavrata vows that the son of the maiden shall be king, and the fisherman, though satisfied, still has doubts about the children Devavrata may have.
shots.B01C100S03H01: Devavrata renounces his right to the throne and vows lifelong celibacy, and says that if he dies sonless he will attain heaven.
shots.B01C100S03H02: The fisherman gives his daughter, flowers fall from the sky, the gods name Devavrata Bhishma, and he helps the maiden into his chariot.
shots.B01C100S03H03: Bhishma takes the maiden to Hastinapura, the kings praise him, and Santanu grants him the boon of dying only when he chooses.

B01C101.summary: Santanu marries Satyavati, and their sons Chitrangada and Vichitravirya are born, after which Santanu dies. Chitrangada is later slain in a battle with a Gandharva of the same name, and Bhishma crowns the young Vichitravirya, who obeys him.

scenes.B01C101S01: Santanu's sons are born to Satyavati, Santanu dies, Chitrangada is killed by a Gandharva, and Bhishma installs Vichitravirya.

shots.B01C101S01H02: After Santanu's marriage to Satyavati, their sons Chitrangada and Vichitravirya are born; Santanu dies, Bhishma places Chitrangada on the throne, a Gandharva of the same name kills him in battle, and Bhishma crowns the young Vichitravirya, who obeys him.

B01C102.summary: Bhishma, acting for his half-brother Vichitravirya, carries off the three princesses of Kasi at their swayamvara, defeating the assembled kings and sparing the defeated Salya. He lets the eldest, Amba, go to the king she had loved, and marries Ambika and Ambalika to Vichitravirya, who dies of disease after seven years. Bhishma then arranges his funeral rites.

scenes.B01C102S01: Bhishma wins the Kasi princesses by force, defeats the kings and Salya, lets Amba go, and marries Ambika and Ambalika to Vichitravirya, who dies of consumption.

shots.B01C102S01H02: After Chitrangada's death, Bhishma rules under Satyavati, and goes to Kasi, where he carries off three princesses for his brother, saying that taking a bride by force is a lawful form of marriage.
shots.B01C102S01H03: The challenged kings give chase, and Bhishma defeats them all, cutting down bows, armour and heads, and takes the princesses on to Hastinapura.
shots.B01C102S01H04: King Salya challenges Bhishma, who destroys Salya's charioteer and horses and defeats him, but lets him live.
shots.B01C102S01H05: Bhishma brings the princesses to Hastinapura, allows Amba to go to the king she loved, and marries Ambika and Ambalika to Vichitravirya, who dies of consumption after seven years, and Bhishma performs his funeral rites.

B01C103.summary: Satyavati, grieving for her son, asks Bhishma to raise children on his brother's widows to continue the line. Bhishma refuses, saying he will not give up his vow of truth, and that a Kshatriya must not break truth. He promises to suggest another remedy for the line's extinction.

scenes.B01C103S01: Satyavati asks Bhishma to raise children on his brother's widows, and Bhishma refuses on grounds of truth and his vow.

shots.B01C103S01H02: Satyavati, grieving, asks Bhishma to raise children on Ambika and Ambalika, to keep the line alive, and to take the throne and marry.
shots.B01C103S01H03: Bhishma refuses, reminding her of his vow of truth, saying he would give up the three worlds before he would give up truth, and promising to suggest a Kshatriya remedy.

B01C104.summary: To persuade Satyavati, Bhishma tells how Parashurama emptied the earth of Kshatriyas, and how Kshatriya women then bore children to Brahmanas. He recounts the story of Dirghatamas, born blind after Brihaspati ignored the unborn child's protest, who was later cast into the Ganges, rescued by King Vali, and fathered sons on Vali's wife and her nurse. Bhishma concludes that the Kshatriya line has often been continued by seed from Brahmanas.

scenes.B01C104S01: Bhishma tells Satyavati of Parashurama's destruction of the Kshatriyas and the story of Utathya's son Dirghatamas, born blind, and of his marriage and quarrel with his wife.
scenes.B01C104S02: Dirghatamas is cast into the Ganges, rescued by King Vali, and fathers sons, and Bhishma concludes that the line may be continued by Brahmanas' seed.

shots.B01C104S01H02: Bhishma says Parashurama slew the Kshatriya king of the Haihayas and then destroyed the Kshatriyas twenty-one times.
shots.B01C104S01H03: When the earth was emptied of Kshatriyas, Kshatriya women had children by Brahmanas, and the children belonged to the husband, so the Kshatriya race was revived.
shots.B01C104S01H04: Utathya's wife Mamata was with child when Brihaspati approached her, and the unborn child protested; Brihaspati cursed the child, who was born blind and named Dirghatamas.
shots.B01C104S01H05: Dirghatamas marries and has children, but his wife complains that he does not support her, and he tells her that a woman must keep one husband only.
shots.B01C104S02H01: Dirghatamas's sons, at their mother's command, cast him into the Ganges; King Vali rescues him and asks him to father children on his queen, and he fathers eleven sons through the queen's nurse and five through the queen, after whom five countries are named.
shots.B01C104S02H02: Bhishma says that the line of Vali was perpetuated by a great Rishi, that many warriors were born of Brahmanas' seed, and tells Satyavati to do as she likes.

B01C105.summary: Bhishma proposes that a Brahmana be paid to raise children on Vichitravirya's widows. Satyavati reveals that her son Vyasa, born to the sage Parashara before her marriage, can do it, and Bhishma approves. Vyasa agrees on condition that the women keep a year-long vow, and after Satyavati persuades one of the widows, the princess of Kosala, to accept him, the plan goes ahead.

scenes.B01C105S01: Bhishma proposes a paid Brahmana, Satyavati reveals that Vyasa, her son by Parashara, can serve, and Bhishma approves and calls Vyasa.
scenes.B01C105S02: Vyasa agrees on condition of a year's vow and warns of his looks, and Satyavati persuades the princess of Kosala to accept him.

shots.B01C105S01H02: Bhishma proposes that an accomplished Brahmana be paid to raise children on Vichitravirya's wives.
shots.B01C105S01H03: Satyavati, smiling and shy, says she will name the means, calling Bhishma the embodiment of virtue and truth.
shots.B01C105S01H04: Satyavati recalls that as a young ferrywoman she carried Parashara across the Yamuna and bore Vyasa, who divided the Vedas, and offers to summon him.
shots.B01C105S01H05: Bhishma approves, Vyasa comes to his mother, and Satyavati asks him to beget children on the widows.
shots.B01C105S02H01: Vyasa agrees to beget children for his brother, provided the women first keep a vow for one year.
shots.B01C105S02H02: Satyavati urges that the women conceive at once, since a kingdom without a king falls into ruin.
shots.B01C105S02H03: Vyasa says his looks and odour are grim, and asks that the princess accept him anyway.
shots.B01C105S02H04: Vyasa asks that the princess of Kosala wait for him, and Satyavati persuades her daughter-in-law to accept.
shots.B01C105S02H05: Satyavati feeds Brahmanas, Rishis and guests for the occasion.

B01C106.summary: The princess of Kosala, Vichitravirya's eldest widow, shuts her eyes in fear of Vyasa and bears a blind son, Dhritarashtra. Ambalika turns pale at his sight and bears Pandu, who is pale in complexion. A third widow sends a maidservant, who bears Vidura, a son who is wise and fortunate.

scenes.B01C106S01: The three widows bear Dhritarashtra, who is blind, Pandu, who is pale, and Vidura, born of a maidservant, each as Vyasa has foretold.

shots.B01C106S01H02: Satyavati prepares the princess of Kosala, who shuts her eyes in fear when Vyasa enters, and Vyasa says her son will be blind because of her fault.
shots.B01C106S01H03: Ambalika turns pale at Vyasa's sight, so he says her son will be pale and named Pandu, and Pandu is born.
shots.B01C106S01H04: The third widow sends a maidservant to Vyasa, who promises that her son will be wise and fortunate, and this son is Vidura.
shots.B01C106S01H05: Thus Vyasa's sons, the splendid heirs of the Kuru line, are born in Vichitravirya's field.

B01C107.summary: Janamejaya asks what the god of justice did to be cursed to be born in the Sudra caste, and by which Brahmana. Vaisampayana tells of the sage Mandavya, who sat silent under a tree while thieves hid their loot in his hermitage. The officers impaled him as a thief, and the sage survived, and other sages came to him in the form of birds to ask what sin he had committed.

scenes.B01C107S01: Janamejaya asks about Dharma's curse, and Vaisampayana tells how the sage Mandavya was impaled as a thief and was visited by sages in bird form.

shots.B01C107S01H02: Janamejaya asks what the god of justice did to be cursed, and which Brahmana cursed him to be born a Sudra.
shots.B01C107S01H03: The learned sage Mandavya sits silent under a tree while thieves hide their loot in his hermitage, and the officers impale him as a thief, and other sages come as birds to ask what sin he has committed.

B01C108.summary: Mandavya, still alive on the stake, forgives the king and is known from then on as Ani-Mandavya, the sage with the stake in him. He goes to the god of justice and asks what sin he committed, and the god says it was pricking an insect as a child. Mandavya rules that a child's offence is no sin, and curses the god of justice to be born a Sudra, which is how Vidura came to be born.

scenes.B01C108S01: Mandavya forgives the king, questions the god of justice, learns that his offence was a child's, and curses Dharma to be born as Vidura.

shots.B01C108S01H02: Mandavya, still living on the stake, forgives the king, who cuts the stake off so that a part remains in him, and he becomes known as Ani-Mandavya, and goes to ask the god of justice why he was punished.
shots.B01C108S01H03: The god of justice says Mandavya pricked a little insect as a child, and Mandavya rules that a child's offence is not sin and curses the god to be born a Sudra.
shots.B01C108S01H04: Dharma is born as Vidura in the Sudra order, learned in morality and politics, free from greed and anger, and devoted to the Kurus.

B01C109.summary: After the three sons are born, the Kuru land prospers in a golden age, with good harvests, honest people and a splendid capital. Bhishma raises Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura as his own sons, and each excels in a different art. Pandu becomes king, since Dhritarashtra is blind and Vidura is born of a Sudra woman, and Bhishma then turns to Vidura for counsel on family matters.

scenes.B01C109S01: The Kuru land prospers, Bhishma raises the three princes, Pandu becomes king, and Bhishma turns to Vidura for counsel.

shots.B01C109S01H02: The text describes the prosperity of the Kuru land, with good harvests, a splendid capital, honest people, and the upbringing of Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura by Bhishma, who excel in archery, strength and virtue, and the reasons Pandu rules, and then Bhishma speaks to Vidura.

B01C110.summary: Bhishma proposes marriages for the Kuru princes, naming three noble maidens of pure blood, and Vidura defers to him. Bhishma hears that Gandhari, daughter of Suvala, has a boon of a hundred sons from Siva, and arranges her marriage to the blind Dhritarashtra. Gandhari blindfolds herself out of devotion to her husband, and her brother Sakuni brings her to Hastinapura, where she serves the family faithfully.

scenes.B01C110S01: Bhishma proposes marriages, Vidura defers, and Gandhari is married to Dhritarashtra, blindfolding herself out of devotion.

shots.B01C110S01H02: Bhishma says the Kuru line must be expanded, names three maidens of pure blood from the Yadava, Suvala and Madra families, and asks Vidura for his view, which Vidura defers to him.
shots.B01C110S01H03: Bhishma hears that Gandhari, daughter of Suvala, has a boon of a hundred sons from Siva; Suvala gives her to the blind Dhritarashtra, Gandhari blindfolds herself, and Sakuni brings her to Hastinapura, where she serves her husband and family faithfully.

B01C111.summary: Pritha, the daughter of Sura, is given to Kuntibhoja, and Durvasa gives her a mantra to summon any god. Testing it as a maiden, she summons the Sun, who fathers Karna, and she abandons the child in the water. Karna is raised by Radha and her husband, and later gives his natural armour to Indra in disguise, earning the name Karna for cutting it away.

scenes.B01C111S01: Pritha receives Durvasa's mantra, summons the Sun, and bears Karna, who is abandoned and raised by Radha and her husband, gives his armour to Indra, and is named Karna.

shots.B01C111S01H02: Sura's daughter Pritha is given to Kuntibhoja, and when she serves the sage Durvasa, he gives her a mantra to summon any god, so she summons the Sun.
shots.B01C111S01H03: Pritha asks the Sun's pardon for testing the mantra, and the Sun insists that his approach must bear fruit.
shots.B01C111S01H04: Pritha consents, and bears Karna with armour and earrings, then casts him into the water, and Radha and her husband raise him as Vasusena; Karna later gives his armour to Indra in disguise and receives a dart.
shots.B01C111S01H05: Karna, having cut off his natural armour, is called Karna.

B01C112.summary: Pritha, now called Kunti, has no suitors, so her father holds an assembly at which she may choose her husband. She chooses Pandu, the Kuru prince, and they are married with the rites and return to Hastinapura.

scenes.B01C112S01: Kunti chooses Pandu at her father's assembly, and the couple is married and goes to Hastinapura.

shots.B01C112S01H02: Kunti, though beautiful and virtuous, has no suitors, so her father invites kings to an assembly; she places the garland on Pandu, and the rites are performed before he returns to Hastinapura with his bride.

B01C113.summary: Bhishma goes to Madra to seek Madri as a second wife for Pandu. King Salya explains his family custom, and Bhishma, accepting it, offers gifts that persuade Salya to give his sister. Pandu marries Madri, conquers many kingdoms, and returns to Hastinapura in triumph.

scenes.B01C113S01: Bhishma wins Madri for Pandu from Salya with gifts, Pandu marries her, and he conquers many kingdoms and returns in triumph.

shots.B01C113S01H02: Bhishma goes to Madra for Madri, Salya says his family custom must be kept, Bhishma accepts it and gives him gold, gems and carriages, and Salya gives his sister, whom Bhishma brings to Hastinapura.
shots.B01C113S01H03: Pandu marries Madri, then sets out to conquer, subduing the robber tribes, Magadha, Videha, Kasi and others, and receives tribute before returning to Hastinapura, where Bhishma welcomes him with tears of joy.

B01C114.summary: Pandu shares his conquest wealth with Bhishma, Satyavati and the others, and performs sacrifices with the money. He then retires with Kunti and Madri to the forests of the Himalaya to hunt, and is supplied with comforts at Dhritarashtra's command. Bhishma marries Vidura to Devaka's daughter, who is born of a Sudra wife, and they have many sons.

scenes.B01C114S01: Pandu shares his wealth with the family and performs sacrifices, retires to the woods with his wives, and Bhishma arranges Vidura's marriage.

shots.B01C114S01H02: At Dhritarashtra's command, Pandu gives his conquest wealth to Bhishma, Satyavati, the mothers and relatives, and Ambalika embraces her son with joy; Dhritarashtra then performs five great sacrifices with the wealth.
shots.B01C114S01H03: Pandu retires with Kunti and Madri to a hilly region of the Himalaya, where he hunts deer and roams freely.
shots.B01C114S01H04: At Dhritarashtra's command, people supply Pandu in his retreat with all pleasures.
shots.B01C114S01H05: Bhishma marries Devaka's daughter, born of a Sudra wife, to Vidura, and they have many sons like him.

B01C115.summary: Gandhari, granted a boon of a hundred sons, goes two years without delivering and in grief strikes her womb, producing a lump of flesh. Vyasa divides it into a hundred and one parts, which grow in pots of butter. Duryodhana is born first, with ominous signs, and Dhritarashtra asks whether his son or the eldest Yudhishthira should be king, and Vidura advises casting off the first son, but Dhritarashtra refuses.

scenes.B01C115S01: Gandhari's boon and two-year pregnancy lead to a lump of flesh, which Vyasa divides into parts that are kept in pots of butter to mature.
scenes.B01C115S02: Duryodhana is born with ominous signs, Dhritarashtra asks who should be king, and Vidura's advice to cast off the eldest is refused, and the hundred sons, a daughter and Yuyutsu are born.

shots.B01C115S01H02: Vaisampayana says Dhritarashtra had a hundred sons and a son by a Vaisya woman, while Pandu had five sons by Kunti and Madri, begotten by the gods.
shots.B01C115S01H03: Janamejaya asks how Gandhari bore her hundred sons, how long each lived, how Yuyutsu was born, and how Pandu's sons were begotten despite his curse.
shots.B01C115S01H04: Vyasa grants Gandhari a boon of a hundred sons; after two years she strikes her womb in grief and produces a hard lump of flesh, which Vyasa then tells her to sprinkle with water and keep in pots.
shots.B01C115S01H05: The lump is divided into a hundred and one parts, put in pots of butter, and kept under watch, and Vyasa goes off to the Himalaya for asceticism.
shots.B01C115S02H01: Duryodhana is born from one of the pots, and Yudhishthira is named the oldest, and the news goes to Bhishma and Vidura.
shots.B01C115S02H02: Duryodhana brays like an ass and omens of disaster follow, Dhritarashtra asks whether his son or Yudhishthira should be king, Vidura advises casting off the first son, and Dhritarashtra refuses; a hundred sons, a daughter, and Yuyutsu by a Vaisya maid are born.
shots.B01C115S02H03: The text closes its account of the sons: a hundred heroic sons, a daughter, and Yuyutsu of a Vaisya woman.

B01C116.summary: Janamejaya asks how Gandhari came to have a daughter, Duhsala, when Vyasa had divided the lump into only a hundred parts. Vaisampayana explains that Gandhari secretly wished for a daughter, and Vyasa set aside an extra part in its own pot, which became Duhsala. Vaisampayana then offers to tell more.

scenes.B01C116S01: Janamejaya asks how Duhsala was born, and Vaisampayana explains that the extra part of the lump, set aside for Gandhari's wish, became her daughter.

shots.B01C116S01H02: Janamejaya asks how Gandhari had a daughter in addition to the hundred sons, when the lump was divided into only a hundred parts.
shots.B01C116S01H03: Vaisampayana explains that Gandhari secretly longed for a daughter, and Vyasa counted out the hundred parts and set an extra part aside, which was put in its own pot to become Duhsala.
shots.B01C116S01H04: Vaisampayana says he has now told the whole story of Duhsala's birth.
shots.B01C116S01H05: Vaisampayana asks Janamejaya what more he should tell.

B01C117.summary: Janamejaya asks for the names of Dhritarashtra's sons in order of birth. Vaisampayana gives the long list of the hundred sons and names their one sister, Duhsala. He says they were all warriors and scholars, and that Duhsala was given in marriage to Jayadratha, king of Sindhu. This closes the account of the Kaurava side before the story turns to the Pandavas.

scenes.B01C117S01: Janamejaya asks for the sons' names in birth order, and Vaisampayana recites them, adding that they were skilled warriors and that Duhsala was married to Jayadratha.

shots.B01C117S01H02: Janamejaya asks for the names of Dhritarashtra's sons in the order they were born.
shots.B01C117S01H03: Vaisampayana recites the long list, says the sons were warriors and scholars, and reports that Duhsala was wed to Jayadratha.

B01C118.summary: Janamejaya asks to hear about the Pandavas from their birth, now that he has heard the Kaurava names. Vaisampayana tells how Pandu, hunting in the Himavat woods, shoots a deer that is actually a sage, Kindama, while the sage is mating with his mate. The dying sage rebukes Pandu and curses him to die at the moment desire rises in him, with his wife following him to the land of the dead. This curse is the reason for Pandu's later renunciation.

scenes.B01C118S01: Janamejaya asks about the Pandavas, and Vaisampayana begins with Pandu shooting a deer in the forest, which turns out to be a sage in animal form, who cries out like a man.
scenes.B01C118S02: Pandu defends the killing, and the dying sage answers that the timing was the crime and curses Pandu to die when desire takes him.

shots.B01C118S01H02: Janamejaya asks to hear everything about the Pandavas from the moment of their birth.
shots.B01C118S01H03: Pandu, hunting on the slopes of the Himavat, shoots with five arrows a deer that is serving its mate, and the wounded animal turns out to be a sage in deer form who cries out like a man.
shots.B01C118S01H04: The deer rebukes Pandu for a cruel act against dharma, and Pandu replies that kings hunt deer as they hunt enemies, citing an old precedent from the sage Agastya.
shots.B01C118S01H05: The deer answers that striking an unprepared foe is wrong, though killing after war has been declared openly is not.
shots.B01C118S02H01: Pandu says deer are killed in many ways whether they are careful or not, so the deer has no reason to reproach him.
shots.B01C118S02H02: The deer says its real grievance is that it was shot mid-act, reveals that it is the sage Kindama, and curses Pandu to die at the moment desire rises in him, with his wife dying alongside him.
shots.B01C118S02H03: The deer dies, and Pandu is overcome with grief.

B01C119.summary: After the curse, Pandu weeps and resolves to give up desire, children and worldly life for forest asceticism. His wives insist on going with him, and he sends word to the court that he has retired to the woods. He gives his wealth to Brahmanas, sends his attendants back to Hastinapura, and travels with his wives through the Himalayas toward Satasringa. The chapter begins the forest life of Pandu and his wives.

scenes.B01C119S01: Pandu vows to renounce desire and the world, and his wives insist on sharing his forest life. He gives away his wealth, and his attendants carry the news back to Hastinapura, where Dhritarashtra grieves.
scenes.B01C119S02: Pandu travels with his wives through a series of named mountains and lakes in the Himalayas, reaching the Hundred-Peak mountain where he continues his austerities.

shots.B01C119S01H02: Pandu, grieving over the deer's curse, blames his own lust and fate and vows to live as a celibate ascetic, listing the restraints he will keep.
shots.B01C119S01H03: Pandu asks that his family and court be told he has gone to the forest, and his wives Kunti and Madri insist on following him in austerity.
shots.B01C119S01H04: Pandu agrees to take up the forest life of severe penances, offerings to the gods and ancestors, and the Vanaprastha rules with his wives.
shots.B01C119S01H05: Pandu gives his jewels and robes to Brahmanas, his attendants leave for Hastinapura, and Dhritarashtra mourns his brother and loses his taste for comfort.
shots.B01C119S02H01: Pandu and his wives travel through named mountains and lakes of the Himalayas, guarded by Siddhas and sages, and reach the Hundred-Peak mountain where he keeps up his austerities.

B01C120.summary: Pandu's austerities win him the regard of the Siddhas and sages, and when the sages set out for Brahma's gathering he asks to join them, though they warn that the northern heights are too dangerous for his wives. Pandu says a sonless man cannot reach heaven and that his debt to his ancestors remains unpaid. The sages foresee a blessed son, and Pandu urges Kunti to bear children by another man of high standing.

scenes.B01C120S01: Pandu asks to go with the sages to Brahma's gathering. They warn him that the northern heights are too dangerous, and he answers that he is sonless and has not repaid his debt to his ancestors.
scenes.B01C120S02: The sages foresee a blessed son for Pandu, and Pandu, recalling his lost power to beget children, asks Kunti to have sons by another man.

shots.B01C120S01H02: Pandu's austerities win him the favour of the Siddhas and Charanas, and sages treat him as a brother, friend or son, so that he becomes almost a Brahmarshi.
shots.B01C120S01H03: On a new-moon day the great sages set out to see Brahman, and Pandu asks where they are going.
shots.B01C120S01H04: Pandu prepares to follow the sages with his wives, but they warn him that the northern heights are too dangerous for ordinary beings and for the princesses.
shots.B01C120S01H05: Pandu replies that a sonless man cannot reach heaven, that his debt to his ancestors is unpaid, and asks whether his wives may bear children.
shots.B01C120S02H01: The sages say a sinless, godlike son is destined for Pandu, and tell him to act on that destiny.
shots.B01C120S02H02: Pandu, remembering that the deer's curse took his power to father children, asks Kunti to bear sons by another man of high standing, citing Saradandayana's daughter as a precedent.

B01C121.summary: Kunti refuses to take any other man and asks Pandu to father children on her himself. To make her case she tells the old story of King Vyushitaswa, whose widow Bhadra, sonless and grieving, was promised offspring by a voice. The dead king's body is said to have fathered seven children on her, and Kunti urges Pandu to use his ascetic power the same way.

scenes.B01C121S01: Kunti tells Pandu she will accept only him, then recounts the story of Vyushitaswa and his widow Bhadra, whose promised offspring came from the dead king's body, and asks Pandu to do likewise.

shots.B01C121S01H02: Kunti tells Pandu she will accept no other man and asks him to father children on her, then announces she will tell an old story.
shots.B01C121S01H03: She tells of King Vyushitaswa, a great sacrificer of the Puru line, whose early death left his widow Bhadra sonless, and of her grief as she asks to follow him.
shots.B01C121S01H04: Kunti continues: a voice promises Bhadra children, and the dead king's body fathers seven of them; she asks Pandu to act with his ascetic power the same way.

B01C122.summary: Pandu replies that in ancient times women moved freely and were not bound to one husband, and that the present rule of fidelity was set by Swetaketu out of anger. He cites other precedents, such as Madayanti bearing a son to Vasishtha, and says a wife must obey her husband's command to bear children. Kunti then reveals a mantra Durvasa gave her to summon a god, and Pandu tells her to call upon Dharma, the god of justice.

scenes.B01C122S01: Pandu argues from old precedents that wives should bear children at their husband's command, and Kunti recalls the mantra Durvasa once gave her to call a god.
scenes.B01C122S02: Pandu chooses Dharma, the god of justice, as the father, and Kunti agrees to call him.

shots.B01C122S01H02: Pandu agrees that Vyushitaswa's example is true, then says women in older times were free and not bound to one husband, without that being sinful.
shots.B01C122S01H03: He explains that Swetaketu set the present rule of wifely fidelity in anger after a Brahmana led off his mother, and says that breaking the rule is a sin for women and men alike.
shots.B01C122S01H04: Pandu cites Madayanti, who had a son by Vasishtha at her husband's bidding, and says a wife must obey a husband's order to bear children, so Kunti should bear sons through a Brahmana.
shots.B01C122S01H05: Kunti recalls that as a girl she served the sage Durvasa, who gave her a mantra to summon any god as a child's father, and asks Pandu which god to call.
shots.B01C122S02H01: Pandu names Dharma, the god of justice, as the one who would never bring sin on them and whose son would be the most virtuous of the Kurus.
shots.B01C122S02H02: Kunti agrees, bows to Pandu, and walks around him before resolving to do as he asks.

B01C123.summary: Kunti calls on Dharma, the god of justice, who fathers Yudhishthira, and then on Vayu, who fathers the strong Bhima. Pandu, wanting a greater son, undertakes a long austerity to win Indra, and Kunti's call to Indra brings forth Arjuna. The gods, sages and celestial singers gather to celebrate, but when Pandu asks for more children Kunti refuses, saying a fourth union is not sanctioned.

scenes.B01C123S01: Kunti calls Dharma and Vayu, who father Yudhishthira and Bhima. Pandu then decides to win Indra's favour through a year of severe austerity, and Kunti keeps her own vow.
scenes.B01C123S02: Indra promises Pandu a son and fathers Arjuna, and the gods and celestial beings gather to celebrate. When Pandu asks for more children, Kunti refuses.

shots.B01C123S01H02: Kunti calls on Dharma, who fathers Yudhishthira, and a voice from the sky foretells that he will be the best of men and a famed king.
shots.B01C123S01H03: Pandu asks for a child of greater strength, and Kunti calls on Vayu, who fathers Bhima; the infant's fall breaks a rock without harm, and Duryodhana is born the same day.
shots.B01C123S01H04: Pandu resolves to win Indra's favour through severe austerity, so that he can have a son of great strength.
shots.B01C123S01H05: Pandu has Kunti keep a yearlong vow, while he stands on one leg through the days and practises austerities.
shots.B01C123S02H01: Indra comes to Pandu and promises a famous son who will be a slayer of foes, and Pandu tells Kunti her vow has succeeded and to call on Indra.
shots.B01C123S02H02: Kunti calls on Indra, who fathers Arjuna, and a loud voice foretells his great deeds and his fame.
shots.B01C123S02H03: Gods, sages, Gandharvas and Apsaras gather in celebration, shower flowers, and dance, and a long list of divine beings honours the son of Pritha.
shots.B01C123S02H04: Pandu wishes to call on another god for more children, but Kunti refuses, saying the wise do not sanction a fourth union.

B01C124.summary: Madri asks Pandu for children of her own, and Pandu persuades Kunti to help. Kunti tells Madri to call a god, and Madri bears the twins Nakula and Sahadeva to the Ashvins. The five sons are named and grow up on the mountain, and Kunti later refuses further requests, complaining that Madri has used the mantra to gain twins.

scenes.B01C124S01: Madri asks Pandu for children, Pandu asks Kunti to help, and Kunti tells Madri to call a god, so Madri bears twins to the Ashvins.
scenes.B01C124S02: The five sons are named and grow up on the mountain, and Kunti later refuses Pandu's request for more children.

shots.B01C124S01H02: Madri, princess of the Madras, tells Pandu she is childless while Kunti has sons, and asks him to help her have children.
shots.B01C124S01H03: Pandu says he has thought about it and will ask Kunti, whom he believes will not refuse.
shots.B01C124S01H04: Pandu asks Kunti privately to give Madri children, pointing to the benefit of offerings and of fame.
shots.B01C124S01H05: Kunti tells Madri to think of a celestial, and Madri summons the Ashvins, who father the twins Nakula and Sahadeva; a voice says they will outshine the Ashvins.
shots.B01C124S02H01: The sages on the mountain name the five sons, Yudhishthira, Bhimasena, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva, and the boys become favourites of the sages.
shots.B01C124S02H02: Pandu asks Kunti again on Madri's behalf, but Kunti refuses, complaining that Madri gained two sons from one mantra and that she was misled.
shots.B01C124S02H03: The five Pandavas, begotten by gods, grow up strong and learned, alongside the hundred sons of Dhritarashtra.

B01C125.summary: Pandu, roaming a flowering grove with Madri, is overcome by desire, forces himself on her, and dies in the act, as the sage's curse had foretold. Kunti and Madri both claim the right to die with him, and Madri argues that she should be the one to follow him and asks Kunti to raise her sons. Madri then climbs onto the funeral pyre.

scenes.B01C125S01: Pandu forces himself on Madri in a spring grove and dies in the act. Kunti and Madri argue over who will follow him in death, and Madri makes her case.
scenes.B01C125S02: Madri ascends her husband's funeral pyre.

shots.B01C125S01H02: In a blossoming spring forest, Pandu, feeling his strength return, is overcome by desire, seizes Madri against her will, and dies in the act, as the curse foretold.
shots.B01C125S01H03: Madri calls Kunti, who comes grieving and blames Madri for taking Pandu into solitude.
shots.B01C125S01H04: Madri replies that she resisted, but Pandu could not control himself, as if he were making the sage's curse come true.
shots.B01C125S01H05: Kunti claims the right to follow Pandu as the senior wife, but Madri asks for Kunti's leave to go with him instead, saying Kunti is better able to raise her sons.
shots.B01C125S02H01: Madri ascends her husband's funeral pyre.

B01C126.summary: The sages on the mountain decide that Pandu's sons, left in their trust, must be taken to Hastinapura, and they set out with Kunti, the boys and the two bodies. At the gate, the court and citizens come out to greet them, and the eldest sage tells the Kurus how each son was born and asks for Pandu's rites to be performed. The sages then vanish from sight.

scenes.B01C126S01: The sages bring Pandu's family to Hastinapura, where the court and citizens gather. The eldest sage presents the five sons, explains their divine births and asks for the funeral rites, and then the sages vanish.

shots.B01C126S01H02: The sages on the mountain agree that Pandu left his sons in their trust, and resolve to take them to Hastinapura.
shots.B01C126S01H03: The sages set out with the children, Kunti and the two bodies; Kunti, unused to hardship, finds the journey short, and at Kurujangala the city comes out in crowds.
shots.B01C126S01H04: Bhishma, Dhritarashtra, Vidura and the court welcome the sages, and the eldest sage tells how Pandu retired, how each son was divinely born, and how Madri died, asking that the rites be performed.
shots.B01C126S01H05: The sages vanish before the eyes of the people, and the citizens return home in wonder.

B01C127.summary: Dhritarashtra orders a royal funeral for Pandu and Madri, with gifts to all who ask and careful wrapping of Madri's body. Vidura and Bhishma prepare the rites, and the bodies are carried in procession to the Ganga, bathed, dressed and burned. After Kausalya collapses in grief, the Kurus perform the water rite, and the city mourns for twelve days with the Pandavas.

scenes.B01C127S01: Dhritarashtra orders a royal funeral, and Vidura and Bhishma carry out the rites by the Ganga, where the bodies are burned while the people weep.
scenes.B01C127S02: The Kurus perform the water rite, and the people mourn for twelve days with the Pandavas.

shots.B01C127S01H02: Dhritarashtra tells Vidura to give Pandu and Madri a royal funeral with gifts to those who ask, and to wrap Madri's body so the sun and wind cannot see it.
shots.B01C127S01H03: Vidura and Bhishma choose a sacred site, and the bodies are carried in procession with priests, music and gifts to a wood on the Ganga, where they are washed, anointed and dressed.
shots.B01C127S01H04: The Kauravas light the pyre with lotuses, sandal paste and other fragrant offerings.
shots.B01C127S01H05: Kausalya falls senseless at the sight of the burning bodies, and the citizens, the birds and the beasts join in the lament, while Bhishma and Vidura are left disconsolate.
shots.B01C127S02H01: The Kurus perform the water rite, the Pandavas and their friends sleep on the ground, and the city mourns for twelve days with them.

B01C128.summary: After Pandu's funeral rites are performed and the people return to Hastinapura, Vyasa warns his mother Satyavati that the age is declining, and she goes to the forest and ascends to heaven. Pandu's sons grow up strong, and Bhima outplays the Kaurava boys, which stirs Duryodhana's jealousy. Duryodhana then plots to drown Bhima, who survives the poisoning and the water and is restored among the serpents.

scenes.B01C128S01: After the funeral, Vyasa warns that the age is declining, and Satyavati retreats to the forest to die. The Pandava boys grow up, and Bhima proves stronger than the Kaurava boys in play.
scenes.B01C128S02: Duryodhana, jealous of Bhima, poisons his food and throws him into the Ganga, but Bhima sinks to the Naga realm, where the serpents' venom cancels the poison and he revives.
scenes.B01C128S03: The Naga king's kin give Bhima nectar that makes him very strong, and he drinks eight jars of it.

shots.B01C128S01H02: Bhishma and Kunti perform Pandu's rites and feed the Kauravas and many Brahmanas, and the citizens return to Hastinapura in mourning.
shots.B01C128S01H03: Vyasa tells his mother Satyavati that sin is rising, the Kuru empire will not last, and she should retire to the forest.
shots.B01C128S01H04: Satyavati asks her daughter-in-law Ambika and Bhishma for leave, goes to the forest with two daughters-in-law, and leaves her body to ascend to heaven.
shots.B01C128S01H05: The Pandava boys are purified and grow up, and Bhima outplays the hundred Kaurava boys by pulling them by the hair and tormenting them in rough play, though not out of malice.
shots.B01C128S02H01: Duryodhana, jealous of Bhima's strength, plans to drown him in the Ganga and builds a water-sport house at Pramanakoti for an outing.
shots.B01C128S02H02: At the feast Duryodhana poisons Bhima's food; after bathing, Bhima collapses, is bound with creepers and thrown into the river, and sinks into the Naga realm, where the serpents' bites neutralise the poison.
shots.B01C128S02H03: Bhima wakes, breaks his bonds and presses the serpents underground, and the survivors report to their king Vasuki.
shots.B01C128S02H04: Vasuki goes to see Bhima, finds that Aryaka is a relative of Kunti's family, and offers Bhima wealth and gems.
shots.B01C128S02H05: Aryaka suggests that Bhima be allowed to drink from the nectar vessels, which hold the strength of a thousand elephants each.
shots.B01C128S03H01: The serpents perform rites, Bhima purifies himself, drinks eight jars of nectar, and lies down on a bed they prepare for him.

B01C129.summary: The Kauravas return to Hastinapura without Bhima, and Kunti, fearing that Duryodhana has killed him, asks for help. Vidura counsels her to protect her other sons, and after eight days Bhima wakes in the Naga realm, strengthened, and returns to his brothers. When Duryodhana tries poison again, Yuyutsu warns the Pandavas, and Dhritarashtra has all the princes taught arms by Kripa.

scenes.B01C129S01: The Kauravas return without Bhima, and Yudhishthira and Kunti, alarmed, ask about him; Kunti fears Duryodhana has killed him.
scenes.B01C129S02: Vidura advises Kunti not to accuse Duryodhana, and to protect her other sons.
scenes.B01C129S03: Bhima wakes, returns from the Naga realm and tells his brothers what happened; Duryodhana tries poison again, and Yuyutsu warns the Pandavas.
scenes.B01C129S04: Duryodhana and his allies keep plotting, but the Pandavas bear it on Vidura's advice, and Dhritarashtra sends the princes to Kripa to learn arms.

shots.B01C129S01H02: The Kauravas ride home without Bhima, assuming he has gone ahead, and Duryodhana is glad to be rid of him.
shots.B01C129S01H03: Yudhishthira, trusting others to be as honest as himself, asks Kunti whether Bhima has come home, and fears he is dead.
shots.B01C129S01H04: Kunti, alarmed, says Bhima has not come to her and urges the brothers to search for him.
shots.B01C129S01H05: Kunti calls Vidura and says she fears Duryodhana, who covets the throne, has killed Bhima.
shots.B01C129S02H01: Vidura tells Kunti not to say such things and to protect her other sons.
shots.B01C129S02H02: He warns that accusing Duryodhana openly could lead him to harm her remaining sons.
shots.B01C129S02H03: He says a great sage has foretold that all her sons will live long.
shots.B01C129S02H04: So Bhima will surely return and gladden her heart.
shots.B01C129S02H05: Vidura goes home, and Kunti remains anxious with her children.
shots.B01C129S03H01: On the eighth day Bhima wakes, his strength increased by the nectar, and the Nagas encourage him and urge him to go home.
shots.B01C129S03H02: Bhima bathes, dresses in white with garlands, eats a rice pudding offered by the Nagas, and is carried back to the garden where he had been playing.
shots.B01C129S03H03: Bhima embraces his mother and brothers, who all rejoice at his return.
shots.B01C129S03H04: Bhima tells his brothers of Duryodhana's treachery and of his time in the Naga realm; Yudhishthira asks them to keep silent and guard one another, and Vidura keeps advising them.
shots.B01C129S03H05: Duryodhana poisons Bhima's food again, but Yuyutsu warns the Pandavas, and Bhima swallows it without harm.
shots.B01C129S04H01: Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni devise more schemes against the Pandavas, who keep their anger in check on Vidura's advice.
shots.B01C129S04H02: Dhritarashtra appoints Gautama, also called Kripa, who was born in a clump of heath, to teach the princes the use of arms.

B01C130.summary: Janamejaya asks how Kripa was born and where he got his weapons. Vaisampayana explains that Gautama's son Saradwat was born skilled in arms, and that after a nymph sent by Indra distracted him, his seed fell on a clump of heath and produced twins. King Santanu adopted the twins, named Kripa and Kripi, and Saradwat later trained Kripa in arms.

scenes.B01C130S01: Janamejaya asks about Kripa's birth, and Vaisampayana traces the twins to Saradwat and a nymph sent by Indra, and tells how Santanu adopted them and Saradwat trained Kripa.

shots.B01C130S01H02: Janamejaya asks how Kripa was born from a clump of heath and where he got his weapons.
shots.B01C130S01H03: Vaisampayana tells how Saradwat, son of Gautama, was born with arms and had a gift for them, and how Indra sent the nymph Janapadi to tempt him, so that his seed fell on heath and became twins.
shots.B01C130S01H04: A soldier of King Santanu finds the twins by their bow and deer-skin, and the king adopts them as Kripa and Kripi; Saradwat then learns where his children are, explains their lineage, and trains Kripa, who later teaches many princes.

B01C131.summary: Bhishma chooses Drona, son of Bharadwaja, to teach the princes, and they quickly master the arts of war. Vaisampayana explains Drona's birth from Bharadwaja's seed, which was caught in a vessel after he saw a nymph, and tells of Drona's marriage to Kripi and the birth of Aswatthaman. Drona then goes to Rama, Jamadagni's son, who gives away his wealth and his weapons to him.

scenes.B01C131S01: Bhishma hires Drona to teach the princes, and Vaisampayana traces Drona's birth from Bharadwaja's seed, his friendship with Drupada, and the birth of his son Aswatthaman.
scenes.B01C131S02: Drona goes to Rama, Jamadagni's son, who has given away all his wealth, and receives all of his weapons and knowledge of arms.

shots.B01C131S01H02: Bhishma, wanting his grandsons well taught, chooses Drona, son of Bharadwaja, as their teacher, and the Kurus and Pandavas soon master the weapons.
shots.B01C131S01H03: Janamejaya asks how Drona was born, where he got his weapons, and how his son Aswatthaman came to be.
shots.B01C131S01H04: Vaisampayana tells how Bharadwaja caught his seed in a vessel after seeing the nymph Ghritachi, which produced Drona, who learned the Vedas and received the Agneya weapon from Agnivesa.
shots.B01C131S01H05: Drupada, son of Prishata, becomes Drona's playmate; after Bharadwaja's death Drona marries Kripi, whose son Aswatthaman is named for his horse-like cry at birth.
shots.B01C131S02H01: Drona hears that Rama, Jamadagni's son, is giving away his wealth and travels to Mahendra to ask for his weapons and wisdom.
shots.B01C131S02H02: Rama says he has given away his gold and lands and offers his body or his weapons, and Drona asks for the weapons.
shots.B01C131S02H03: Drona asks for the weapons along with the secrets of hurling and recalling them.
shots.B01C131S02H04: Rama gives Drona all his weapons and the whole science of arms, and Drona sets out for the city of his friend Drupada, well rewarded.

B01C132.summary: Drona goes to his old boyhood friend Drupada, king of the Panchalas, and claims their friendship. Drupada, proud of his wealth, rebukes him and says that friendship cannot last between a rich man and a poor one. Drona, filled with anger, leaves for Hastinapura.

scenes.B01C132S01: Drona reminds Drupada of their friendship, Drupada mocks his poverty and rejects him, and Drona leaves for Hastinapura.

shots.B01C132S01H02: Drona presents himself to Drupada as his friend, but Drupada, proud of his wealth, scorns him and says old friendships fade and cannot join unequals.
shots.B01C132S01H03: Drona, filled with anger, resolves to check Drupada's arrogance and leaves the Panchala capital for Hastinapura.

B01C133.summary: Drona lives quietly in Kripa's house, while his son Aswatthaman gives the Kuru princes some lessons. When the princes lose a ball in a well, Drona recovers it with blades of grass and then retrieves a ring with an arrow, and Bhishma recognises him. Drona explains how Drupada, once his boyhood friend, has scorned him, and Bhishma gives him the post of teacher to the princes.

scenes.B01C133S01: Drona lives in Kripa's house, and when the princes lose a ball in a well, he recovers it with blades of grass before they know who he is.
scenes.B01C133S02: Drona retrieves a ring, the princes report to Bhishma, and Drona tells how Drupada scorned him; Bhishma then welcomes him as teacher.

shots.B01C133S01H02: Drona lives privately in Kripa's house, and his son Aswatthaman gives the Kuru princes a few lessons, though his skill is still unknown.
shots.B01C133S01H03: A section marker announces Section CXXXIV.
shots.B01C133S01H04: The princes lose their ball in a dry well, and a lean Brahmana, Drona in disguise, offers to bring it up with grass blades for a meal, then drops his ring in as well.
shots.B01C133S01H05: Drona does as he promised, lifting the ball by a chain of grass blades, and the amazed princes ask him to bring up the ring too.
shots.B01C133S02H01: Drona shoots an arrow through the ring and lifts it from the well, and the princes greet him as a master of arms and ask who he is.
shots.B01C133S02H02: The princes tell Bhishma, who recognises Drona, welcomes him to the palace, and asks why he has come.
shots.B01C133S02H03: Drona recounts his marriage to Kripi and the birth of his son Aswatthaman.
shots.B01C133S02H04: Drona tells how, in poverty, his crying son was fooled into thinking rice water was milk, how Drupada, now a king, scorned their old friendship, and why he has come to the Kurus.
shots.B01C133S02H05: Bhishma asks Drona to teach the Kuru princes and promises him the wealth and kingdom of the Kurus.

B01C134.summary: Bhishma gives Drona a house and presents, and Drona takes the Kaurava and Pandava princes as pupils, with Arjuna the most devoted. Refused as a pupil, the tribal prince Ekalavya makes a clay image of Drona and becomes a fine archer on his own; when Drona later demands his right thumb as fee, Ekalavya gives it, and Arjuna is relieved. Drona then tests his pupils by having them aim at a mock bird, and each one reports seeing more than the target and is sent aside.

scenes.B01C134S01: Bhishma honours Drona, and Drona teaches the princes, with Arjuna excelling; Karna, backed by Duryodhana, opposes Arjuna, and Ekalavya is refused as a pupil.
scenes.B01C134S02: On a hunt, a dog leads the princes to Ekalavya, who shows great skill; Drona then asks for his right thumb as fee, and Ekalavya gives it.
scenes.B01C134S03: Drona rates the princes' skills, then tests them with a mock bird, and each pupil reports seeing more than the target and is sent aside.

shots.B01C134S01H02: Bhishma honours Drona with a house and gifts and hands the Kaurava and Pandava princes over to him as pupils.
shots.B01C134S01H03: Drona asks the princes to promise a future service; they stay silent, but Arjuna vows to fulfil it, and Drona embraces him in tears. Karna, backed by Duryodhana, begins to defy Arjuna.
shots.B01C134S01H04: Drona gives his son a wide water jar and the other pupils narrow ones, but Arjuna fills his jar with a water weapon and keeps pace with Aswatthaman, and Drona praises his practice in the dark.
shots.B01C134S01H05: Drona trains Arjuna in fighting from horse, elephant, chariot and ground, and with many weapons; Ekalavya, son of the Nishada king, is refused as a pupil, so he makes a clay image of Drona and practises before it.
shots.B01C134S02H01: On a hunt, a servant's dog wanders into the woods, where it sees the dark, matted Ekalavya and barks at him.
shots.B01C134S02H02: Ekalavya shoots seven arrows into the dog's open mouth; the Pandavas, amazed, search the woods, find him, and learn he is a pupil of Drona.
shots.B01C134S02H03: The Pandavas report to Drona, and Arjuna complains that Drona had promised no pupil would match him.
shots.B01C134S02H04: Drona goes to Ekalavya, who bows and offers anything as a gift to his teacher; Drona asks for the thumb of his right hand as fee.
shots.B01C134S02H05: Ekalavya cheerfully cuts off his thumb and gives it, and when he shoots again he has lost his skill, so Arjuna is relieved.
shots.B01C134S03H01: The princes are rated in turn: Duryodhana and Bhima with the mace, the twins with the sword, Yudhishthira as a chariot warrior, and Arjuna as the best of all, able to fight sixty thousand foes; the Kauravas grow jealous.
shots.B01C134S03H02: Drona sets an artificial bird atop a tree and orders his pupils to shoot off its head when he gives the signal.
shots.B01C134S03H03: Drona asks Yudhishthira what he sees, and Yudhishthira says he sees the tree, himself, his brothers and the bird, so he is sent aside; the other pupils give the same answer and are sent aside too.

B01C135.summary: Drona tests the princes again, and only Arjuna, who sees just the vulture's head, hits the mark, which delights Drona. Later a crocodile seizes Drona in the Ganga, and Arjuna kills it with arrows. Drona then gives Arjuna the Brahmasira weapon, with a strict warning never to use it against a human, and promises that no bowman will surpass him.

scenes.B01C135S01: Arjuna alone passes Drona's aiming test, and later he saves Drona from a crocodile and receives the Brahmasira weapon.

shots.B01C135S01H02: Drona tests the princes again; only Arjuna, who sees just the vulture's head, is able to shoot it off, and Drona clasps him in delight.
shots.B01C135S01H03: While Drona bathes in the Ganga, a crocodile seizes his thigh; Arjuna kills it with arrows, and Drona gives him the Brahmasira weapon with a warning never to use it on a human foe.
shots.B01C135S01H04: Drona tells Arjuna that no one will surpass him as a bowman and that he will never be defeated.

B01C136.summary: Drona asks Dhritarashtra for permission to show the princes' skill in a public tournament, and the king agrees. The arena, stages and galleries are prepared, and on the day the crowd gathers to watch. The princes display archery, horsemanship and swordsmanship, and then Bhima and Duryodhana enter with maces.

scenes.B01C136S01: Drona asks the king's permission for a public display, the arena is prepared, and on the day the princes show their skill, ending with Bhima and Duryodhana entering with maces.

shots.B01C136S01H02: Drona asks Dhritarashtra for leave to show the princes' skill, the king agrees, and Drona consecrates a cleared field where the stages and galleries are built.
shots.B01C136S01H03: On the day, the king, Bhishma, Kripa, the women of the household and the citizens gather in such numbers that the arena looks like a churning ocean.
shots.B01C136S01H04: Drona, dressed all in white, enters with Aswatthaman; the princes, led by Yudhishthira, show archery and horsemanship, then swordsmanship, and finally Bhima and Duryodhana enter with maces like two warring elephants.

B01C137.summary: The crowd splits between partisans of Duryodhana and of Bhima, and Drona has Aswatthaman restrain the two maces. Drona then presents Arjuna, whose feats with weapons, including conjured fire, water and mountains, delight the spectators and Dhritarashtra. Just as the show winds down, a thunderous sound comes from the gate, and Duryodhana rises with his brothers.

scenes.B01C137S01: The crowd divides between Duryodhana and Bhima partisans, Aswatthaman restrains the maces, and Drona presents Arjuna, whose display of weapons wins delight.
scenes.B01C137S02: As the show is nearly over, a thunder-like sound comes from the gate, and Duryodhana and his brothers rise in haste.

shots.B01C137S01H02: The crowd splits into partisans of Duryodhana and of Bhima, and Drona has Aswatthaman restrain the two maces before the uproar grows.
shots.B01C137S01H03: Drona calls for silence and presents Arjuna, Partha, as the dearest of his pupils, and Arjuna enters the lists in golden mail.
shots.B01C137S01H04: The crowd cheers Arjuna, Kunti weeps with joy, and Dhritarashtra, told by Vidura that Phalguna has entered, rejoices in his sons.
shots.B01C137S01H05: Arjuna conjures fire, water, wind, clouds and mountains with his weapons, makes them vanish, and hits moving targets with great skill, and the crowd calms down.
shots.B01C137S02H01: As the show winds down, a sound like thunder comes from the gate, and the crowd turns to look; Duryodhana rises with his hundred brothers and Aswatthaman.

B01C138.summary: Karna enters the arena and matches Arjuna's feats, and Duryodhana embraces him as a friend. When Arjuna insults him, Karna challenges him, but Kripa asks Karna to name his lineage, since a prince fights only one of royal birth. Duryodhana then makes Karna king of Anga, and the two swear friendship.

scenes.B01C138S01: Karna enters the lists and challenges Arjuna, but Kripa asks for his lineage, and Duryodhana makes him king of Anga.
scenes.B01C138S02: Karna is crowned king of Anga, and he and Duryodhana embrace in friendship.

shots.B01C138S01H02: The narrator says Karna was born to Kunti in her maidenhood, a son of the Sun; he enters the lists, performs Arjuna's feats, and Duryodhana embraces him and welcomes him.
shots.B01C138S01H03: Arjuna, feeling disgraced, tells Karna he will die by his hand; Karna replies that the arena is open to all and offers to answer with arrows.
shots.B01C138S01H04: The two prepare to fight while the sky seems to favour one side or the other, and Kunti swoons and is revived by Vidura; Kripa asks Karna to name his lineage before a prince of royal birth fights him.
shots.B01C138S01H05: Karna is shamed, and Duryodhana proposes making Karna king of Anga, since only kings fight kings.
shots.B01C138S02H01: Karna is crowned king of Anga on a golden seat, promises to do whatever Duryodhana asks, and the two embrace in friendship.

B01C139.summary: Karna's foster father, the charioteer Adhiratha, enters the lists, and Karna bows to him as his father. Bhima mocks Karna as a charioteer's son, and Duryodhana rises to defend him by pointing to the obscure origins of heroes. The sun sets and the crowd disperses, with Kunti pleased to see her son honoured and Duryodhana reassured against Arjuna.

scenes.B01C139S01: Karna's charioteer father Adhiratha comes to the arena, Bhima mocks Karna as a charioteer's son, and Duryodhana defends him at length. The day ends with the crowd dispersing.

shots.B01C139S01H02: Adhiratha enters the lists, perspiring and trembling, leaning on a staff with his sheet hanging loose.
shots.B01C139S01H03: Karna bows to the charioteer, who embraces him as his son in tears; Bhima mocks Karna as a charioteer's son unworthy of Anga, and Duryodhana rises to defend him, citing the unknown origins of heroes like Drona and Kripa.
shots.B01C139S01H04: The sun sets and the crowd, divided in its praise, disperses; Duryodhana leads Karna out, Kunti recognises her son and is pleased, and Duryodhana, freed from fear of Arjuna's skill, relies on Karna.

B01C140.summary: At Drona's demand, the princes attack Drupada's capital to seize him as the fee. After a fierce fight, Drupada is captured by Arjuna, who also stops Bhima from slaughtering the people, and the princes bring him to Drona. Drona humbles his old friend, grants him half his kingdom and asks for friendship, and Drupada, learning that Brahmanical power outmatches his own, begins searching for a son who can defeat Drona.

scenes.B01C140S01: Drona sends the princes against Drupada as his fee; the Kauravas are routed, and the Pandavas advance, and Bhima cuts down Drupada's elephants.
scenes.B01C140S02: Arjuna defeats Drupada's general Satyajit, seizes Drupada himself, and holds back Bhima from killing the Panchala people; the princes bring the captive to Drona.
scenes.B01C140S03: Drona humbles Drupada, gives him half his kingdom and asks for friendship, and Drupada resolves to find a son who can defeat Drona; Drona keeps Ahicchatra.

shots.B01C140S01H02: Drona asks the princes to seize Drupada as their fee, and Duryodhana, Karna, Yuyutsu and the other princes race to attack Drupada's capital.
shots.B01C140S01H03: Drupada comes out with his brothers, and the Kauravas rain arrows on him, but he fires back with force from his white chariot.
shots.B01C140S01H04: Arjuna waits outside the town with his brothers, and Drupada routs the Kauravas, who flee wailing toward the Pandavas.
shots.B01C140S01H05: The Pandavas advance, Bhima strikes down Drupada's elephants with his mace, and the Pandavas drive the Panchala army before them like a herdsman driving cattle.
shots.B01C140S02H01: Arjuna fells Drupada from his elephant and fights fiercely against the Panchalas and Srinjayas.
shots.B01C140S02H02: Arjuna defeats Satyajit by cutting his bows and horses to pieces, then cuts Drupada's bow and flag, leaps onto his chariot, and seizes him, and the Panchala troops flee.
shots.B01C140S02H03: Arjuna asks Bhima to spare the soldiers, since Drupada is a Kuru kinsman, and says they should only deliver the fee to Drona.
shots.B01C140S02H04: Bhima holds back, and the princes bring the captive Drupada to Drona, who humbles him and reminds him of their old friendship.
shots.B01C140S02H05: Drupada says he is moved by Drona's nobility and wants a lasting friendship with him.
shots.B01C140S03H01: Drona frees Drupada, gives him half the kingdom, and Drupada, sorrowful at Kampilya, concludes that Kshatriya might cannot beat Brahmanical power and goes searching for a son to defeat Drona.
shots.B01C140S03H02: Drona settles at Ahicchatra, a territory Arjuna had won and given to him.

B01C141.summary: Dhritarashtra makes Yudhishthira heir apparent for his honesty and patience, and the Pandavas grow strong in their training, with Arjuna excelling in every weapon. Drona reminds Arjuna of the Brahmasira weapon and of his promised fee, and the Pandavas go on to conquer the Sauviras, the Yavanas and kings to the east and south. Dhritarashtra, seeing their power, grows uneasy and cannot sleep.

scenes.B01C141S01: Dhritarashtra names Yudhishthira heir apparent, and the Pandavas grow in skill; Drona reminds Arjuna of his promised fee, and the Pandavas conquer many kingdoms, which leaves Dhritarashtra uneasy.

shots.B01C141S01H02: After a year, Dhritarashtra makes Yudhishthira heir apparent for his honesty and patience; Bhima trains under Balarama, and Arjuna masters every weapon, so that Drona says no one equals him.
shots.B01C141S01H03: Drona recalls the Brahmasira weapon he received from Agnivesa, reminds Arjuna of the fee he owes, and Arjuna pledges to pay it; the Pandavas then defeat the Sauviras, the Yavanas and the kings of the east and south.
shots.B01C141S01H04: Dhritarashtra grows uneasy at the great prowess of the Pandavas, and from that day he can hardly sleep.

B01C142.summary: Dhritarashtra, jealous of the Pandavas' growing might, asks his counsellor Kanika whether he should make peace or war with them. Kanika advises ruthless statecraft: strike foes thoroughly, hide one's own weaknesses, use deceit, gifts and spies, and destroy an enemy's allies as well. He illustrates his advice with a fable of a jackal who tricks his companions out of a deer, and urges the king to act the same way toward the Pandavas.

scenes.B01C142S01: Dhritarashtra asks Kanika whether to make peace or war with the Pandavas, and Kanika gives a long list of ruthless principles of statecraft.
scenes.B01C142S02: Kanika tells the fable of the jackal and the deer, then offers more advice on deceit and spies and urges the king to guard against the Pandavas.

shots.B01C142S01H02: Dhritarashtra, troubled by the Pandavas' growing power, asks his minister Kanika whether he should make peace or war with them.
shots.B01C142S01H03: Kanika, a learned Brahmana skilled in politics, prepares to answer frankly.
shots.B01C142S01H04: Kanika says a king should always be ready to strike, hide his own weaknesses, exploit his foes' weaknesses, destroy enemies root and branch, and win their trust before he attacks.
shots.B01C142S01H05: Dhritarashtra asks how a foe can be destroyed by conciliation, money, division or force.
shots.B01C142S02H01: Kanika tells the fable of a clever jackal who lives with a tiger, mouse, wolf and mongoose, and who, after they kill a deer, turns the tiger against the mouse by reporting a false insult.
shots.B01C142S02H02: The jackal sends the mouse, wolf and mongoose away in turn with half-truths and threats, until only he is left with the carcass.
shots.B01C142S02H03: The jackal eats the deer alone, and Kanika says the timid should be frightened, the courageous won by conciliation, the greedy bought, and equals and inferiors subdued by show of force.
shots.B01C142S02H04: Kanika gives more advice: crush foes by any means, hide anger behind smiles, keep spies in every place, never trust the faithless, and guard the Kuru throne against the Pandavas.
shots.B01C142S02H05: Kanika leaves, and Dhritarashtra is left pensive and melancholy.

B01C143.summary: Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni, with Dhritarashtra's consent, plot to burn Kunti and her sons in a house of lac, but Vidura reads their intent and arranges a boat for escape. The Pandavas get away, a Nishada woman and her children burn in the house along with the architect Purochana, and the people are told the Pandavas have died. Back in the capital the citizens favour Yudhishthira as king, and Duryodhana, alarmed, presses his father to act before the kingdom passes to Pandu's line.

scenes.B01C143S01: Vidura learns of the plot to burn Kunti and her sons, provides a boat for their escape, and the house of lac burns; Janamejaya asks for the full story, and Vaisampayana turns to the citizens' talk of Yudhishthira as king.
