scenes.B01C143S02: Duryodhana, distressed by the citizens' support for Yudhishthira, urges Dhritarashtra to act before the kingdom passes to Pandu's line.

shots.B01C143S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva begins.
shots.B01C143S01H02: Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni, with Dhritarashtra's sanction, plot to burn Kunti and her sons; Vidura reads their intent from their faces, arranges a boat, and urges Kunti to flee.
shots.B01C143S01H03: Kunti and her sons cross the Ganga and enter the forest, while the house of lac burns, killing a Nishada woman, her children and Purochana; the people tell Dhritarashtra he has won, and he puts on a show of mourning.
shots.B01C143S01H04: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana to recite in full the story of the house of lac and the escape, which he sees as a cruel act by the Kurus.
shots.B01C143S01H05: Vaisampayana says Duryodhana grew gloomy at the skill of Bhima and Arjuna, and that the citizens, noting that the blind Dhritarashtra could not rule and Bhishma would not, wanted Yudhishthira crowned.
shots.B01C143S02H01: Duryodhana, jealous and distressed, goes to Dhritarashtra and warns that if Pandu's son inherits the throne, the line of Pandu will keep it, and that the king should act now.

B01C144.summary: Duryodhana urges his father to send the Pandavas away to Varanavata. Dhritarashtra hesitates, since Pandu was virtuous and the elders would never sanction such an exile, but Duryodhana argues that Bhishma will stay neutral and that Drona and Kripa will side with his party. The chapter ends with Duryodhana pressing his father to act that very day.

scenes.B01C144S01: Duryodhana urges that the Pandavas be sent to Varanavata; Dhritarashtra hesitates, citing Pandu's virtue and the elders' disapproval, and Duryodhana argues the elders will not oppose it.

shots.B01C144S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C144S01H02: Dhritarashtra wavers after Kanika's counsel, and Duryodhana urges him to send the Pandavas to Varanavata, but Dhritarashtra recalls Pandu's virtue and the people's loyalty to Yudhishthira.
shots.B01C144S01H03: Duryodhana argues that buying the people with wealth and honours will secure their support, and that the Pandavas can be sent away gently and recalled later.
shots.B01C144S01H04: Dhritarashtra admits the exile is in his mind but calls it sinful, since Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and Kripa would never sanction it and the world would condemn them.
shots.B01C144S01H05: Duryodhana replies that Bhishma will stay neutral, Aswatthaman and Kripa are with him, Vidura depends on them, and he urges the exile to happen that very day.

B01C145.summary: Duryodhana wins the people over with gifts, and Dhritarashtra's councillors lure the Pandavas with tales of a festival of Shiva at Varanavata. Yudhishthira, aware that he is weak and friendless, accepts the king's command, and the elders bless him. The Pandavas then complete their preparations and set out.

scenes.B01C145S01: Duryodhana wins the people over, Dhritarashtra's councillors praise Varanavata to the Pandavas, and the Pandavas set out after receiving the elders' blessings.

shots.B01C145S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C145S01H02: Duryodhana wins the people with wealth and honours, and Dhritarashtra's councillors praise a festival of Shiva at Varanavata, until the Pandavas wish to go and the king tells them to enjoy it.
shots.B01C145S01H03: Yudhishthira, knowing he is weak and friendless, agrees, and asks Bhishma, Vidura, Drona, Kripa, Gandhari and the others for their blessings, which they give.
shots.B01C145S01H04: The Pandavas complete their preparations and set out for Varanavata.

B01C146.summary: Duryodhana, having sent the Pandavas to Varanavata, tells his counsellor Purochana to build a house of lac and inflammable material. Once the Pandavas and Kunti are asleep inside, Purochana is to set it alight so that the deaths look accidental. Purochana obeys and sets off at once.

scenes.B01C146S01: Duryodhana instructs Purochana to build an inflammable house in which to burn the Pandavas, and Purochana sets off at once.

shots.B01C146S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C146S01H02: Duryodhana takes Purochana aside, orders him to build a richly furnished house of flammable materials by the arsenal, and to set it alight once the Pandavas sleep, so the fire looks accidental.
shots.B01C146S01H03: Purochana obeys, travels to Varanavata in a swift car, and carries out Duryodhana's orders.

B01C147.summary: The Pandavas take leave of Bhishma, Dhritarashtra, Drona, Kripa and Vidura, and citizens lament the injustice of their exile, but Yudhishthira asks them to go home. Vidura warns Yudhishthira in a language only the two of them understand that the house is a trap and that they should keep a way out in mind. Kunti asks what Vidura said, Yudhishthira explains the warning, and the Pandavas reach Varanavata.

scenes.B01C147S01: The Pandavas take leave of the elders and citizens, and Vidura secretly warns Yudhishthira in code that the house is a trap.
scenes.B01C147S02: Kunti asks what Vidura said, Yudhishthira explains the warning, and the Pandavas set out for Varanavata.

shots.B01C147S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C147S01H02: The Pandavas take leave of Bhishma, Dhritarashtra, Drona, Kripa, Vidura and the elders, and set out for Varanavata while Vidura and the citizens follow.
shots.B01C147S01H03: Citizens lament the injustice of the exile and offer to follow the Pandavas, but Yudhishthira asks them to go home, obey the king, and bless him.
shots.B01C147S01H04: Vidura speaks to Yudhishthira in a foreign tongue that only he understands, warning him to beware of flammable traps and to keep many exits and his senses under control.
shots.B01C147S01H05: Yudhishthira replies that he understands, Vidura goes home, and Kunti asks Yudhishthira what the two of them said.
shots.B01C147S02H01: Yudhishthira tells Kunti that Vidura warned the house was built of flammable material, that they should know the path of escape, and that those who control their senses can win the world.
shots.B01C147S02H02: The Pandavas set out on the eighth day of Phalguna under the star Rohini and arrive at Varanavata, where they see the town and its people.

B01C148.summary: The citizens of Varanavata welcome the Pandavas, and Purochana lodges them in the palace he has built. After a while Purochana shows them the house he calls the Blessed Home, and Yudhishthira realises it is a flammable trap set by Duryodhana, as Vidura had warned. Bhima wants to leave, but Yudhishthira counsels calm, disguise and a secret escape route.

scenes.B01C148S01: The Pandavas are welcomed and lodged in Purochana's house; Yudhishthira realises it is a trap set by Duryodhana, and he tells Bhima to stay calm and plan a secret escape.

shots.B01C148S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C148S01H02: The citizens welcome the Pandavas with rituals, and they are installed in Purochana's palace with fine food, beds and robes.
shots.B01C148S01H03: After ten nights Purochana shows them the Blessed Home, and Yudhishthira, smelling fat and lac, recognises that the house is made of flammable material and recalls Vidura's warning.
shots.B01C148S01H04: Bhima suggests they go back to their old quarters, but Yudhishthira says they should seem unsuspicious, dig a secret passage, and live in disguise until they can escape.

B01C149.summary: A skilled miner sent by Vidura reveals himself to the Pandavas and warns that Purochana will set their house on fire. Yudhishthira trusts him, and the miner digs a secret passage under the house, covered with planks. The Pandavas keep up a show of contentment, sleeping armed and hunting by day, while preparing to escape.

scenes.B01C149S01: A miner sent by Vidura warns of the fire and digs a secret tunnel under the house while the Pandavas feign contentment.

shots.B01C149S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C149S01H02: A miner sent by Vidura reveals himself and warns of a fire on the fourteenth night of the dark fortnight; Yudhishthira trusts him, and the miner digs a secret passage, covered with planks, while the Pandavas sleep armed and hunt in the forest by day.

B01C150.summary: After a year of apparent calm, Yudhishthira decides the time to escape has come. On a night when Kunti feeds Brahmanas and women, a Nishada woman and her sons sleep drunk inside the house. Bhima sets the house alight where Purochana sleeps, and the Pandavas and Kunti flee through the tunnel, with Bhima carrying them through the darkness.

scenes.B01C150S01: After a year of calm, the Pandavas choose their moment; on the feast night Bhima sets the house on fire, and the family escapes through the tunnel while the citizens watch the blaze.

shots.B01C150S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C150S01H02: Seeing Purochana deceived for a full year, Yudhishthira judges the time to escape has come and proposes burning the arsenal and Purochana and leaving unseen.
shots.B01C150S01H03: At Kunti's almsgiving a Nishada woman and her five sons, drunk, fall asleep in the house; Bhima sets fire to it, and the citizens watching the blaze lament Purochana's wickedness and Dhritarashtra's partiality.
shots.B01C150S01H04: The Pandavas and Kunti enter the tunnel and flee unseen while the citizens wait outside, and Bhima carries his mother and brothers through the dark, breaking trees and treading the earth deep.

B01C151.summary: Vidura's trusted agent finds the Pandavas and Kunti in the forest by the Ganga and shows them a sturdy boat, proving his loyalty by repeating Vidura's coded words. He ferries the family across the river, blesses their journey and goes home. The Pandavas send word back to Vidura and hurry on in secret.

scenes.B01C151S01: Vidura's agent meets the Pandavas by the Ganga, shows them a boat, proves his trustworthiness with Vidura's coded words, and ferries them across.

shots.B01C151S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C151S01H02: Vidura's trusted agent finds the Pandavas and their mother measuring the depth of a river, shows them a sturdy boat, and proves who sent him with Vidura's coded words and his promise that Yudhishthira will defeat Karna and Duryodhana.
shots.B01C151S01H03: The agent takes them into the boat and reminds them, in Vidura's name, not to be careless on their journey.
shots.B01C151S01H04: He ferries them across the Ganga, sees them safe on the far bank, wishes them victory, and returns to his own place.
shots.B01C151S01H05: The Pandavas send a message to Vidura through the agent and hurry on in secret after crossing the river.

B01C152.summary: At dawn the people of Varanavata find the ashes of the house, with Purochana dead, and blame Duryodhana for the plot. Dhritarashtra, told that the Pandavas have perished, mourns them and orders their funeral rites, while Vidura alone does not weep because he knows the truth. Meanwhile the fugitives cross the Ganga and struggle through a dense forest, until Yudhishthira asks Bhima to carry them on.

scenes.B01C152S01: The people of Varanavata find the burnt house and blame Duryodhana, and Dhritarashtra mourns the Pandavas and orders their rites, while Vidura does not weep.
scenes.B01C152S02: The Pandavas cross the Ganga and reach a dense forest, exhausted, and Yudhishthira asks Bhima to carry them on.

shots.B01C152S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C152S01H02: At dawn a crowd comes to the burnt house, finds the lac-built ruins and Purochana dead, and blames Duryodhana, with Dhritarashtra's knowledge, for the murder of the Pandavas.
shots.B01C152S01H03: Searching the ashes, the people find the Nishada woman and her five sons burnt, while Vidura's miner covers his tunnel with ash so that it goes unnoticed.
shots.B01C152S01H04: The citizens report to Dhritarashtra that the Pandavas are dead, and he weeps and orders funeral rites for them and their mother, to be paid for with wealth.
shots.B01C152S01H05: The Kauravas offer water in mourning, calling the Pandavas' names, and the citizens weep, but Vidura does not weep much because he knows the truth.
shots.B01C152S02H01: The six fugitives cross the Ganga with the boatmen's help, then head south by starlight into a dense forest, exhausted and thirsty.
shots.B01C152S02H02: Yudhishthira tells Bhima that they cannot find their way and asks him to carry them, and Bhima takes his mother and brothers on his body and goes swiftly on.

B01C153.summary: Bhima carries his mother and brothers through the forest and rivers until evening, when they reach a wild, waterless place. When Kunti cries out with thirst, Bhima finds a lake and brings water back, then sees his family asleep on the bare ground, laments their fall and rails at Dhritarashtra's sons. He sits up awake to keep watch over them.

scenes.B01C153S01: Bhima carries his family through the forest, fetches water for the thirsty Kunti, laments their hardship, and keeps watch while they sleep.

shots.B01C153S01H01: Heading: the Jatugriha (house of lac) Parva continues.
shots.B01C153S01H02: Bhima forces a path through the forest like a rutting elephant with his mother and brothers on his back, reaches a wild place at evening, fetches water for Kunti from a lake, and laments their fall while threatening Dhritarashtra's sons, held back only by Yudhishthira.
shots.B01C153S01H03: Angry and sorrowful, Bhima sits awake to guard his sleeping mother and brothers, thinking a town must be nearby.

B01C154.summary: A man-eating Rakshasa named Hidimva, perched in a sal tree nearby, smells the sleeping Pandavas and sends his sister to fetch them as food. Instead the Rakshasa woman falls in love with Bhima and offers to help him, and Bhima refuses to abandon his sleeping family. She offers to wake them and save them from her brother.

scenes.B01C154S01: Hidimva sends his sister to fetch the sleepers, but she falls in love with Bhima and offers to help him; Bhima refuses to abandon his family.
scenes.B01C154S02: Bhima tells the Rakshasa woman that he will not wake his family and that Rakshasas cannot match his strength.

shots.B01C154S01H01: Heading: the Hidimva-vadha (slaying of Hidimva) Parva begins.
shots.B01C154S01H02: Hidimva, a grim red-haired man-eater in a sal tree, smells the sleeping Pandavas and orders his sister to bring them to him as food.
shots.B01C154S01H03: The sister finds Bhima awake, falls in love with him, decides to disobey her brother, and offers herself as his wife.
shots.B01C154S01H04: Bhima refuses to leave his sleeping mother and brothers to the Rakshasa or to his own desire.
shots.B01C154S01H05: The Rakshasa woman says she will wake the family and save them from her brother.
shots.B01C154S02H01: Bhima refuses to wake his family while the Rakshasa is near, tells her she may go or send her brother, and says no Rakshasa can match his arms.

B01C155.summary: Hidimva comes down from his tree, sees his sister disguised as a human and infatuated with Bhima, and in rage rushes at her to kill her. Bhima stops him, defends her, and challenges Hidimva to a single combat. The two wrestle fiercely, and the noise wakes the Pandavas, who see Hidimva before them.

scenes.B01C155S01: Hidimva comes down from his tree, sees his sister's infatuation, and rushes to kill her, but Bhima stops him.
scenes.B01C155S02: Bhima challenges Hidimva alone, the two wrestle, and their struggle wakes the Pandavas.

shots.B01C155S01H01: Heading: the Hidimva-vadha (slaying of Hidimva) Parva continues.
shots.B01C155S01H02: The Rakshasa Hidimva comes down from the tree, and his sister, alarmed, asks Bhima to let her carry the family away through the sky.
shots.B01C155S01H03: Bhima tells her not to fear, promises to slay the cannibal before her eyes, and boasts of his arms and chest.
shots.B01C155S01H04: The sister replies that she does not scorn Bhima, but she knows what Rakshasas do to men.
shots.B01C155S01H05: Hidimva sees his sister disguised and smitten, is enraged at her disobedience, and rushes at her to kill her, but Bhima cries out to stop him.
shots.B01C155S02H01: Bhima mocks Hidimva's threat, says his sister is not to blame for desire, and challenges him to single combat.
shots.B01C155S02H02: Hidimva answers that Bhima should prove his strength first, and vows to kill Bhima, then the brothers, then his sister.
shots.B01C155S02H03: Hidimva charges; Bhima seizes his arms and drags him away from the sleepers, and the two fight like rutting elephants, waking the Pandavas, who see Hidimva before them.

B01C156.summary: Kunti questions Hidimva, who explains that she was sent to kill the family but fell in love with Bhima, and that her brother has now come after them. The brothers wake to see Bhima wrestling the Rakshasa, and Arjuna urges him to finish quickly before dawn. Bhima kills Hidimva, and the family hurries off toward a town, with the Rakshasa woman following them.

scenes.B01C156S01: Kunti questions Hidimva, and the brothers wake to see Bhima fighting; Arjuna urges haste, and Bhima kills the Rakshasa.
scenes.B01C156S02: The Pandavas set out with their mother, followed by Hidimva's sister.

shots.B01C156S01H01: Heading: the Hidimva-vadha (slaying of Hidimva) Parva continues.
shots.B01C156S01H02: Kunti is charmed by the Rakshasa woman and asks who she is, and Hidimva explains that her brother was sent to kill them, that she loves Bhima, and that Bhima is now fighting her brother.
shots.B01C156S01H03: The brothers wake to see Bhima and the Rakshasa grappling in the dust; Arjuna offers to help, then urges Bhima to finish before the Rakshasa grows stronger at dawn.
shots.B01C156S01H04: Bhima whirls the Rakshasa in the air a hundred times, rebukes him, and vows to end his man-eating; Arjuna offers help again.
shots.B01C156S01H05: Bhima dashes Hidimva to the ground and kills him, then breaks the body in two, and his brothers praise him and urge that they leave before Duryodhana finds them.
shots.B01C156S02H01: The Pandavas and their mother set out, and Hidimva's sister follows them.

B01C157.summary: Bhima threatens Hidimva's sister, but Yudhishthira forbids him to harm a woman. Hidimva humbly begs Kunti and Yudhishthira to let her marry Bhima, and Yudhishthira agrees on condition that she bring him back each night. After wandering the world with Hidimva, Bhima fathers a son, Ghatotkacha, who is bald and fierce but loyal to the Pandavas, and Hidimva and the boy take their leave.

scenes.B01C157S01: Yudhishthira stops Bhima from harming Hidimva's sister, who begs to marry him; Bhima agrees to stay with her until she bears a son, and Ghatotkacha is born.
scenes.B01C157S02: Hidimva and her son Ghatotkacha take their leave of the Pandavas.

shots.B01C157S01H01: Heading: the Hidimva-vadha (slaying of Hidimva) Parva continues.
shots.B01C157S01H02: Bhima warns the Rakshasa woman to follow her brother, but Yudhishthira stops him from harming a woman, since her brother is already dead.
shots.B01C157S01H03: Hidimva humbly asks Kunti and Yudhishthira to let her have Bhima as her husband, pleading that she will serve them and carry them through dangers.
shots.B01C157S01H04: Yudhishthira agrees, on condition that Bhima attend to her during the day and that she bring him back to the family each nightfall.
shots.B01C157S01H05: Bhima agrees to stay with her until she has a son; Hidimva carries him through many regions until she bears Ghatotkacha, a bald, fierce child who grows up quickly and becomes devoted to the Pandavas.
shots.B01C157S02H01: Hidimva takes leave, Ghatotkacha promises his father to come when needed and goes north, and the narrator says Indra made Ghatotkacha as a match for Karna's dart.

B01C158.summary: The Pandavas wander through forests and lands of the Matsyas, Trigartas and Panchalas, living disguised as ascetics and studying the Vedas. They meet their grandfather Vyasa, who tells them their exile is for their good and not to grieve. He leads them to the town of Ekachakra and predicts that Yudhishthira will one day rule the earth, and then he departs.

scenes.B01C158S01: The Pandavas wander disguised through the lands, meet Vyasa, and are led to Ekachakra, where Vyasa predicts a great future for Yudhishthira.
scenes.B01C158S02: The Pandavas agree to wait for Vyasa, and he goes back to his home.

shots.B01C158S01H01: Heading: the Hidimva-vadha (slaying of Hidimva) Parva continues.
shots.B01C158S01H02: The Pandavas travel in disguise through the lands of the Matsyas, Trigartas, Panchalas and Kichakas, sometimes carrying their mother, studying the Vedas, and then meet their grandfather Vyasa.
shots.B01C158S01H03: Vyasa says he foresaw their exile, that it is meant for their happiness, and tells them to wait in disguise in a nearby town until he returns.
shots.B01C158S01H04: Vyasa leads them to Ekachakra and comforts Kunti by predicting that Yudhishthira will rule the earth and that the brothers will perform great sacrifices.
shots.B01C158S01H05: Vyasa places the Pandavas in the house of a Brahmana and tells Yudhishthira to wait for him, adding that they will be happy if they adapt to the country.
shots.B01C158S02H01: The Pandavas agree, and Vyasa returns to the place he came from.

B01C159.summary: At Ekachakra the Pandavas live on alms, which Kunti divides among them. One day, when only Bhima is at home with Kunti, they hear a Brahmana family lamenting, and Kunti resolves to help them. The Brahmana laments that he cannot escape the calamity or give up any of his family, and he is ready to die with them.

scenes.B01C159S01: The Pandavas live by alms at Ekachakra; while Bhima is at home, Kunti hears a Brahmana household wailing and asks Bhima to help.
scenes.B01C159S02: The Brahmana, his wife, son and daughter lament their helplessness and speak of dying together.

shots.B01C159S01H01: Heading: the Vaka-vadha (slaying of Vaka) Parva begins.
shots.B01C159S01H02: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after arriving at Ekachakra.
shots.B01C159S01H03: The Pandavas live by alms and win the townspeople's favour, and Kunti divides the food they bring into two shares, one for herself and her sons and one for Bhima.
shots.B01C159S01H04: One day, while the brothers are out begging, Kunti hears a heart-rending wail from the Brahmana's house and feels compelled to help, since they are living under his roof.
shots.B01C159S01H05: Bhima tells his mother to learn the cause of the Brahmana's distress, and promises to relieve it however hard the task may be.
shots.B01C159S02H01: Kunti enters and finds the Brahmana with his wife, son and daughter in despair; he laments the emptiness of life and his inability to give up any of them, so he thinks of dying with them.

B01C160.summary: The Brahmana's wife tells him not to mourn, since all must die, and offers to go to the Rakshasa in his place. She argues that her husband's life and their children's future matter more, and that he may take another wife. The Brahmana embraces her, and the two weep together in silence.

scenes.B01C160S01: The Brahmana's wife offers to go to the Rakshasa in his place, and the couple weep together in silence.

shots.B01C160S01H01: Heading: the Vaka-vadha (slaying of Vaka) Parva continues.
shots.B01C160S01H02: The Brahmana's wife tells him not to mourn, says death is inevitable, and offers herself to the Rakshasa, arguing that her husband and their children must be saved.
shots.B01C160S01H03: The Brahmana embraces his wife, and the two weep together in silence.

B01C161.summary: The daughter asks her parents to give her up, arguing that her sacrifice can rescue the family and that she would otherwise be a helpless burden. The little son cheers them with a playful threat to slay the Rakshasa with a blade of grass. Kunti then steps forward, and her words revive the family as nectar revives the dead.

scenes.B01C161S01: The daughter urges her parents to sacrifice her, the little son makes them smile, and Kunti steps forward to speak to them.

shots.B01C161S01H01: Heading: the Vaka-vadha (slaying of Vaka) Parva continues.
shots.B01C161S01H02: The daughter asks her parents to stop weeping and offers herself, likening herself to a raft that can carry them across their troubles.
shots.B01C161S01H03: The little son, lisping sweetly, tells his parents and sister not to weep and says he will slay the man-eating Rakshasa with a blade of grass; their faces brighten, and Kunti steps in.

B01C162.summary: Kunti asks the Brahmana the cause of his grief and offers to remove it. He explains that the Rakshasa Vaka rules the region and is fed in turn by each household with a cart of rice, two buffaloes and a man, and that his family's turn has now come. He has no money to buy a substitute and sees no escape, so he plans to go to the Rakshasa with his whole family.

scenes.B01C162S01: Kunti asks the cause of the Brahmana's grief, and he explains the tribute owed to the Rakshasa Vaka and his plan to go with his family.

shots.B01C162S01H01: Heading: the Vaka-vadha (slaying of Vaka) Parva continues.
shots.B01C162S01H02: Kunti asks the Brahmana to tell her the cause of his grief, promising to remove it if she can.
shots.B01C162S01H03: The Brahmana explains that the man-eater Vaka is fed in turn by each household with rice, buffaloes and a man, that his family's turn has come, and that with no money for a substitute he will take his whole family to be devoured.

B01C163.summary: Kunti offers to send one of her five sons to the Rakshasa in the Brahmana's place, since his son and daughter are too young. The Brahmana refuses to let anyone die in his stead, saying he would rather die himself than sacrifice a Brahmana or a guest. Kunti assures him that her son Bhima is mighty enough to deliver the tribute and save himself, and Bhima agrees to go.

scenes.B01C163S01: Kunti offers one of her sons, the Brahmana refuses to let anyone die for him, Kunti promises her son's strength, and Bhima agrees to go.

shots.B01C163S01H01: Heading: the Vaka-vadha (slaying of Vaka) Parva continues.
shots.B01C163S01H02: Kunti tells the Brahmana not to grieve, since she has five sons and will send one of them with the tribute, because his children are too young.
shots.B01C163S01H03: The Brahmana refuses, saying he will never sacrifice a Brahmana or a guest to save himself, and that he would rather die himself.
shots.B01C163S01H04: Kunti replies that she values Brahmanas, and that her son Bhima, endowed with great might and mantras, will deliver the food and save himself, and asks the Brahmana to keep this secret.
shots.B01C163S01H05: The Brahmana, relieved, accepts, and Kunti takes the matter to Bhima, who says so be it.

B01C164.summary: Bhima pledges to take on the task, and Yudhishthira, reading the matter from Bhima's face, asks his mother what has been arranged. Kunti explains that Bhima will go to save the Brahmana and the town. Yudhishthira objects that the plan is reckless and against the Vedas, and that the family depends on Bhima's strength, but Kunti answers that the Brahmana deserves repayment and that Bhima's might has already been proved.

scenes.B01C164S01: Yudhishthira objects to Kunti's plan to send Bhima to the Rakshasa; Kunti defends it by pointing to Bhima's strength and the debt owed to the Brahmana.

shots.B01C164S01H01: Heading: the Vaka-vadha (slaying of Vaka) Parva continues.
shots.B01C164S01H02: Bhima pledges to do the task, and the brothers return with the day's alms; Yudhishthira, reading the matter from Bhima's face, asks his mother privately what task Bhima has taken on.
shots.B01C164S01H03: Yudhishthira calls the plan rash and almost suicidal, condemns sacrificing one's child against custom and the Vedas, and reminds Kunti that the family's hopes rest on Bhima's arms.
shots.B01C164S01H04: Kunti replies that her judgement is sound, that she is repaying the Brahmana's kindness, that Bhima's might was proved at the house of lac and against Hidimva, and that Kshatriyas must protect Brahmanas, as Vyasa taught.

B01C165.summary: Yudhishthira accepts that Kunti acted from compassion and trusts Bhima to win. That night Bhima carries the Rakshasa's tribute into the forest and eats it in full view of Vaka, who charges in fury. The two fight with trees and wrestle until Bhima bends Vaka double over his knee, and Vaka begins to vomit blood.

scenes.B01C165S01: Yudhishthira approves of the plan, and Bhima takes the tribute to Vaka's forest, where a long fight breaks out.

shots.B01C165S01H01: Heading: the Vaka-vadha (slaying of Vaka) Parva continues.
shots.B01C165S01H02: Yudhishthira says Kunti's compassion is admirable and that Bhima will surely return alive, but asks that the Brahmana keep the arrangement secret from the townspeople.
shots.B01C165S01H03: At night Bhima carries the food into the forest, begins to eat it, and calls the Rakshasa by name, and Vaka comes out in rage.
shots.B01C165S01H04: Vaka, huge and red-haired, rushes at Bhima, who keeps eating unperturbed; the two hurl trees at each other, Bhima wrestles him down, bends him double over his knee, and Vaka begins to vomit blood.

B01C166.summary: Bhima kills Vaka and makes the Rakshasa's kin promise to stop eating men, then leaves the body at the town gate. When the townspeople find it, the host Brahmana says a Brahmana skilled in mantras had taken the food to the forest and done the deed, which keeps the Pandavas hidden. The town marks the event with a festival honouring Brahmanas.

scenes.B01C166S01: Bhima makes Vaka's kin promise to stop eating men, the townspeople find the body, and the host Brahmana credits an unnamed Brahmana with the killing to protect the Pandavas.

shots.B01C166S01H01: Heading: the Vaka-vadha (slaying of Vaka) Parva continues.
shots.B01C166S01H02: Bhima comforts Vaka's terrified kin and makes them promise never to kill human beings again, then drags the corpse to a town gate and leaves unseen.
shots.B01C166S01H03: Bhima tells Yudhishthira everything; the next morning the people find the mangled Rakshasa, and their Brahmana host says a Brahmana skilled in mantras took the food to the forest and did the deed.
shots.B01C166S01H04: The Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras hold a festival in which the worship of Brahmanas is the main ceremony.

B01C167.summary: The Pandavas stay on at Ekachakra, and a visiting Brahmana tells them of distant lands, shrines and the wonders of Drupada's sacrifice, including the birth of Draupadi. The Pandavas ask for the full story of how Dhrishtadyumna and Draupadi were born and how Drona and Drupada became enemies. The Brahmana begins to recount Draupadi's birth.

scenes.B01C167S01: The Pandavas stay on at Ekachakra, Janamejaya asks what they did next, and a visiting Brahmana tells them of distant lands and of Draupadi's birth.
scenes.B01C167S02: The Pandavas ask the Brahmana for the details of the births and of the broken friendship, and he begins his account of Draupadi's birth.

shots.B01C167S01H02: The citizens go home, and the Pandavas stay at Ekachakra as before.
shots.B01C167S01H03: Janamejaya asks the Brahmana what the tigers among men did after slaying Vaka.
shots.B01C167S01H04: The question ends by naming the Pandavas and Vaka's death.
shots.B01C167S01H05: Vaisampayana says a visiting Brahmana of rigid vows lodges with their host, and at the Pandavas' request he tells of lands and shrines, and of Draupadi and Dhrishtadyumna's births at Drupada's sacrifice.
shots.B01C167S02H01: The Pandavas ask how Dhrishtadyumna and Krishna were born, how Drupada's son learned all weapons from Drona, and why the friendship between Drona and Drupada broke off.
shots.B01C167S02H02: Vaisampayana says the Brahmana then began to tell all the particulars of Draupadi's birth.

B01C168.summary: The visiting Brahmana tells how Drona was born from Bharadwaja's seed in a pot and grew up as the boyhood friend of Drupada, son of Prishata. After Drona receives Rama's weapons, Drupada scorns his claim to friendship, and Drona later has the Pandavas capture Drupada as his fee. The humbled Drupada accepts Drona's terms and makes peace, but he never forgets the humiliation.

scenes.B01C168S01: The Brahmana narrates Drona's birth, his boyhood friendship with Drupada, Drupada's scorn, and the Pandavas' capture of Drupada as fee.

shots.B01C168S01H02: The Brahmana recounts Drona's birth from Bharadwaja's seed caught in a pot, his boyhood friendship with Drupada, and his journey to Rama to ask for weapons.
shots.B01C168S01H03: Rama gives Drona all his weapons; Drona then goes to Drupada, asks to be his friend, and is scorned by him as unworthy.
shots.B01C168S01H04: Humiliated, Drona takes up the Kuru princes as pupils, sets them to capture Drupada as his fee, and divides Drupada's kingdom between them.
shots.B01C168S01H05: The defeated Drupada accepts a bond of friendship and returns home, but the humiliation stays with him and he begins to waste away.

B01C169.summary: Drupada, bent on revenge, seeks a sacrifice that will give him a son to kill Drona. After Upayaja refuses, his brother Yaja, promised a large reward, performs the rite, and from the sacrificial fire come a son, Dhrishtadyumna, destined to slay Drona, and a dark, beautiful daughter, Krishna. An unseen voice foretells that Krishna will be the foremost of women and the cause of many Kshatriyas' deaths, and Drona trains Dhrishtadyumna in arms.

scenes.B01C169S01: Drupada courts the sages Yaja and Upayaja to get a Drona-slayer, and Yaja's sacrifice produces Dhrishtadyumna and Krishna, and Drona trains the prince.

shots.B01C169S01H02: Drupada, despondent that his children lack accomplishment and bent on revenge, courts the sages Yaja and Upayaja; Upayaja at first refuses the sacrifice and then points him to his greedy brother Yaja, who agrees for a great fee.
shots.B01C169S01H03: Yaja pours the oblation, and when the queen asks to wait, he refuses, since the offering is already prepared and consecrated.
shots.B01C169S01H04: From the fire rises an armoured, crowned son destined to slay Drona, followed by a dark-complexioned, beautiful daughter; an unseen voice says the girl will cause many Kshatriyas to die, and the Brahmanas name them Dhrishtadyumna and Krishna.
shots.B01C169S01H05: Drona takes the prince as a pupil and teaches him all weapons, in return for the half of Drupada's kingdom he took earlier, and the narrator notes that Drona accepts destiny.

B01C170.summary: The Pandavas are deeply troubled by the Brahmana's tale. Kunti proposes that they leave Ekachakra, since they have seen all its sights and alms are harder to get, and suggests going to Panchala, where King Yajnasena is generous to Brahmanas. Yudhishthira agrees that they must obey, but wonders whether his younger brothers will want to go.

scenes.B01C170S01: Kunti proposes leaving Ekachakra for Panchala, and Yudhishthira agrees but asks whether his younger brothers will consent.

shots.B01C170S01H02: The Pandavas are unsettled by the Brahmana's tale, and Kunti suggests they leave for Panchala, where alms are plentiful and the king is devoted to Brahmanas.
shots.B01C170S01H03: Yudhishthira agrees that his mother's command is for their good, but wonders whether his younger brothers will be willing.

B01C171.summary: The Pandavas agree to Kunti's plan and leave Ekachakra for Panchala. Before they go, Vyasa visits them and tells of a maiden who, in a past life, prayed to Shiva for a husband and was promised five husbands, so that Draupadi, born in Drupada's line, is to be the wife of all five brothers. Vyasa bids them farewell and departs.

scenes.B01C171S01: The Pandavas set out for Panchala, and Vyasa visits them to foretell Draupadi's marriage to all five brothers, then departs.

shots.B01C171S01H02: Kunti tells her sons of the plan, they agree, and the family takes leave of their host and sets out for Drupada's city.
shots.B01C171S01H03: Vyasa visits the Pandavas, asks whether they keep the law and honour Brahmanas, and tells of a maiden who was promised five husbands by Shiva, so Draupadi of Drupada's line is to be the wife of all five; he urges them to go to Panchala.
shots.B01C171S01H04: Vyasa blesses the Pandavas and departs for his own place.

B01C172.summary: On the way to Panchala the Pandavas reach the Ganga, where the proud Gandharva Angaraparna bars their path, claiming the river at that hour belongs to the Gandharvas and the Rakshasas. Arjuna refuses to yield, and after a fiery weapon burns the Gandharva's chariot, he drags him away, but Yudhishthira spares him at his wife's plea. The grateful Gandharva offers Arjuna a science of illusion and a hundred swift horses, and explains that the Pandavas were rebuked for travelling at night without wives or a priest.

scenes.B01C172S01: The Gandharva Angaraparna bars the Pandavas at the Ganga; Arjuna defeats him with a fiery weapon, and Yudhishthira orders mercy at his wife's plea.
scenes.B01C172S02: The grateful Gandharva offers Arjuna a science of illusion and horses in exchange for his fire weapon, and explains why he rebuked the Pandavas.

shots.B01C172S01H02: The Pandavas walk north toward Panchala, Arjuna leading with a torch, and reach the Ganga, where the Gandharva Angaraparna, bathing with his wives, boasts of his strength and orders them away.
shots.B01C172S01H03: Arjuna retorts that no one can bar people from the sacred Ganga, which flows to the sea and purifies all who bathe in it.
shots.B01C172S01H04: The Gandharva shoots arrows at the Pandavas, Arjuna shields himself and answers that he will fight with a celestial weapon, the fiery weapon passed down from Vrihaspati to Drona.
shots.B01C172S01H05: Arjuna hurls the fire weapon, burning the Gandharva's chariot, then drags him by the hair; his wife Kumbhinasi begs for mercy, and Yudhishthira, seeing a defeated foe under a woman's protection, orders Arjuna to spare him.
shots.B01C172S02H01: The Gandharva acknowledges defeat, gives up his old name, and offers Arjuna his science of illusion, called Chakshushi, and a hundred Gandharva horses, explaining the thunderbolt's fragments that make a warrior's strength.
shots.B01C172S02H02: A section marker begins Section CLXXIII.
shots.B01C172S02H03: Arjuna says he will not accept the gifts for free, and the Gandharva asks in exchange for Arjuna's fiery weapon.
shots.B01C172S02H04: Arjuna accepts the horses in exchange for his weapon, asks why the Gandharva rebuked them at night, and wants a lasting friendship.
shots.B01C172S02H05: The Gandharva says the Pandavas travelled without wives or a priest, that he knows their ancestors, and that a king with a priest prevails and the realm lasts where Brahmanas hold power.

B01C173.summary: Arjuna asks why the Gandharva calls them Tapatyas, and the Gandharva explains through the story of Tapati, the Sun's daughter, whom no one in the three worlds equals in beauty. The Sun chooses King Samvarana, a devout worshipper, as her husband. When Samvarana's horse dies on a hunt in the hills, he sees Tapati and is struck with desire, and he asks who she is.

scenes.B01C173S01: Arjuna asks about the name Tapatyas, and the Gandharva tells how the Sun chose King Samvarana for his daughter Tapati, and how the king came upon her in the hills.
scenes.B01C173S02: Samvarana declares his desire and asks Tapati's name, but she vanishes, and the king wanders in grief.

shots.B01C173S01H02: Arjuna asks what the name Tapatya means, since his family is called Kaunteya and not after Tapati.
shots.B01C173S01H03: The Gandharva agrees to tell the story, which is well known throughout the three worlds.
shots.B01C173S01H04: The Gandharva says Tapati, daughter of the Sun and younger sister of Savitri, has no equal in beauty, and the Sun chooses King Samvarana, a devoted worshipper of him, as her husband.
shots.B01C173S01H05: While hunting in the mountains, Samvarana's horse dies of exhaustion, and on foot he comes upon Tapati, who shines like gold, and is struck with desire.
shots.B01C173S02H01: Burning with desire, the king asks the maiden who she is and whose she is, praises her beauty, and says Kama is tormenting him.
shots.B01C173S02H02: Tapati says nothing and vanishes like lightning, and the king searches the forest in a daze, lamenting and standing motionless in grief.

B01C174.summary: Tapati reappears and gently tells the king to rise, and he pours out his passion and begs her to accept him. She replies that she is under her father's control, so he must ask the Sun for her hand with worship and vows. She then names herself as the Sun's daughter and Savitri's younger sister.

scenes.B01C174S01: Tapati reappears, the king declares his passion, and Tapati tells him to ask her father, the Sun, for her hand.

shots.B01C174S01H02: Tapati reappears and gently tells the fallen king to rise, and the king begs her in passionate words to accept him and to wed him in the Gandharva form.
shots.B01C174S01H03: Tapati replies that she is under her father's control, so the king should ask the Sun for her hand with worship and penance, and she names herself as Tapati, Savitri's younger sister and the Sun's daughter.

B01C175.summary: Samvarana, revived by his minister, worships the Sun, and his priest Vasishtha asks the Sun for Tapati's hand on his behalf. The Sun consents, and the couple live together on the mountain for twelve years, until a long drought ravages the kingdom and Vasishtha brings the king home to end it. The Gandharva explains that Arjuna is called Tapatya because Samvarana's son Kuru was born of Tapati.

scenes.B01C175S01: Samvarana is revived and worships the Sun, Vasishtha wins Tapati for him, and when a drought strikes Vasishtha brings the couple home and the rains return; the Gandharva then explains why Arjuna is called Tapatya.

shots.B01C175S01H02: Samvarana, revived by his minister, worships the Sun; Vasishtha goes to the Sun, asks for Tapati on the king's behalf, and after the marriage on the mountain the couple live together twelve years, until a long drought is ended when Vasishtha brings the king home and the rains return.
shots.B01C175S01H03: The Gandharva says this is the history of Tapati, and that Arjuna is called Tapatya because Samvarana's son Kuru was born of her.

B01C176.summary: Moved by the story, Arjuna asks about Vasishtha. The Gandharva describes Vasishtha as Brahma's mind-born son and the family priest of Arjuna's forebears, whose ascetic power outmatched even Desire and Wrath. He urges the Pandavas to choose a learned Brahmana as their priest, since a Kshatriya needs one to conquer the earth.

scenes.B01C176S01: Arjuna asks about Vasishtha, and the Gandharva describes his power and urges the Pandavas to appoint a learned priest.

shots.B01C176S01H02: Arjuna asks about Vasishtha, and the Gandharva describes him as Brahma's mind-born son and the family priest of the Pandavas' forebears, whose austerity overcame Desire and Wrath, and urges them to choose a learned Brahmana as their priest.

B01C177.summary: The Gandharva tells the old feud between Vasishtha and the king Viswamitra, who coveted Vasishtha's wish-granting cow Nandini and offered a kingdom for her. When Viswamitra seized the cow, Nandini produced armies of barbarians from her body and routed his troops. Humbled, Viswamitra renounced his kingdom and set out to win Brahmanhood through austerity.

scenes.B01C177S01: Arjuna asks about the feud, and the Gandharva tells how Viswamitra, after a visit to Vasishtha's hermitage, coveted the wish-granting cow Nandini and offered a kingdom for her.
scenes.B01C177S02: Viswamitra seizes Nandini by force, and Vasishtha, bound by his forgiving vow, leaves the cow to resist for herself.
scenes.B01C177S03: Nandini routs Viswamitra's army with barbarian troops from her body, and Viswamitra renounces power and becomes a Brahmana through austerity.

shots.B01C177S01H02: Arjuna asks what caused the hostility between Viswamitra and Vasishtha, who both dwelt in a celestial hermitage.
shots.B01C177S01H03: The Gandharva tells how Viswamitra, son of King Gadhi, came weary from hunting to Vasishtha's hermitage, where he was fed with food and drink from Nandini, the wish-granting cow.
shots.B01C177S01H04: Viswamitra asks Vasishtha to give him Nandini in exchange for ten thousand cows or his kingdom.
shots.B01C177S01H05: Vasishtha refuses, since the cow is kept for the gods, guests, the ancestors and sacrifices, and Viswamitra says he will take her by force.
shots.B01C177S02H01: Vasishtha tells the king to act at once without concern for propriety, since he is a powerful Kshatriya.
shots.B01C177S02H02: Viswamitra seizes Nandini and beats her, and she lows piteously and goes back to Vasishtha's hermitage, refusing to leave it.
shots.B01C177S02H03: Vasishtha, seeing her plight, speaks to the cow.
shots.B01C177S02H04: He says he hears her cries, but that Viswamitra is carrying her off by force.
shots.B01C177S02H05: He says he can do nothing about it, as a forgiving Brahmana.
shots.B01C177S03H01: He asks what he can do, since he is a forgiving Brahmana.
shots.B01C177S03H02: Nandini protests that he is casting her off, and Vasishtha replies that she may stay if she can, pointing to her calf tied with a stout cord nearby.
shots.B01C177S03H03: Nandini rages, sending out armies of Palhavas, Dravidas, Sakas, Yavanas and many other tribes from her body, and routs Viswamitra's army; Viswamitra says the Brahmana's power is true strength, renounces his kingdom, and becomes a Brahmana who drinks Soma with Indra.

B01C178.summary: The Gandharva tells of King Kalmashapada, who strikes the sage Shakti, Vasishtha's eldest son, with a whip when neither will yield on a forest path, and is cursed to become a man-eating Rakshasa. Viswamitra, who had wanted the king as his disciple, secretly has a Rakshasa enter him, and the possessed king serves human flesh to a hungry Brahmana, earning a second curse. The king then kills and devours Shakti and his brothers, and Vasishtha, grief-stricken, tries again and again to end his life.

scenes.B01C178S01: Kalmashapada and Shakti clash on a forest path; Shakti curses the king, Viswamitra possesses him with a Rakshasa, and the king's cook serves human flesh to a Brahmana, who curses him again.
scenes.B01C178S02: The possessed king devours Shakti and the other sons, and Vasishtha tries to kill himself by several means, all of which fail.

shots.B01C178S01H02: King Kalmashapada of the Ikshvaku line hunts in the forest, killing deer, boars and rhinoceroses, and tires, and gives up the chase to rest.
shots.B01C178S01H03: On a forest path he meets Shakti, Vasishtha's eldest son; neither will yield, the king strikes him with a whip, Shakti curses him to become a man-eating Rakshasa, and Viswamitra, who had wanted the king as his disciple, sends a Rakshasa named Kinkara to possess him.
shots.B01C178S01H04: The possessed king, having forgotten his promise to a hungry Brahmana, sends his cook to feed him with meat.
shots.B01C178S01H05: The cook, finding no meat, serves human flesh, and the Brahmana, seeing it is unholy, curses the king to become fond of such food and wander the earth as a man-eater.
shots.B01C178S02H01: The possessed king kills and devours Shakti, the Rakshasa, urged on by Viswamitra, devours Vasishtha's other sons, and Vasishtha, grieving, throws himself from Meru, into fire and into the sea, but cannot die, and returns to his hermitage.

B01C179.summary: Vasishtha, bereft of his sons, tries to drown himself in rivers, but each current casts him ashore, and the rivers are renamed after his failed attempts. He learns from his daughter-in-law Adrisyanti that she is carrying a child by his son Shakti, and so he gives up his plan to die. He then frees the Rakshasa-possessed King Kalmashapada, who asks for a son to continue his line, and the queen eventually bears Asmaka after twelve years.

scenes.B01C179S01: Vasishtha tries to end his life in rivers, learns from Adrisyanti that she carries Shakti's child, and frees Kalmashapada, who asks for an heir, which Vasishtha grants.

shots.B01C179S01H02: Grieving over his lost sons, Vasishtha ties himself with cords and throws himself into flooded rivers, but the currents break the cords and cast him ashore; the rivers are named for his failure, and he cannot die.
shots.B01C179S01H03: Hearing the Vedas recited behind him, Vasishtha learns from his daughter-in-law Adrisyanti that she is carrying Shakti's child, and he refrains from self-destruction; then he meets the Rakshasa-possessed King Kalmashapada, who is about to devour him.
shots.B01C179S01H04: Vasishtha restrains the king with a sacred sound and sanctified water, freeing him from the curse, and the king asks for a son to carry on the Ikshvaku line.
shots.B01C179S01H05: Vasishtha agrees, goes to the king's capital Ayodhya, and beds the queen; after twelve years of pregnancy the queen tears open her womb and Asmaka is born, the founder of Paudanya.

B01C180.summary: Adrisyanti bears a son, Parasara, whom Vasishtha raises as his grandson. When the boy calls Vasishtha father, his mother corrects him, and he resolves to destroy the world. To turn him from this, Vasishtha tells how the Kshatriyas slaughtered the Bhrigus after a hidden treasure was found, and how a Bhrigu woman's unborn son burst from her thigh to avenge them.

scenes.B01C180S01: Parasara is born, calls Vasishtha father, and resolves to destroy the world; Vasishtha begins to dissuade him by telling the story of the Bhrigus and the Kshatriyas.

shots.B01C180S01H02: Adrisyanti bears Parasara, a second Shakti, whom Vasishtha raises; when the boy calls Vasishtha father, his mother corrects him, and in grief and anger he resolves to destroy the world.
shots.B01C180S01H03: Vasishtha tells how the descendants of King Kritavirya begged from the Bhrigus, found the treasure the Bhrigus had hidden, and then slaughtered the Bhrigus, even their unborn children, until a Bhrigu woman's son burst from her thigh and blinded the Kshatriyas.

B01C181.summary: The Bhrigu woman tells the blinded Kshatriyas that her unborn son, held in her thigh for a hundred years, blinded them to avenge his slaughtered race, and that they must propitiate him. The thigh-born child, named Aurva, restores their sight, but he resolves to destroy the whole world in revenge. The Pitris come to beg him to restrain his wrath.

scenes.B01C181S01: The Bhrigu woman tells the Kshatriyas that her son blinded them; Aurva restores their sight but resolves on destruction, until the Pitris beg him to restrain his wrath.

shots.B01C181S01H02: The Bhrigu woman tells the Kshatriyas she did not blind them, but her unborn son, held in her thigh for a hundred years, was angered by their slaughter of his race and has blinded them, so they must propitiate him.
shots.B01C181S01H03: The Kshatriyas propitiate the child, who is named Aurva for being born from the thigh and restores their sight; Aurva then sets out to destroy the whole world through severe austerity to avenge his ancestors.
shots.B01C181S01H04: The Pitris come to Aurva and beg him to restrain his wrath, explaining that the Bhrigus had let themselves be slain by choice and that he should not destroy the Kshatriyas or the worlds.

B01C182.summary: Aurva refuses to give up his vow, arguing that kings failed to protect the Bhrigus and that his anger must be satisfied. The Pitris advise him to cast the fire of his wrath into the waters, and he throws it into the ocean, where it becomes the horse-headed fire Vadavamukha that still consumes the sea. Vasishtha then urges Parasara to give up his own plan to destroy the world.

scenes.B01C182S01: Aurva defends his wrath, the Pitris suggest he cast it into the sea, and Aurva does so, which Vasishtha offers as a lesson to Parasara.

shots.B01C182S01H02: The Gandharva says Vasishtha goes on with the story, telling how Aurva replied to the Pitris.
shots.B01C182S01H03: Aurva answers that his vow cannot be undone, that wrath is useful to restrain the wicked, and that kings failed to protect the Bhrigus, so his fire must consume the worlds unless he finds a way to quench it.
shots.B01C182S01H04: The Pitris advise him to throw his wrath into the waters, since the worlds depend on water and his fire can be contained in the great ocean.
shots.B01C182S01H05: Aurva casts the fire into the ocean, where it becomes the horse-headed fire Vadavamukha that consumes the sea, and Vasishtha tells Parasara not to destroy the worlds.

B01C183.summary: Parasara, persuaded to restrain his wrath toward the worlds, nevertheless begins a Rakshasa sacrifice to avenge his father Shakti, and Vasishtha does not stop him. The sages Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu come to halt the rite, and Pulastya says Shakti brought his death on himself and that the Rakshasas are innocent. Parasara ends the sacrifice and casts its fire into the northern forest.

scenes.B01C183S01: Parasara begins a sacrifice to destroy the Rakshasas in revenge; the sages urge him to stop, and he ends the rite and casts its fire into the north.

shots.B01C183S01H02: Parasara, restrained from destroying the worlds, performs a grand Rakshasa sacrifice to avenge Shakti, while Vasishtha does not stop him, and he sits like a fourth fire among three blazing ones.
shots.B01C183S01H03: Sages Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu come to save the Rakshasas, and Pulastya tells Parasara that Shakti brought on his own death, that the Rakshasas are innocent, and that he should end the sacrifice.
shots.B01C183S01H04: Persuaded by Pulastya and Vasishtha, Parasara ends the sacrifice and casts its fire into the deep woods north of the Himalayas, where it still burns Rakshasas and trees.

B01C184.summary: Arjuna asks why King Kalmashapada sent his queen to Vasishtha, and whether Vasishtha sinned in lying with her. The Gandharva explains that the cursed king devoured a Brahmana while his wife wept, and she cursed him to die when he approached his queen and to father a child on her by Vasishtha. Remembering the curse after his queen sent him away, the king repented and asked Vasishtha to beget an heir.

scenes.B01C184S01: Arjuna asks about the queen's union with Vasishtha, and the Gandharva tells of the Brahmani's curse and the king's repentance and request for an heir.

shots.B01C184S01H02: Arjuna asks why King Kalmashapada sent his queen to Vasishtha, and whether Vasishtha committed a sin in knowing her.
shots.B01C184S01H03: The Gandharva explains that the cursed king devoured a Brahmana while his wife wept, that she cursed him to die when he went to his queen and to have a son by Vasishtha, and that the king, remembering the curse after his queen sent him away, repented and asked Vasishtha for an heir.

B01C185.summary: Arjuna asks the Gandharva which learned Brahmana would make a good priest, and the Gandharva names Dhaumya, who lives in a shrine called Utkochaka. Arjuna hands over his fire weapon, and the Gandharva keeps the horses until they are needed. The Pandavas install Dhaumya as their priest and set out for Drupada's Swayamvara.

scenes.B01C185S01: Arjuna asks the Gandharva for a priest; the Gandharva names Dhaumya, whom the Pandavas install before setting out for the Swayamvara.

shots.B01C185S01H02: Arjuna asks the Gandharva which Brahmana learned in the Vedas would make a worthy priest for them.
shots.B01C185S01H03: The Gandharva names Dhaumya, younger brother of Devala, who performs austerities at the shrine of Utkochaka.
shots.B01C185S01H04: Arjuna gives the Gandharva his fire weapon, leaves the horses with him for later, and the Pandavas install Dhaumya as their priest; they then set out for the Swayamvara, regarding their kingdom and Draupadi as already as good as theirs.

B01C186.summary: The Pandavas set out for Panchala and meet Brahmanas bound for Drupada's Swayamvara, a great contest to win Draupadi. The Brahmanas describe the princess and the many kings expected, and invite the Pandavas to come along. Yudhishthira agrees to go with them.

scenes.B01C186S01: On the road the Pandavas meet Brahmanas bound for Drupada's Swayamvara, who describe Draupadi and invite them along, and Yudhishthira agrees.

shots.B01C186S01H02: The Pandavas set out for Panchala, and on the road they meet Brahmanas bound for Drupada's Swayamvara, who describe the lovely Draupadi, sister of Dhrishtadyumna, and the princes who will compete for her, and invite the brothers to come.
shots.B01C186S01H03: Yudhishthira agrees to go with the Brahmanas to witness the Swayamvara.

B01C187.summary: The Pandavas meet Vyasa on the road and enter Panchala, lodging as mendicant Brahmanas in a potter's house, unknown to anyone. Drupada, who secretly hopes Arjuna will be his son-in-law, has a very stiff bow made and a mark set up above a machine, and proclaims that whoever strings the bow and shoots the mark will win his daughter. Kings, sages and crowds gather in a splendid amphitheatre, and on the sixteenth day Draupadi enters and her brother Dhrishtadyumna announces the contest.

scenes.B01C187S01: The Pandavas enter Panchala unrecognised, Drupada announces the contest with a stiff bow, and the Swayamvara begins before a great crowd of kings.

shots.B01C187S01H02: On the road the Pandavas meet Vyasa, then enter Panchala and take lodging as Brahmanas in a potter's house, where no one recognises them.
shots.B01C187S01H03: Drupada, who secretly wants Arjuna for his daughter, has a very stiff bow made that only Arjuna could bend, and sets up a mark to be shot through a machine in the sky.
shots.B01C187S01H04: Drupada proclaims the Swayamvara, and kings, sages, Duryodhana, Karna and the Kurus arrive, and the splendid amphitheatre with its white mansions is described in detail.
shots.B01C187S01H05: The Pandavas sit among the Brahmanas, and on the sixteenth day Draupadi enters with a golden dish and garland, the sacrificial fire is lit, and Dhrishtadyumna proclaims the contest.

B01C188.summary: Dhrishtadyumna names the many princes who have come to win his sister: Duryodhana and his brothers with Karna, Shakuni, Aswatthaman, a long roll of kings from many lands, and the Yadavas Krishna and Balarama, along with Jarasandha and Shishupala. He says these men will shoot the mark, and that Draupadi should choose whoever succeeds.

scenes.B01C188S01: Dhrishtadyumna names the Kaurava princes, Karna and a long list of kings and Yadavas who have come to compete for Draupadi.

shots.B01C188S01H02: Dhrishtadyumna names Duryodhana and his brothers with Karna, Shakuni, Aswatthaman, a huge roll of kings from Kalinga to Madra, the Vrishnis, Jarasandha and Shishupala, and says that the one who shoots the mark is the one Draupadi should choose.

B01C189.summary: The princes rise in jealous desire for Draupadi, while the gods, sages and Yadavas watch and Krishna points out the Pandavas to Balarama. One by one the princes fail to string the stiff bow, and Karna succeeds in drawing it until Draupadi declares she will not choose a charioteer's son, so he sets the bow down. When Shishupala, Jarasandha and Shalya also fail, Arjuna steps forward to try.

scenes.B01C189S01: The princes try the bow and fail one after another; Karna draws it, but Draupadi rejects him as a charioteer's son, and Arjuna steps forward when the rest give up.

shots.B01C189S01H02: The princes, jealous and lovesick, rise to win Draupadi while the gods, sages and Yadavas watch; Krishna points out the Pandavas to Balarama, and the princes try the bow but cannot string it.
shots.B01C189S01H03: Several kings are thrown down and gasp, their hopes cooled; Karna picks up the bow and strings it, but Draupadi declares she will not choose a Suta, and Karna throws the bow down in vexation.
shots.B01C189S01H04: Shishupala, Jarasandha and Shalya each fall to their knees trying the bow, and when the others have given up, Arjuna rises to string it.

B01C190.summary: When the other kings give up, Arjuna, disguised as a Brahmana, rises amid murmurs from the Brahmanas about a stripling's presumption. He bows to Shiva, strings the bow with ease, and shoots the mark through the machine, to the delight of the gods and the crowd. Krishna greets him with a garland, and Arjuna leaves the hall with Draupadi as his bride.

scenes.B01C190S01: Arjuna, in Brahmana disguise, strings the bow and shoots the mark, and wins Draupadi, to the joy of the gods and the crowd.

shots.B01C190S01H02: Arjuna, a Brahmana to all appearances, rises as Brahmanas murmur about the stripling's boldness, bows to Shiva, strings the bow effortlessly, and shoots the mark through the machine; the gods shower flowers, bards sing, Krishna greets him with a garland, and Arjuna leaves the hall with Draupadi as his bride.

B01C191.summary: The rejected kings, angry that Drupada has given his daughter to a Brahmana, resolve to kill him and his son, since the Swayamvara was meant for Kshatriyas. They rush at Drupada, who takes shelter with the Brahmanas, but Bhima and Arjuna step forward to face them. Krishna names the brothers to Balarama and is glad that they escaped the house of lac.

scenes.B01C191S01: The rejected kings rush at Drupada, Bhima and Arjuna face them, and Krishna identifies the brothers to Balarama.

shots.B01C191S01H02: The rejected kings, angry that Drupada has given his daughter to a Brahmana, resolve to kill him, arguing that the Swayamvara is for Kshatriyas only.
shots.B01C191S01H03: The kings rush at Drupada, who seeks protection from the Brahmanas; Bhima uproots a tree to use as a weapon and stands with Arjuna, and Krishna tells Balarama that the warriors are the Pandavas who escaped the fire of the house of lac, and Balarama is glad that Pritha survived.

B01C192.summary: Arjuna and Bhima stand up to the attacking kings: Arjuna duels Karna to a standstill, and Bhima hurls Shalya aside. Impressed, the kings ask who the Brahmanas are, and Krishna persuades them that the maiden was rightly won, so they withdraw. Meanwhile Kunti, anxious at her sons' delay, fears for their lives until Arjuna walks into the potter's house.

scenes.B01C192S01: Arjuna and Bhima fight off the kings, Arjuna duels Karna and Bhima tosses Shalya; Krishna persuades the kings to withdraw, and Kunti worries at home.

shots.B01C192S01H02: Arjuna tells the Brahmanas to stand aside and watch as he and Bhima charge the kings, and he duels Karna until Karna guesses who he might be, and Arjuna answers that he is a Brahmana skilled in weapons who will defeat him.
shots.B01C192S01H03: Bhima wrestles Shalya and tosses him to the ground without hurting him; the kings, alarmed, ask who these Brahmanas are and call for a halt to the fight.
shots.B01C192S01H04: Krishna tells the kings that the maiden was justly won, and they withdraw, while the Pandavas, wounded and surrounded by Brahmanas, leave the crowd with Krishna.
shots.B01C192S01H05: Kunti, anxious at her sons' delay, imagines that the Kauravas or Rakshasas have killed them, and wonders whether Vyasa has misled them, until Arjuna enters the potter's house with a group of Brahmanas.

B01C193.summary: The brothers present Draupadi to Kunti as their alms, and Kunti, having told them to share everything, is alarmed. Yudhishthira proposes that Arjuna marry her, but Arjuna insists that the eldest should marry first. Seeing that all five desire her, Yudhishthira declares that Draupadi shall be the common wife of all five, and Krishna and Balarama then visit the potter's house.

scenes.B01C193S01: The brothers present Draupadi to Kunti, who is alarmed by her own words, and Yudhishthira resolves that Draupadi shall be the common wife of all five.
scenes.B01C193S02: Krishna and Balarama visit the potter's house, and Krishna greets Yudhishthira and praises the brothers' escape.

shots.B01C193S01H02: The brothers return to their mother and present Draupadi as the alms they got; Kunti, not yet seeing what they have brought, tells them to share it, but when she sees Krishna she cries out in alarm.
shots.B01C193S01H03: Kunti asks Yudhishthira how to keep her word without sin, and Yudhishthira tells Arjuna, who won the maiden, to take her hand in marriage.
shots.B01C193S01H04: Arjuna refuses to be party to sin and says the eldest should marry first, then Bhima, then himself, the twins, and that they all obey Yudhishthira's command.
shots.B01C193S01H05: The brothers look at Draupadi and at one another, all overcome with desire for her; Yudhishthira, fearing division among the brothers, declares that she shall be the common wife of all five.
shots.B01C193S02H01: Krishna and Balarama come to the potter's house, find the five brothers, greet Yudhishthira, praise their escape from the fire, and urge them to return to the tents; then they leave.

B01C194.summary: Dhrishtadyumna secretly follows the Pandavas and hides in the potter's house. That night he overhears the brothers, while Kunti divides the food and they sleep on kusha grass with Draupadi at their feet. In the morning he reports all this to Drupada, who anxiously asks who has won his daughter.

scenes.B01C194S01: Dhrishtadyumna hides in the potter's house and overhears the Pandavas, and in the morning he reports to Drupada, who asks who won his daughter.

shots.B01C194S01H02: Dhrishtadyumna secretly follows the Pandavas and hides in the potter's house; Kunti divides the food, the brothers eat and sleep on kusha grass with Draupadi at their feet, and Dhrishtadyumna listens to their talk.
shots.B01C194S01H03: At dawn Dhrishtadyumna hurries to report everything to Drupada, who is anxious and asks who has taken his daughter, and hopes it was Arjuna who shot the mark.

B01C195.summary: Dhrishtadyumna tells his father Drupada how the archer won Krishna, and how the winners took refuge at a potter's house where their mother was waiting. Drupada sends his priest to ask who the strangers are, and Yudhishthira answers that the bride's price was paid fairly, so Drupada has no cause to grieve. A messenger then announces that the wedding feast is ready. The chapter sets up the revelation that the strangers are the Pandavas.

scenes.B01C195S01: Dhrishtadyumna reports the contest and the night at the potter's house, Drupada's priest asks the strangers who they are, and Yudhishthira answers and the feast is announced.

shots.B01C195S01H02: Dhrishtadyumna reports the contest: the archer hits the mark, the rival kings are beaten, and the winners take Krishna to a potter's house where their mother waits.
shots.B01C195S01H03: Drupada, delighted, sends his priest to ask who the strangers are, adding that he had long hoped Arjuna would wed his daughter.
shots.B01C195S01H04: Yudhishthira has the priest honoured with water and offerings, then argues that the bride was won fairly and Drupada should not grieve.
shots.B01C195S01H05: A messenger hurries in to say the wedding feast is ready.

B01C196.summary: A messenger invites the group to the wedding feast, and they ride in golden-lotus chariots to Drupada's palace. Drupada lays out goods of many kinds to judge their caste, and the guests are seated and fed with honour. Their royal bearing and interest in the weapons convince Drupada and his son that they are of royal blood.

scenes.B01C196S01: The invitation comes, the party rides to the palace, and Drupada's display and the meal show the guests' royal bearing to Drupada and his son.

shots.B01C196S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C196S01H02: A messenger invites the group to the wedding feast and says the chariots are ready.
shots.B01C196S01H03: The party rides to the palace, Kunti goes inside, and the guests are seated and fed; while Drupada gathers goods to test their rank, the guests' interest in the weapons persuades Drupada and his son that they are royal.

B01C197.summary: Drupada asks who the strangers are, and Yudhishthira reveals that they are Kshatriya sons of Pandu who escaped the lac house. Drupada is overjoyed, vows to help restore Yudhishthira to his throne, and asks Arjuna to take Krishna's hand. Yudhishthira then insists that Krishna be the wife of all five brothers, which Drupada resists, and the family is left to decide the matter when Vyasa arrives.

scenes.B01C197S01: Drupada asks who they are, Yudhishthira reveals the Pandavas' identity and their escape from Varanavata, and Drupada promises support and asks Arjuna to take Krishna's hand.
scenes.B01C197S02: Yudhishthira proposes that Krishna be shared by all five brothers, Drupada objects, Yudhishthira defends it by his mother's command, and Vyasa arrives as the matter is being discussed.

shots.B01C197S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C197S01H02: Drupada asks cheerfully whether they are Kshatriyas, Brahmanas or gods in disguise, and asks for the plain truth.
shots.B01C197S01H03: Yudhishthira declares that they are Kshatriyas and sons of Pandu, names his brothers, and says Kunti and the twins are waiting nearby.
shots.B01C197S01H04: Drupada, overjoyed, asks how they escaped Varanavata, hears the account, blames Dhritarashtra, and vows to restore Yudhishthira's throne.
shots.B01C197S01H05: Drupada gives the group a home and asks Arjuna to take his daughter's hand in marriage that day.
shots.B01C197S02H01: Drupada offers to give Krishna to Yudhishthira or any brother, and Yudhishthira replies that she must be the common wife of all five, as their mother ordered.
shots.B01C197S02H02: Drupada objects that a man may have many wives but no woman has had many husbands, and Yudhishthira answers that morality is subtle and his mother's command settles it.
shots.B01C197S02H03: Drupada asks Yudhishthira, Kunti and Dhrishtadyumna to settle the matter among themselves and tell him by morning.
shots.B01C197S02H04: Yudhishthira, Kunti and Dhrishtadyumna begin to discuss it, and then Vyasa arrives on his wanderings.

B01C198.summary: Vyasa arrives and is welcomed by all, then asks each person for their view of one woman marrying several men. Drupada and Dhrishtadyumna object on grounds of custom and the Vedas, while Yudhishthira cites old precedents and his mother's command. Kunti fears her word may be untrue, and Vyasa promises to explain the custom privately to Drupada, which sets up his defence of polyandry.

scenes.B01C198S01: Vyasa asks for the company's views; Drupada and Dhrishtadyumna object, and Yudhishthira defends the match with precedent and his mother's command.
scenes.B01C198S02: Kunti voices her worry about untruth, and Vyasa says he will explain the custom only to Drupada, taking him aside to begin.

shots.B01C198S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C198S01H02: Everyone rises to greet Vyasa, and after Drupada asks how one woman can wed many men without sin, Vyasa calls the practice obsolete and asks each man's view.
shots.B01C198S01H03: Drupada says the custom is sinful, contrary to usage and the Vedas, and that he cannot agree to it.
shots.B01C198S01H04: Dhrishtadyumna objects that an elder brother should not approach a younger brother's wife, and he refuses to say Draupadi should be shared.
shots.B01C198S01H05: Yudhishthira cites old precedents, a woman who married seven sages and a tree-born maiden who married ten brothers, and argues that his mother's command makes the match virtuous.
shots.B01C198S02H01: Kunti agrees with Yudhishthira but fears her own words may prove untrue.
shots.B01C198S02H02: Vyasa says the matter is an old and eternal virtue, that Yudhishthira's view is sound, and that he will explain it only to Drupada in private.
shots.B01C198S02H03: Vyasa takes Drupada into a private room while the others wait, and begins to explain why the custom is not sinful.

B01C199.summary: Vyasa tells Drupada a story to explain who the Pandavas really are. Yama stopped killing during a sacrifice, and after Indra is humbled by Mahadeva for his pride, he and four other Indras are sent to be born as men, with the goddess Sri as their common wife. Vyasa then identifies the brothers as those Indras and Draupadi as Sri, and grants Drupada divine sight to see them in their former forms.

scenes.B01C199S01: Vyasa tells the story of Yama's pause in killing, Indra's humbling by Mahadeva, the curse that sends five Indras into the world of men, and the birth of Krishna and Valadeva.
scenes.B01C199S02: Vyasa names the brothers as the former Indras and Draupadi as Sri, grants Drupada divine sight, and tells the story of a maiden who asked Mahadeva for five husbands.

shots.B01C199S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C199S01H02: Vyasa says that when Yama paused killing during a sacrifice, humans multiplied, and the gods went to Prajapati, who said Yama would resume his work later.
shots.B01C199S01H03: Indra sees golden lotuses floating down the Bhagirathi, follows the stream to its source, and finds a weeping woman washing there.
shots.B01C199S01H04: The woman leads Indra to a peak where Mahadeva is playing dice; Indra's pride is punished, and he and four other Indras are cursed to be born as men.
shots.B01C199S01H05: Indra makes a fifth Indra, the five are named, Sri is given as their common wife, and Narayana sends two hairs that become Valadeva and Krishna, while the brothers are the Indras and Arjuna is part of Sakra.
shots.B01C199S02H01: Vyasa explains that the Pandavas are those Indras and Draupadi is Sri, who must be born in an extraordinary way, and grants Drupada spiritual sight.
shots.B01C199S02H02: With this sight Drupada sees the brothers in celestial form, is amazed, and hears Vyasa tell of a maiden who asked Mahadeva for five husbands.
shots.B01C199S02H03: Vyasa applies the story to Drupada's daughter, who was pre-ordained to be the common wife of five husbands, and tells the king to do as he wishes.

B01C200.summary: Drupada accepts the story, saying fate and Mahadeva's decree have settled the matter, and gives his consent. Vyasa names an auspicious day, and the wedding goes ahead with Dhaumya presiding, Yudhishthira going first and the brothers taking Krishna's hand in turn. Drupada sends the couples off with cars, elephants, servants and wealth, and the Pandavas settle in his capital.

scenes.B01C200S01: Drupada accepts Vyasa's account, Vyasa names the day, and the wedding is held with Dhaumya presiding, followed by Drupada's gifts and the Pandavas' settling in Panchala.

shots.B01C200S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C200S01H02: Drupada says he now accepts what the gods have ordained, since fate, not his own acts, has settled the marriage, and gives his consent.
shots.B01C200S01H03: The wedding is held on Vyasa's auspicious day, with Dhaumya lighting the fire, the brothers taking Krishna's hand in turn, and Drupada giving rich gifts; the text also notes a marvel that Krishna regained her maidenhood each day.

B01C201.summary: Drupada is pleased with the alliance and no longer fears even the gods. Kunti blesses Krishna, comparing her to famous wives of gods and heroes, and asks her to bear strong sons and rule as queen. Hari (Krishna) then sends the Pandavas costly gifts, including ornaments, robes, servants, elephants, horses and gold, which Yudhishthira accepts to please Govinda.

scenes.B01C201S01: Drupada's women greet Kunti, Kunti blesses Krishna, and Hari (Krishna) sends the newly married Pandavas a great store of gifts.

shots.B01C201S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C201S01H02: Drupada's household women greet Kunti, and Kunti blesses Krishna, comparing her to famous wives and asking for sons and a royal future.
shots.B01C201S01H03: Hari (Krishna) sends the brothers ornaments, robes, servants, elephants, horses and gold, and Yudhishthira accepts them gladly to please Govinda.

B01C202.summary: Word reaches the kings that Draupadi has married the Pandavas, that Arjuna won her in disguise, and that the brothers are alive after all. Duhsasana and the others return to Hastinapura dejected, and Dhritarashtra, first thinking his son has won her, then praises the Pandavas and their powerful allies. Vidura leaves, and Duryodhana and Karna urge their father to weaken the Pandavas before they overpower the Kauravas.

scenes.B01C202S01: News of the marriage spreads, the kings blame Bhishma and Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana returns dejected, and Vidura tells Dhritarashtra the Pandavas are alive and allied with Drupada.
scenes.B01C202S02: After Vidura leaves, Duryodhana and Karna press Dhritarashtra to act against the Pandavas in private.

shots.B01C202S01H02: Spies report that Draupadi has married the Pandavas, and the kings, who had thought the brothers dead in the lac house, blame Bhishma and Dhritarashtra.
shots.B01C202S01H03: Duryodhana and his company return dejected, and Duhsasana says Arjuna only won by disguising himself as a Brahmana and that fate rules.
shots.B01C202S01H04: Vidura tells Dhritarashtra that the Pandavas are alive and allied with Drupada, but the blind king first thinks his own son has won Draupadi and orders ornaments made for her.
shots.B01C202S01H05: Dhritarashtra says the Pandavas are as dear to him as they were to Pandu, and that an alliance with Drupada is a fine thing.
shots.B01C202S02H01: Vidura tells the king to keep his good sense for a hundred years and goes home; then Duryodhana and Karna come to Dhritarashtra alone, accuse him of favouring his enemies, and urge him to weaken the Pandavas before they swallow the Kauravas.

B01C203.summary: With Vidura gone, Dhritarashtra asks his son Duryodhana and Karna to speak openly about how to undo the Pandavas. Duryodhana lists a string of schemes: sowing discord among the brothers, buying off Drupada, luring them away from Panchala, turning Krishna against them, and having Bhima killed. He argues that time is short, because once the brothers win Drupada's trust they will be beyond reach.

scenes.B01C203S01: Dhritarashtra asks for his son's plans in private, and Duryodhana sets out a list of ways to ruin the Pandavas, ending by asking Karna's opinion.

shots.B01C203S01H01: Heading: the Viduragamana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C203S01H02: Dhritarashtra says he will keep his plans from Vidura and asks his son and Karna to speak now that Vidura has left.
shots.B01C203S01H03: Duryodhana lists his schemes, including sowing discord, bribing Drupada, luring the brothers to Panchala or Hastinapura, turning Krishna against them, and having Bhima killed, then asks Karna for his view.

B01C204.summary: Karna argues that Duryodhana's subtle plans cannot work, because the Pandavas are now grown, allied with Drupada, and bound together by their shared wife, and Krishna will not abandon them. He advises an open attack on Drupada before Krishna's Yadava forces arrive. Dhritarashtra praises his courage but wants the elders' advice, and he calls his ministers together.

scenes.B01C204S01: Karna rejects Duryodhana's subtle plans and urges open war on Drupada, Dhritarashtra praises him but asks the elders to advise, and the king gathers his ministers.

shots.B01C204S01H01: Heading: the Viduragamana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C204S01H02: Karna rejects the subtle plans, argues that the brothers cannot be divided or turned against Krishna, and urges an open attack on Drupada before Krishna's forces gather.
shots.B01C204S01H03: Dhritarashtra praises Karna's courage but asks Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and the others to advise on a course that benefits all.
shots.B01C204S01H04: Dhritarashtra calls his chief ministers together to take counsel.
